Years ago Dominique's New England clam Chowder was by far the best canned chowder available, He apparently sold the rights to his trade name and did not have any further control over the recipe. Over time, the manufacturer made several unfortunate changes to the recipe, apparently not realizing that to try to compete on price was futile. Soup sold through regular (non-gourmet) channels and priced a few cents higher than Campbell's won't sell. A truly premium product priced 50% higher might succeed. What we have today is a chowder in the identical can it has always used. The can looks the same, but the soup inside is now no better than several chowders available in grocery stores. It is a non-premium product trading on a destroyed reputation. It may be a blessing that it is now hard to find. To complete the tragedy, Campbell's probably makes the beset chowder available today, though it is not very good.

column10: I buy the Kraft Parmesan Grated cheese every month. I love the taste and put in on a lot of foods. These flowering teas are a wonder to behold and fun to watch.  The tea ball, right out of the package, looks like a funny colored nut with the scent of tea and jasemin.  Place it in the bottom of a tea cup or tea pot (the best show happens in an all glass one), and add hot, but not boiling water, sit back and watch.  It's amazing to see it open up into a beautiful bouquet.  The green leaves are the tea (green scented with jasmin) and the flower are one a 12 different selections. column9: Assorted Green Tea Flowers but Same Flavor
column10: We got this for my mom and she really likes it.  While the tea flowers vary in presentation, they are all "Green Tea with Fresh Jasmine."  It would have been nice to mix up the flavor of the tea.  I would recommend this more for presentation than flavor.

Assorted Green Tea Flowers should be called Assorted Jasmine Green Tea Flowers.  It's the blooms that are assorted not the tea flavor.  They are all Jasmine.  Having said that, it's a wonderful surprise when you put in the bud and don't know what kind of flower you're going to be getting next!Usually when I buy Jasmine Tea I get the finest- A small 4 ounce bag that runs me  $20 and although this tea isn't as good as what I regularly buy it's still very nice tasting.  The best part is that it's practically impossible to overbrew.  Jasmine Tea in particular can get really bitter easily if it is overbrewed even a bit and I was afraid I would have to take the flower out after a couple of minutes to stop the brewing process.  But NO!  The makers thought ahead and made it so that you can leave the flower in and it won't overbrew.  The only bad thing about this is that if you like your Jasmine Tea really strong then you won't like the way this works for you.  But strong Jasmine Tea is always bitter so you might want to try a lighter brew like this.Hint: If you never liked the way Jasmine Tea tasted because of it's bitterness here's a trick.  Standard instructions for Jasmine include having your water at around 180 degrees and brewing for aprox 2 minutes.  Instead of this, try using a lower temperature instead- say 130ish and brew for 7 minutes.  What you'll get is a tea with all the Jasmine and none of the bitterness.  With these flowers however you don't have to worry about brewing time (unless you like your tea VERY weak) and are free to enjoy the flower until your tea is gone.

This product was a huge disappointment. I bought this planning to serve it at a Witches Tea party. It's a good thing I did a "rehearsal brew" first, because this was an absolute dud. The product is packaged attractively, but with no instructions. However, I'd read enough about presentation teas to know the procedure, which I followed carefully. Using my brand new, purchased-just-for-this borosilicate glass teapot, I chose a tea ball and placed it in the empty pot, then gently poured in very hot - but not boiling - water. The tea ball immediately floated and bobbed around as it slowly unfurled into a mass resembling a clump of seaweed. Eventually a whitish mess became visible in the middle, not in any way resembling the gorgeous yellow blossom pictured on the tea packet. Although disappointed, I thought the "flower" looked pretty creepy and just might work, since it was a Witches Tea after all. When the correct steeping time was reached, I poured a small cup of the heavenly fragranced tea to sample it. UGH. So bitter and vile, even witches wouldn't want it! I tried adding some honey, but still couldn't drink it. Really nasty stuff!I'm going to try another variety, just in case that one ball was defective. If I get better results, I'll post an update. But as of now, Primula Flowering Tea gets two thumbs down from me.

column9: Possibly the best small dog food

Like most little dogs with allergies, I've noticed the eye discharge is minimal compared to other foods.So for any super-finicky small dog parent, I would definitely recommend this kibble.

column9: My picky dogs eats every piece!
column10: I have a three year old yorkipoo who has always been extremely picky about his food.  We had some success (by "some success" I mean he'd eat half of what he was supposed to) with the Prarie brand by Natures Variety, but he always had runny eye problems and had trouble keeping weight on.  My mother's vet recommended the Wellness brand for her dog to lose weight and suggested I try the small breed formula for my picky dog. I'm so glad I tried it! Since switching my dog to the Wellness small breed formula my dog eats every single piece.  I don't have to sit there and encourage him to eat. He willingly eats the whole bowl and cannot wait for his next meal. I'm convinced that I could feed him 5 times a day and he'd still eat every last piece because its just that good. I have never seen him so excited to eat! On top of this his coat is as soft as ever and his watery, running, cloudy eyes are completely clear. He has the same amount of small dog energy but doesn't seem as anxious when I leave (apparently filler in dog foods can cause anxiety in sensitive dogs).  I'm amazed at how great this product is working for my little man. Highly recommend for those with picky, small breed dogs.

column9: Hands down one of the best foods on the market today
column10: I have two Basenjis both of who are under breed weight/size and who have corn allergies. I cannot stress enough how awesome this food has been for them. Their appetites are up, they are putting on weight, they have more energy where their other food (which was also on the Top Ten Dog Foods List) made them sluggish and caused one to lick a hole in herself. I could go on and on about the differences but honestly, buy a bag and try it. There is nothing I can say that you won't see for yourself.

column9: One of the best dog food you can buy for the price
column10: Ok let me clarify first of all, why I gave it 4/5 instead of 5/5.If it were to up to me alone, this food is 5/5.The ONLY reason why I took 1 star off, is because my dogs hate the taste :(I have a Pomeranian and a Maltese. column9: Caviar That Not Really Worth It
column10: I recently found this caviar product here on Amazon and was tempted to try it given the fact that the shipping was free with Amazon Prime. Some time ago I bought Black Capelin Caviar 12oz here on Amazon, but the $18.00 or so for the shipping nearly doubled it's cost, so free shipping with this Marky's caviar was very tempting for me, so I placed the order. The shipping was fairly fast 4 days, and when I opened the box I found 4 jars, each packed into a clear bubble wrap and then wrapped into a sealed green plastic pouch. Upon the opening the bubble wrap from all 4 jars, I unintentional touched the lid of one of the jars and heard a distinct "pop", which meant that the lid was not hermetically screwed to the jar. I immediately notified Amazon about this and when I woke up on the next day, a refund of $6.00 was issued to me. Each full and sealed jar weights 202 grams and an empty one (jar and lid) weights 105 grams, which means that you get 97 grams of caviar per jar. All the caviar roes are very uniform and glossy. When I tried a teaspoon of this caviar I immediately noticed how artificially salty it was outside, probably due to added preservatives, stabilizer and spice. I also noticed that the small roes were somewhat hard but made distinct "pops" when you bit on them, and the internal flavor was bland to nonexistent. Later when I spread the caviar on a slice of bread, the whole caviar mass was difficult to spread around and the roes stuck to each other very firmly. In the end I concluded that this caviar is mediocre and most (if not all) of the flavor comes from the added ingredients. I did not feel like a sultan while eating this caviar, but rather than like an easy mark who fell for the low price and free shipping.The ingredients of this Lumpfish Black Caviar are the following:- Lumpfish roes- Salt- Water- Stabilizer (Xanthan Gum)- Spices- Citric Acid- Sodium Benzoate- Blue #1 Food Coloring- Yellow #6 Food Coloring- Red #40 Food ColoringI would not buy this caviar ever again, even with free shipping. The Black Capelin Caviar 12oz was distinctly better than this mediocre caviar. And like with the Black Capelin Caviar 12oz, you also get green poop if you eat 3/4 of the 3.5oz jar.
First of all it's too salty,taste is good but today I went to the bathroom my poop came out all green,I don't know why,that scared me a little.

column10: I loved the General Foods International Chai Latte (sugar free).  But since it has been discontinued, I haven't really found anything I really like.  Now Maxwell House has produced the Coffee Chai Latte (not sugar free).  It is OK, but I miss the GF chai (sugar free).  I am hoping that Maxwell House will come out with the Chai Coffee (or Tea) Latte in sugar free and then I will try it again.  I am also disappointed in the other Maxwell House line of coffees.  They are very weak in flavor.  I have tried the David Rio Orca Spice Chai Tea (sugar free) and it is OK a little sweet for me, but better than nothing.

The ingredients for chai tea latte should be tea, honey, spices. Not corn solids, hydrogynated oils, etc. like in this "tea" latte product. Instant tea is one of the last ingredients listed. Something is wrong.  This product is not good.
I love this tea and have had a hard time finding it in the stores. I was very excited to find it online. If you havent tried it yet you should.

I love this product. It is very hard to get.  I got an email saying it was no longer available.  But I hope that is not true.  It's good anytime.  I add CoffeMate liquid creamer to mine and it makes it more delicious. You can make it with water or milk, have it hot or cold. yum yum!!!  I have an automatic order every six months. And I reorder myself in between.

column9: A little bit changed with Maxwell House in charge, but still good!
column10: This item used to be available as "General Foods International" and has since switched over to Maxwell House.  It also used to be availabls to me in my area; it has been off the shelves for months now and I was very happy to find a supply on Amazon under the new ownweship.  I have tried other chai mixes, powdered and liquid but this is hands down the best and easiest one to make.  Make it with milk to get the best flavor.  Now if only Amazon would make it a subscription like they used to have it when it was with General Foods!

It is quite difficult to order the Caribou Coffee Daybreak Morning Blend  from area coffee suppliers.  I have searched other online coffee suppliers too and Amazon is the only place to obtain our desired morning K-Cup coffee.  We had ordered 24 K-Cups in a box, but the Caribou goes cery quickly and we all were delighted that we could order a quantity of 80.  We buy two boxes of 80 K-Cups.  Amazon is also the only convenient site that I can order my boss her Earl Gray DeCaf K-Cups.  I order a variety of coffee of K-Cups.  It is easy to use the site and the delivery is faster than area coffee suppliers.  Excellent Caribou Coffee Daybreak Morning Blend.  Extremely satisfied customers in the office.China Blue Eyes

column9: Very sweet version of hazelnut flavored coffee
column10: This is a lighter roast, hazelnut flavored coffee, one that is probably the most favorite of the flavored coffees along with French Vanilla.For me, I found it was too sweet--not that there is sugar in it, there isn't; I drank it black, but it's a very light, fragrant blend and the sense I got is of sweetness. If you don't like bitterness in your coffee and like a strong hazelnut fragrance, you are going to love this. I like my coffee a bit stronger so even on "strong" this wasn't dark enough for me. But it is a very intense, sweet scent and there is no doubt that there is HAZELNUT in your cup.Coffee such as this makes a very nice iced cappuccino. My late husband (who worked as a barista when I met him, that was a match made in heaven!) had a secret recipe for an iced coffee drink that was sweetened with maple syrup.  It was a best-seller at the shop where he worked and people would stand with their tongues hanging out, waiting for the next batch to be ready when it ran out. I still don't have ALL the formula, which sadly he took to the grave, but I know a few of the ingredients  You can make a variant of it with Gloria's Hazelnut, by brewing this over ice and mixing with half and half or evaporated milk and adding a touch of maple syrup. Serve on crushed ice. It's usually a big hit with people. The maple and hazelnut are very compatible. His flavored coffee used a different flavor (I think....) but this works really well, too.

This is an excellent brand rice. We keep 4:1 (water:rice) ratio in a pressure cooker, and rice comes out fluffy. Very tasty and never had problems with it. It is wrapped in a plastic slim cover and covered with the nice cloth cover. Had used for over 2 years and never disappointed.

column9: ABSOLUTELY the WORLD's BEST TASTING RAW HONEY - FROM AMAZON
column10: This Propolis enriched Raw Honey purchased from AMAZON, which is the only place I have every seen it for sale, is unheated, unprocessed and unfiltered so that all its attributes are fully preserved. Propolis enriched Honey consists of pure raw honey (39-oz) enriched with all natural Proolis (30,000 mg). Propolis gives raw honey distinctively appealing taste.I have been buying raw honey from all over the world for many many years looking for just the 'right one'.  I have had different raw honey's from all the continents except Antartica, and from most countries where raw honey is sold.  That includes Iceland, Ireland, Scotland, England, Europe, Eastern Europe, Africa, China, Near-Middle and Far East including Japan and so on.  The most unusual tasting honey came from some rare trees found only in New Zealand.  OK but takes getting used to.  Be warned it is really costly and the amount you get is small.The best: RAW HONEY ENRICHED WITH PROPOLIS.  Best in all categories:  Best tasting, not overly sweet; best unique palate friendly taste; best texture; best color - not the see through stuff but a light tan thick creamy appearance with the propolis mixed through; best cost for 40 oz.  Use it for cooking, sweetner, as a pick-me-up  and by the way it is NOT overly oppressively sweet, but modestly sweet with a friendly flavor.  Wonderful in all respects and way worth the money.My second favorate is simply called RAW HONEY.  These honey's also have medicinal qualities.  Got a burn or cut, spread some on.  Applies to animals too (if they can't reach it with their tongue), or you can cover it.  The  country Vet was right and saved us a bundle.I continue to look for new types from small producers from all over the world but in 20 some years of searching RAW Honey Enriched With Propolis is the best tasting, the best for cooking, eating and best for the amount and cost.  I have sent jars to my four sisters, parents, friends, and others as birthday and Christmas gifts.  They all say pretty much the same as above.Daniel H. NielsenSaipan (Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands).

column4: Heather L. Parisi "Robert and Heather Parisi"
column9: VERY FRESH PEANUTS THOUGH AN EXPENSIVE WAY TO BUY THEM
column10: IN A NUTSHELL: EACH PACKAGE CONTAINED 2 OZ. OF FRESH PEANUTS OR CASHEWSThese 2 oz. packages are filled with fresh nuts with nothing but salt added [& peanut oil or cottonseed oil]. As snack foods go, this is a very healthy choice. Although expensive on an ounce for ounce basis, as portions of snack foods go, this is still a fair value and a relatively healthy choice. Bear in mind that about 75% of the 170 calories per ounce are from fat, but there are NO TRANS-FATTY ACIDS or CHOLESTEROL while there are some healthy mono-saturated oils.My big complaint against many other snack-nut products is their lack of freshness, and in fact a rancid taste to the nuts which NEVER happened with these Planters nuts. In fact, each individual package has an expiration date clearly marked on the front of the package.BOTTOM LINE: I PREFER THE LARGER JAR BECAUSE I EAT MORE THAN 2 OZ. AT A TIMEMy preference is to get these peanuts and cashews in the larger jar and unsalted, but for the summer, the salt is okay and the freshness was consistent in every package.For product info, Kraft has a website [plantersdotcom][I AM NOT AFFILIATED WITH ANY PRODUCT OR COMPANY]

column9: Costly and product varies in taste
column10: This looked like a great way to buy a variety pack of nuts, in snack sizes that would keep me from eating too many. The problem is that peanuts are sort of the "junk" nut if you're trying to eat healthy. (stick to almonds and walnuts)Plus buying individual packs is more expensive. But the worse offense- several packages were rancid! It seemed to be the plain salted peanuts mostly. The honey nuts had a slightly off taste, but not as bad as the salted peanuts. The cashews were OK, but not as good as cashews I've had from regular cans of Planters. I think what might happen is that shipping in the summer in the Southern states causes a lot of degradation in the flavor in the packages.Don't waste your money on this, because you just don't know what you're going to get.

Nothing wrong with product as Planters nuts are always a favorite. But the box arrived with one flap pulled up and after counting the packages inside I discovered that it was one short of the salted peanuts (should be 12). Because of the limitations of contacting Amazon about problems - you must repackage item and return everything - I am keeping the item because it is part of a care package for my Marine nephew in Afghanistan. I am just so disappointed that someone was so hungry they had to steal from my shipment and I wish there was a direct contact with Amazon where you could share this kind of incident instead having to return everything for replacement or credit.

column9: BEWARE - Sizes have decreased - no longer 2 oz packs
column10: I have ordered and reordered this item several times.  The last shipment I received (two boxes) the package sizes had decreased from 2 oz to 1.75 for the peanuts and 1.5 for the cashews.I realize this is from Planters and it's a sign of the times but the product description needs to be updated.We like these at work but just like Granola bars, the price stays the same (or goes up) and the product size goes down.The product itself is fine but I am sick of getting ripped off by changes in product portions. Planters-Nuts On the Go Snack Packs, 24/2 oz Variety Packs
The seller was very good at responding to email inquiries, shipping method chosen was honored, product received on time & undamaged.
i loved these peanuts they were just so good all of them and they came just as advertised.

column9: Convenient to have when on the go
column10: This package of variety nuts is very convenient to have when on the go and for my son's lunch box, he likes these but the price on Amazon is too high for mostly peanuts. It is a much better price at Sam's Club for the exact same thing. I love buying on amazon (sort of an Amazon addict)because of the convenience and great prices but you do have to keep in mind Sam's Club is very competitive price wise it's just a pain in the neck going there (when spoiled by Amazon) plus always end up spending more and having to bring it all home. Love the free home delivery Amazon offers so if you want to pay more for the convenience then you should buy these on Amazon.
You can get the exact same box of Planters Nuts from Sams Club for $11.72!!!!!  They are tasty with a good mix of different nuts.  If only Amazon can watch those prices.
The nuts tasted old. It is supposed to be a variety pack but 80 percent of the items were salted peanuts. Not buying this product again.
excellent selection of nuts in a nice package size (2oz). very handy to take along for a snack between meals.very tasty.

these are excellent for snacks through out the day ... the packs are pretty big so I split the tube in half so I can keep the calories a little lower. A 100 calorie version would be perfect but I can split it up just fine that's what baggies are for. :)

Just finished off a bag of Cashews. These are nothing like the tiny bags of salted nuts we purchased as children, these are LARGE 2 ounce bags! You get twice (12) the number of regular salted peanuts compared to the Cashews and Honey Roasted but that's ok, as I like them all.Very pleased.
This "deal" is a rip off when you can get 2/$1 at the store. And you get to pick which types of Planters you want.
I must admit that this is a bad temptation but I have always really like the flavor of planters peanuts.These come at a fair price and it is an easy way to stock up where you will not go broke.

column9: Only thing better is fresh roasted on the boardwalk
column10: This item is one of my periodic Sam's Club purchases. There's never been a bad pack in the bunch--something I can't say for all the convenience-store & vending machine competitors I've tried, such as Lance. The only thing consistently better than Planters packaged nuts is if you can get them still warm from the roaster (and that always makes me think of Planters, too, because of the shop near 8th Street on the boardwalk in Ocean City).
I love Platters and this was a great purchase. I found out that my son loves the Honey Roasted, Me not at all.

I started out the year with a vow to watch my diet and take better care of myself.  These small bags of nuts help me do that.  A good snack for a packed lunch or just something to keep in your desk at work, to help you fend of the less-healthy stuff in the company vending machine or break room.Nice variety to change things up.  Yes, a little more expensive than buying in bulk, but the packaging helps with portion control.  Without the small packaging, I'd be snacking on these things all day!
I mailed this to my husband when he was deployed to Afghanistan. Great product...and FREE shipping!!!
These arrived fresh. Come in individual packs just right for a snack without too many calories. Arrived in about a week after ordering.

Tasty treat.  Great from the fridge or even the freezer.  I'm not big on marshmallow treats, but this suits my sweet tooth and one will satisfy my craving for days.  One box every 6 months is perfect.  Great transaction, good treat and not overly horrible for you if eaten in moderation.  Highly recommended.

column9: Big fan of barilla pasta, not so much their sauce though
column10: I love barilla's 51% wheat pasta so i decided to try their marinara sauce. I found it is nothing special. its about average, and the twist with this one is it has carrots in it. having never tried tomato sauce with a hint of carrot taste to it, this one is definately unique. it's still average, but if you like carrot juice, give it a shot. it is still one of the better "average" sauces out there, id probably place it somewhere near the top as far as the two dollar sauces go. unfortunately it's not something i would continuously buy, and i couldve literally pulled any other sauce off the shelves. besides the carrot gimmmick, theres nothing terribly unique about this one. with that said i am still a big fan of barilla pasta, and that, they do amazing. so find another sauce, and put it on barilla's pasta and you're good to go :)

I bought this because my friend told me about it. I'm currently on HerbaLife (diet) and replace 2 meals with shakes. The PB2 is perfect because I can control how much is going in without the sticky mess of traditional peanut butter & can figure calories, protein, fat, etc. alot more easier! PB2 also lasts a long time but I will def order again as soon as I start running low. Awesome idea!! Also, the recipe cards are wonderful too.

I bought this stuff with really low expectations, but I had been desperately searching for a new peanut butter substitute for a long time, and I was desperate. The first time I tried PB2, I knew I was hooked. I can't go a day without eating something I made with PB2. I would recommend trying it at least once. It's not for everyone, but you won't know if it's something you'll like until you try it! I prefer the original to the cocoa version for most purposes, but the cocoa version has its uses as well.
This stuff is awesome! makes any milkshake or smoothie taste like peanut butter for 1/3 of the calories. I got a great deal on the price too

column9: Great substitute for peanut butter...but much less fat
column10: I have been using this product and the chocolate version for over a year now.  I find it wonderful in protein smoothies I eat each morning, for weight control/management. The texture is great, and taste is exactly what you'd expect. I understand it is literally ground up peanuts, just no oils added, as they would do for spreadable peanut butter. In addition, the lower calories (and fat) make this a useable "diet" enhancement food item. I highly recommend it. Great for any non-dieter too.

column9: Excellent substitute for the real thing
column10: My wife and I are on Weight Watchers and this helps keep our points down!  With only 1 point plus per serving versus 4 for regular peanut butter, excellent midnight snack.

As someone who LOVES peanut butter - I was skeptical about a powder.  So far, I have used it in baked goods and also my protein shakes - both with great results.  My reason for 4 stars - when mixing with water to make peanut butter to use plain, however, will take some practice.  You have to play with the ratio to get your perfect consistency - but overall I am going to recommend this product to all peanut lovers!!It has a very nice nutty flavor.  Best for adding to recipes to add that peanut flavor without the calories!
this has a nice pea nutty flavor  but lacks the punch and fat, of course, of the real thing  pb sandwiches are a bummer with this product

I was talked into these by some dieting pals online.  I like the taste, but find that this is something totally unnecessary in my life and I won't be buying again.  If you like this stuff, definitely get it via Amazon.

PB2 more than met my expectations. It has a delicious flavor and is very versatile. I am addicted to peanut butter and was eating brands with less than appealing ingredients, calories and fat. Having only 45 calories per 2 tablespoons was what attracted me to PB2, but now I love the flavor and health benefits.

column9: All the peanut taste with less calories and fat!
column10: I'd been hearing several Beachbody coaches talk about using this product in the chocolate Shakeology.  I was grinding peanuts for homemade peanut butter to add to mine, but liked the idea of something more shelf stable and lower in calories.  Both the PB2 PB and PB2 Cocoa PB are awesome!  I suspect my backpack camping family will be utilizing this as it is lighter weight for carrying on those back country trip.s
I love PB2!  Post RNY surgery this is my new favorite food.  Good amount of protein and fiber for the calorie count and oh so decadent.  I don't miss real peanut butter at all. :)

I originally ordered these two flavors of peanut butter due to a recommendation from an email that I receive several times a week.  I really like the chocolate flavor because it is really creamy when you mix it with the water and not overly sweet.  It is very satisfying and I don't even use jelly with it.  The peanut butter flavored one was just OK which is why I only gave it four stars.  The chocolate one would have gotten five stars and I have already reordered it two more times.

Wow, this is great stuff.  Works perfectly for my smoothies!  I haven't tried any of the recipes, but these are just what I was looking for to easily add pb to my smoothies and shakes.  Both taste great!

I actually go this from a diet clinic, but keep buying it because it makes great flavors in cookies and whip cream.  You have to mix well, but it is makes a so-so dessert that much tastier and you don't have all the extra fat.  Love this stuff.

Great idea; don't know why someone didn't come up with this sooner! All the taste and protein of regular peanut butter with a third of the calories. I mix it with milk and cereal, protein powder, and jelly so far. Have more ideas to still try!
I use this for smoothies. It's a great way to add protein. I haven't had a chance to try it for many other things. It was good on a sandwich though. It's delicious!!
Yum! Very good stuff. I especially like to use it in smoothies.Thanks for the recipe cards, very good ideas!

This product is AMAZING! I love it in my Protein smoothies! It blends amazing, It taste so great & the best part is how much less fat & calories it has. It works for so many other things in cooking also. My Favorite and main use is for all my protein shakes. It also adds protein with every serving. I will be a life long fan for sure!

column9: Not Peanut Butter, Peanut Flavored Peanut Butter
column10: I ordered this at the asking of my wife because she is dieting. I was against it from the start, but I will make my review fair.The product is not peanut butter, if you expect peanut butter than you will be disappointed. It tastes like peanut butter. If I could compare it to something it is like eating a regular Oreo and a reduced fat Oreo. The reduced Oreo tastes like and Oreo, but really just leaves you wanting the real thing. This product is no different. If you mask it will jelly and bread, the off taste becomes less noticeable, but there in lies the problem. You have to add more calories back in to make this product taste better. There by negating the fact that you have cut calories. As I explained to my wife after we both decided this product was not for us. The problem with any peanut butter food is normally everything but the peanut butter. The fat is the healthiest part. You wouldn't eat omega free fish because it's lower in fat, why would you do the same to peanut butter?The only way I could recommend this is if you are doing a starvation sort of diet (i.e. you eating this with celery and water). If you are doing a healthy diet don't cut out the peanut butter of your PB&J, cut out the jelly first and then the grain. I eat again "regular" non-hydrogenated peanut butter will celery, now there is a healthy food.Pros+lower calorie+great price here on amazon+does taste similar to peanut butterCons-less nutritional value-doesn't taste like real peanut butterI will give it four stars if you are doing a starvation sort of diet, which I don't recommend, but it does taste alright for a lot less calories. For everyone else I give it one star as you should not be eating products like this and the product itself is not that good. Overall 2 stars, weighted towards everyone else.

column9: Deliscious and delivered to my door
column10: A lot of tuna at a great price. Exactly what I was looking for. Haven't noticed any taste difference over regular cans Vs Lower Sodium. If you like canned tuna and know how to make it, this is for you. If you are only used to tuna in bags, then you need to know how to drain the cans.It's really easy. Use your can opener, cut the entire top but don't remove it. Take the can over to your sink. Use the freshly cut top to squeeze out the water down your drain. Squeeze slowly until no more water comes out. Now you are ready.I am describing this only because other reviews of cans on Amazon have labeled them as "tuna soup". reviews written by people who haven't used tuna in cans before, and haven't known that you need to drain them.

column9: Good old chicken of the sea canned tuna fish in water
column10: What can I say-same as you get anywhere else except a little cheaper, fast delivery and a long expiration date. Will buy again

My roommate and I received a package of this tuna from an anonymous donor.  It has been a giant blessing in our lives! The texture is just right.  Creamy, almost.  It's just like eating tuna flavored mayonnaise! You hardly need to mix any sauces in it at all!To whoever sent this to us:  thank you!  We are greatly enjoying your gift as we have already, in only 2 days, gone through half of the case!We love this tuna and hope that our anonymous friend decides to give us such a lovely gift again!

I ordered this by mistake to begin with.  Then I was punished every time I opened a can to eat.  It is impossible to squeeze the water out of the can as the tuna mush just pushes out and over the lid.  When you add mayonnaise to it, you cannot have a tuna sandwich as you have to eat it with a spoon, it is so soggy.  I guess I will give it to our feral cats to eat and buy some albacore even though it is twice the price.

We have tuna salad sandwiches at least once a week.  The tuna is small so it has plenty of surface area to absorb the flavor from the sauces.  Probably wouldn't be as good for a casserole where you'd like large pieces.  We appreciate the lower sodium because it's unavailable in our town.

column9: It really is Chicken of the Sea
column10: Sad to say, I buy this canned tuna on standing order for my elderly dogs that have allergies and I eat it myself occassionally.  It is of much better quality than the supermarket brands, very consistent, it really does look like chicken, and does not have a strong odor like other canned tuna.  I especially like the lower sodium, better for me and the dogs.

Still a very good product but the 5 oz is only good for 1 good sandwich.Think the pricing is a bit stiff but the free shipping saves me fromgoing to the store so basically I'm satisfied but would rather be thrilled!

My tuna cans arrived in perfect condition, no dented cans or damaged in anyway. These tuna cans are nice and tastey and really convenient for those who are real busy or lazy to cook. I am trying to lose fat and build muscle and these are a great source of protein and low-fat nutrition. I can very comfortably recommend these for anyone.

column9: What can I say about tuna?
column10: Having all these cans delivered so quickly to my door is a plus, and Chicken of the Sea is a great brand to buy. The taste is clean and fresh, and it's great plain with just a splash of lemon. Of course, it makes a super traditional tuna salad sandwhich. For us, the best use is in wraps with low-fat cheese and sprouts.Fabulous stuff!

column4: these pretzels r making me thirsty
column9: They've improved the lids on the batch I just received!
column10: I was among those who were trying to drain the tuna out with the previous lids and most of the tuna/mush would escape out of the side when trying to drain the liquid (I like to give it to my cats as a treat and in addition to their water).  Well this batch I just got I had no problem draining the liquid!  It was a nice tough lid like in the old days of canned tuna.  Made draining so easy!  The tuna was nice and chunky inside.  Very solid, not mushy at all and I really couldn't tell that it was low sodium by the taste.  Tastes great!  I hope they will continue to use these lids!  Thanks Chicken of the Sea!
This does not have any chunks at all! It's like mush. I'm giving my case to my friend to see if her daughters cat will eat it, but I doubt it.
This tuna has multiple colors, scales and isn't really in "water". I would not recommend subscribing to this item b/c you WILL be disappointed in its taste and context.
Drain out the water and you have a great product.  I like a little cheese in a soft taco shell with this tuna, just roll it up for a fast lunch.

The advertising says tuna in water.  Their web site won't tell you what is in the can!  However if you read the label you see that it is NOT tuna in water, but tuna in water which has been adulterated with genetically modified soy.  This is not good for your health.  It disturbs me when people buy food that they think is healthy but is loaded with genetically modified soy or corn ingredients.  There is no reason to do this!Buy a better brand which is honestly tuna in water only!  Try Natural Sea or Crown Prince brand and see the difference for yourself. There are also other brands that are healthy. You will also find that the tuna is higher quality in those brands - not just watery flakes.

column9: Good Enough to Fool the Goombah!
column10: If you are going to eat this pasta naked you will see, feel and taste a difference from wheat pasta.  But who does that anyway?  It's the sauce that makes the pasta, and this brand of rice pasta is terrific.  Unable to eat wheat, I brought this pasta with me on a visit to my sister's house, and her husband Paulie "the Goombah" refused to eat it.  At least, he thought he did.  He ate it, just didn't know it.  But here is one warning about this product:  if you are going to have it in a macaroni salad or similar, you should plan for hardly any leftovers.  It does not keep well in the fridge, becoming hardish and crunchy-ish and unappetizing.  I don't think it is the cold that makes it that way, because I store leftovers with marinara in the cold and it does not react the same way.  Maybe it is the salt in the salad dressing, or some other ingredient that reacts badly with the pasta.  But other than that this is a Godsend to folks who can't have regular pasta.

Tinkyada Brown Rice gluten free products are simply some of the best imitations of wheat noodles. Our one child has gluten sensitivities so we're switched to some alternatives. Tinkyada is one of the best finds. The noodles cook over a reasonable length of time (around 15-17 minutes) and have a firm texture and a taste that is quite indistinguishable from regular noodles. We've enjoyed the noodles with spaghetti, macaroni and cheese, and casseroles. For texture and taste these cannot be beat for those needing something gluten free due to Celiac disease or other reasons. Everyone in the family is willing to eat these noodles. There is a slight taste difference when tried side by side with regular noodles but not pronounced at all unlike the yucky after taste of noodles made from bean flour.  We would highly recommend these to others and have given packages away as gifts to friends with gluten issues.

We LOVE Tinkyada pasta!  My son is allergic to wheat and egg and this was recommended to us as the best wheat free pasta.  They weren't kidding!  Both my son and I eat it and love it.  It's not mushy and has a great taste.  Even my 4 year old without any food allergies likes it!

I have tried quite a few GF pastas, but this one is most versatile. It remains firm, and can take just a minute or so longer to cook this that wheat pasta. I have noticed that it seems to soak up more juices in my mac and cheese recipe, so I have to put it a little to avoid it from drying out.

Not only does this pasta not get mushy when cooked a minute or three too long, but it holds up! I make baked mac and cheese that requires lots of stirring and most gf pastas break up and fall to pieces, but this pasta holds up to all the harassment. I really enjoy all the Tinkyada pastas, but this is the one I buy the most of!Must have for any GF/CF kitchen!
Good taste and easy to cook. I add noodles to boiling water, cover and turn off heat. Ready in about 15 minutes.

I have found all Tinkyada pasta products to be good tasting and easy to fix.  You should use the energy saving method of cooking and reduce the set time to around 15 minutes, however.  This pasta can become mushy if overcooked or left in liquid for a long period so we always cook it al dente and it is wonderful.  After dealing with a gluten free diet for several years, I have to say this is one of our favorite gf lines of food.  I am excited to see that Amazon Grocery is now carrying this line of pasta.

column9: So yummy Gluten-Free pasta, better than traditional pasta!
column10: The ingredients are: brown rice, rice bran, water.Excellent texture (basically the same as traditional noodles, just a tad thicker)Excellent flavor, perhaps a bit richer/deeper/nuttier than traditional noodles (like the difference between white rice and brown rice)Cooking time just a couple minutes longer than traditional noodlesMy sister and I need to eat gluten-free, so we gave these noodles a shot with my mom's homemade mac and cheese recipe that we've always eaten growing up (Velveeta, milk, butter). These noodles actually made it taste BETTER than traditional noodles!  My mom's sauce is pretty runny, which is how we've always eaten it, and for some reason, these noodles either soaked it up more, or caused it to thicken more. It created a nice, thick dish with a richer flavor than white noodles. We let some of the family taste it, and they all liked it better!  Too bad they are so expensive, so we will only use them for the GF eaters in the family.I can't wait to try the rest of the Tinkyada pastas for spaghetti, pasta salad, and fettuccini. Who says you can't have pasta when you are gluten-free?! Not me! Soooo good.

This pasta is great for people with Celiac.  I think the taste is great and when you miss your pasta, this is a great subsitute.  It does take longer to cook and is better when rinsed in hot water before serving.  Does not go mushy like other brands.

This is so great tasting. I used it to make macaroni salad and mac and cheese and both came out great. It does soak up liquid more so use extra. When I made the macaroni salad I had to add more mayonnaise twice while it was chilling. Leftover mac and cheese after a few hours was a little dry, but still tasted good. My non gf husband said it was the best mac and cheese he's had, and he also enjoyed the macaroni salad. He never likes whole wheat items so for him to like this says something about it. column9: Amazing suprise awaits the opening of this package!!!
column10: For those of us used to Tuna in the can this product seems very unique and certainly economical if you have several people in your family.What you are getting is a single solid slab of tuna measuring approx. 6 inches wide 9 inches long and 1 inch thick. 2 whole pounds of Wild Planet's low mercury wild caught tuna. As you can see from the reviews of their canned Tuna this really is a very delicious Tuna and they cook it right in the aluminum type pouch that it comes in. When you open the pouch the juices from that cooking are evident. I know many of you probably have bought fresh Tuna in the fish market and find canned Tuna of no comparison. I, myself have only done that once and it turned out very dry and leathery when broiled. I don't know how to compare a Tuna loin like this to a fresh cooked piece of Tuna but if you don't have access to fresh tuna or just want a high quality Tuna for sandwiches or other dishes I truly don't know where you could find a higher quality and certainly more economical piece of fish. This truly is a novel idea whose time has come. Taking a large, fresh piece of fish and putting it in a sealed pouch and cooking it. It is the next best thing to fresh fish, especially when your favorite fish is not in season or available frozen.I wish someone would package Sockeye Salmon like this. The only ingredients in this product are Tuna and sea salt. None of the extenders etc.. in commercial store bought Tuna. Now, Wild Planet's new can's of Tuna are 5 ounces, so you would have to buy 6 1/3 cans to equal this 2 lb. pouch. A cost of $27.00 verses $16.00. So you can see it certainly is a better bargin. The only caveat to ordering this product in such a large size is that once you open it you only have x amount of days to eat it. No problem for a family of 3 or 4 but if it is just one person it may prove to be a bit to much when all you want is one Tuna sandwich, but, I have found that by eating a little each day I can finish a package in 4 days just by having a piece once a day. It's a great way to get some extra protein and omega 3's and I really look forward to having it because it tastes so good. I hope this was helpful.

column9: Good product, but canned versions are more moist
column10: Let me explain that title.  Given how the products are sealed and cooked in the container in their own natural juices, there is as much juice per ounce (allowing for variation in each fish) in both the canned and pouched versions.  However, at least in my experience, the cans keep the meat chunks immersed in the liquid - whereas the pouch allows the juice to pool at the bottom, leaving much of the meat not in contact with it.  I had my pouch laying flat, so it should have kept the meat as moist as possible.  However, the meat seemed quite dry when it came time to eat it.I still give it four stars because (a) the product is of high quality, (b) I respect the fishing practices of this company, and (c) the meat can be moistened by breaking it up and mixing it around in the juices.  Because I use about one-fourth of the package at a time, the need to figure out how much juice to pour out of the pouch for the meat along with having to break it up and mix it together causes me to remove a star.A good product, for sure, but I certainly prefer the canned versions.  I give the canned versions five stars without hesitation.

Imagine, something healthy, tasty, filling, full of omegas and can be eaten hot or cold, you can't beat it!  Excellent tuna well worth the price.  After all, can you put a price on your good health?  Eating healthy is expensive, but my husband and I can get at least four meals out of one pouch, so when you think of it that way, it's not so pricey.  Plus, this tuna can be taken anywhere, camping, hiking, whatever, and takes up very little space.  Put the leftovers in a zip lock bag and chill and you have tuna for several days.  It makes a wonderful protein pick-me-up for lunch at work.  Wild Planet is the brand all the health experts recommend because of its low mercury, its clean water location and the fact that it is wild-caught.  They tout it as the cleanest, purest, freshest tuna available.  If the proof is in the taste, I wholeheartedly agree!

I was simply looking for a tuna product that does not contain "vegetable broth" when I discovered I could have that AND low mercury, low environmental impact tuna too.This tuna tastes better than any of the canned stuff (with or without broth) that I was buying at the local supermarket. It does not taste as great as fresh caught, obviously, but it is great for putting on salads or making tuna sandwiches, dips, etc. We would buy the most expensive well-known brands and this tops them all. My first thought was that it tastes "fancy" like it came from a deli. My finicky husband loves it!The fish remains "moist" but not wet like the canned kind. If you squeeze out the water of canned tuna anyway, this is already done for you, basically. And, the foil pouch is infinitely easier to deal with than opening several sharp-edged cans.As for price... I do not live close to any discount stores and the only brand I was buying (which unfortunately started adding vegetable broth recently) would cost me $7.49 for a four pack. If you choose the subscription price, which includes shipping, this tuna becomes very competitive with the expensive supermarket versions. Tasting better and being better for you makes it an easy winner.

What you get is a very delicious tuna steak that has been sourced from a healthy location and packaged consciously both for the sake of the environment and the consumers' health.  Good value for the money and I would definitely recommend it as well as keep purchasing it.

column9: Works for me - at half dose.

He keeps throwing up big hard pieces of the bone and had a hard time breathing a few times when pieces were getting stuck in his throat on the way out. HORRIBLE product, and very dangerous. I can't believe Purina can sell these with a clear conscious.
After giving my dog one of the bones she became very sick and threw up for an hour later that night. And continued to dry heave for 20-30 mins after that. Don't chance it!

I have a 4 year old male lab and he ate this thing in about half hour (some people were saying it lasts days, thats bs) but anyway it expensive considering how  fast it was gone.......I will not be buying anymore

This stuff is great!!  I was so skeptical, but there were no harsh effects like gas or diarrhea.  I used to use "Chiro-Klenz", which I had to time just right and clear out my schedule one morning a week.  That's not a great way to live.  This stuff works so naturally, and I'm so glad I found it.  You will be too!

I love this tea.  It has a smooth mild flavor and it works!  I drink one glass of tea before I go to bed.  When I wake up, I'm ready to go.  It did cause any cramping or negative side effects.  I think it has a much better taste than the other constipation tea, "Smooth Move".

I am a tea-aholic. I tried this tea one morning, just to see what it tasted like, and it was not bad for this type of stuff, if you know what I mean. I actually kind of enjoyed the taste. So I started using it every day and let me say, it made me go regularly. It's very natural, but it actually works in helping you go regularly an is not overkill.

I purchased this because I am on a medication (Wellbutrin) that has completely stopped everything pretty drastically. Despite that situation, I still experienced alot of cramping the greater part of the next day after drinking the tea before bed, something that I didn't think would happen because of the chamomile, etc. in the tea.  I suppose 'it worked', but it was just very very uncomfortable for me.  I will probably use this again because of my situation and when I have a free day at home of course, but wouldn't recommend for someone with just mild issues.

First had this tea in a restaurant.  Bought a couple of boxes for my son, who likes good tea, but can't brew loose at school.  This is an excellent choice.  I also like the Twinings English Breakfast, but he finds this tea better.  I've been happy with all of their teas and particularly like the holiday tea.

This is the best black tea I've ever had that came out of a teabag.  It has a distinct and rich tangy flavor that is almost reminiscent of an expensive bourbon.  Most other brands seem highly unsatisfactory after getting used to this delicious tea, so I plan to keep some around all the time.  It's a little expensive but nowhere near as expensive as going to a cafe or tea house to get a great cup of tea.

This is a really nice tea and I love the beautiful packaging.  I wanted to love everything else about it but I kept tasting a slightly sour note in some cups... I thought it might be the milk I'd used, but many brands and quarts of milk later, I still notice it sometimes.  It is still really good tea but I will probably go back to Twinings English Breakfast after this box as it is just as good and a bit cheaper, albeit with less attractive packaging.  I also ordered the Harney & Sons English Breakfast tea sachets and those do not have the occasional sour aftertaste but are a bit more expensive for an everyday tea and not quite as good as Kusmi teas for special occasions.

Just discovered this flavor and prefer it to Hazelnut  - I  bought a small pack in the grocery store because Hazelnut seems to be scarce in my area.  Altho I wish customers could purchase K-Cups individually to try flavors;  I'm contented for awhile with the double 24 pack offered thru Amazon of the Green Mountain Caramel Vanilla Cream.
I am not a coffee drinker, but I like the Caramel Vanilla Cream with the Keurig Brewer.  It is my daughter's coffee maker and when she moves out I'll have to buy my own.

From the name and the description, I was expecting a creamy drink.  This is just coffee with a little caramel flavoring, barely enough to taste.  I'd rather have plain coffee than this.  I was looking for something really creamy with a nice caramel flavoring.  I finally found it - Grove Square Caramel Cappuccino.  It is exactly what I wanted.  It's sweet and creamy and I don't have to add a thing to make it taste the way I want it to. Great for a special treat to myself. And if you like that kind of drink, I also recommend Cafe Escapes Chai Tea Latte.  It has a wonderful aroma and flavor too.

Good flavor. I use vanilla soy milk in my coffee so it enhances the flavor of this coffee without the need for sugar. I will purchase it again and I am pleased that I can find it on Amazon cheaper than near my home.

This blend brews nicely on smaller settings but if you're looking for a full size drinker, this isn't it. It tastes good and smells great while brewing. Don't try to spread it too thin and you'll have a nice little cup of flavorful goodness.

I like this a lot.  My favorite is Wolfgang Puck Creme Caramel....but this definitely comes close to it.  It's mild...doesn't have a bad aftertaste, and soothes that "sweet" urge when you want that in your coffee.
Great taste and an aroma that fills the house when you brew it. I had some guests come over and they all raved about it when they had it.
This is my favorite flavor of coffee for my Keurig.  I like coffee that is a lighter brew, and this is perfect. I was happy to find it at an even lower price here.
Love the coffee and the best price. Arrived fast and reliabe. I will order more as soon as we run low.

Even though there are several hundred different blends now in the K-cup line I have become fond of the Green Mountain brand.  This new one to me has become one of my favorites.  I always drink it black so adding flavored creamers is not something I do.  There is just enough vanilla cream in this to give it some taste and the caramel adds just enough to make it special.  If I am having only one cup, no matter what time of day, this is my choice usually.My wife isn't really a hot coffee fan but we drink it iced, this is one of her favorites on ice also.

column9: Was a gift, but transaction was flawless
column10: I sent these to a friend of mine who fell in love with them when we studied abroad. They arrived on time and apparently quite edible because she has been loving them! Only downside is the seller doesn't allow for any sort of note enclosure to let the recipient know who its from. Luckily this gift was a no-brainer as she knew I sent it.  Add in the option of allowing a written message and I'd give this 5 stars.

"Bounty" bars consist of a soft, almost molten center of sweet coconut coated in an outer layer of milk chocolate. You can easily buy them "over the counter" here in Australia. But if that's not the case where you are, and you don't mind a diet rich in junk food, then yes, this is a candy bar worth going to the trouble of ordering over the internet.Note that here on Amazon you can purchase bounty bars in boxes with varying numbers of bars inside, so it is worth your while to crunch the numbers and think about what package offers the best value for you. At the same time, it may not be entirely in the best interests of your health to have _too_ many of these things lying around at home all at once!Theo.

You only know the soul of a company (or a person for that matter) when something goes WRONG. Well there was a mix up on my order. Unfortunately the woman on the phone was unfriendly, accusing and rude! Wow! How can people run a business like this? How can they think it is okay to talk to someone, much less a customer, with such an attitude? Needless to say I did not receive my order in time for my event. It is time to find a different brand of gluten free flours. Any ideas?

column9: It's pretty good for certain things
column10: This flour works fine for certain things, depending on your taste preferences.  It has a very strong aftertaste (kind of bitter/sour) because of the bean flour.  Thus it is pretty strong in plain breads and rolls.  If you don't mind that, then good for you!  (My husband is pretty sensitive and can't tolerate the bean flour or taste very well.)  I found it works better in cookies, chocolate or spice cakes, brownies, banana bread, and pizza dough.  Because these baked goods are made with other strong flavors, they help mellow out the bean taste which can be pretty overpowering if you don't have something with which to temper it.  I like the consistency of this flour better than the rice flour blend I've also been using but again, consider your taste preferences and what you'll be baking/cooking with it.

column9: Just like Mama used to make...
column10: With a son recently diagnosed with Autism, I was faced with revamping his diet to a gluten-free, dairy-free diet.  I tried mixing different gluten free flours (rice, potato, tapioca) myself, but it's not nearly as good as this flour blend. I really think the addition of the bean flours makes the difference. I made chocolate chip cookies (dark chocolate chips--no dairy)with it and served it to my daughter's girl scout troop, and they couldn't tell the difference.  That's all the validation I needed.

This flour stinks of Garbanzo beans, and I like Garbanzo beans on any other occasion, but for some reason the smell is so strong when ground, I have learned to read the labels of GF products and if beans are the first ingredient I will not but it.  My guess is some people are more sensitive to it then others, it almost makes me gag when the flour is wet.  I do have friends who don't mind it or don't notice it, but me and my non Celiac boyfriend think it's nasty.  Since we love to bake, I have found that equal parts white rice flour and Tapioca flour with a teaspoon of xanthem gum work great in place of flour.

We used this for Pancakes Christmas morning. Personally I did not like the bean flour at first, I thought it tasted like soap. My non-gluten-free family, however, LOVED it and *insisted* I use it from now on. They said it was not as gritty as rice flour and had the texture of "real" bread. As for the taste, they didn't know what I was talking about. They loved it.I tried this one again, and snuck some into cookies, then tried the Bob's Red Mill GF Chocolate Cake mix with the bean flour, and it's grown on me. I stand corrected and I am actually kicking myself for not allowing myself to grow a taste for it sooner.It's opened a new world of Gluten free baking for me just when I thought I had it all together with the rice flour.I have gone back now and looked at my "Gluten Free Gourmet" book and have a new eye for the recipes requiring bean flour.It took our stomachs minimal time getting used to the beans, if you catch my drift, but after the first few batches of baked goods (about 3 in a week) we have adjusted.We feel better after using this mix because of the fiber and protein, as opposed to all that starch and empty carbs of the the white rice flour. I don't have to pass round the laxative anymore (a common reality of switching to the GF diet.)Make some pancakes (2 cups of the flour mix, 1 tsp baking soda, an egg, 1/4 cup oil, and 1/2 tsp xantham gum--thin with water or milk to desired consistency)and ease yourself into it with butter and syrup.  Of course the flour smells like beans (duh), but the flavor of the beans is mild after it has been cooked.

I'm allergic to milk, eggs, yeast and all grains (except rye), and this is SOOOO much better than trying to mix all the other non-wheat flours together to get the right combination. Even better, I used it to make dumplings and I couldn't tell the difference from my White Lily flour dumplings! My husband said they were "almost" better than my regular dumplings!  This flour is a God-send for me, the best of the wheat-free flours.  One less tear I have to shed for all the things I can't eat!!

column4: K. Anderson "Living Gluten and Casein free fo...
column10: This is a great GF flour, use it in place of white flour.  Only thing I noticed is sometimes you need to add more than a 1:1 ratio in recipes calling for wheat flour to get the stiffness you need.  Also the addition of Xanthan gum makes for better consistency using this flour.  The back of the packet of flour tells you how much to use depending on the type of finished product you're making.  A bag of Xanthan gum is pricey, but the amounts you need (ie 1/4 tsp for each cup of flour for cookies) is minimal, so it will last for oodles of bags of this flour.  I use the Bob's red mill Xanthan gum too.

I decided to try a bag at a store first before buying in bulk here - man I am glad I did. I didn't really think about the ingredients too much, figuring if it was called "all purpose flour" it would probably work in anything - wrong! Though the texture is nice, the smell and taste completely overpower that benefit.I tried using these to make cookies, and it was horrible...way too much after taste of the bean flavor. Also, the fava bean thing kind of scares me too - apparently kids should not eat it because of possible health risks if they have certain genetic dispositions. Bob's Red Mill has some great stuff that is gluten free, but this one should be labeled as "garbanzo/fava bean flour", not all purpose.

My daughter can't eat anything with gluten. She was feeling bad because she loves fruitcake. I made some using this flour. I tasted great; almost impossible to tell that it did not contain flour. The only problem is keeping the bread from drying out by the next day, even in the case of fruitcake which have more liquid than most breads.
This flour can be used just like regular flour in most recipes.  It is so nice not to have to mix so many different flours together to be able to bake something.

column9: Rou for gumbo and use for giblet gravy
column10: I use this instead of white flour and like the taste better when making a rou (base) for gumbo. It requires cooking at a little lower temperature when making a rou but it works just fine.  I've been very happy with all of Bob Mill's products.

Can you imagine drowning in your kitchen and someone throwing you a life-line? This is kinda how I felt when the doctor put my son on a gluten free diet for life and then I discovered Bobs Redmill all-purpose flour. For a mother of five and on a tight budget I knew we could not afford the pre-mixed packages as often. I ran out and bought a small bag to try it out first. Now the wet dough does have a strong beany odor and is very different to work with than regular wheat dough, but the recipes were just simple, and the beany smell was NOT there once it was baked. Ive been using it for pizza crusts, loaf sandwhich bread, pancakes, waffles, corn bread, and banana bread. (lots of recipes on Bobs website) Just follow the instructions-room temp. ingredients, add xantham gum, and pre-heated oven. Ive had no problems and all five of my kids have not complained once with our new baked goods! Then to see it on Amazons subscribe and save I was so happy to save an extra percentage and get free shipping. I am also ordering the Annies GF Mac n Cheese, the GF Nut thins carckers, and the GF Nature Valley Almond Crunch bars. Slowly Im building up my amazon subscriptions and actually my time in the specialty stores reading small print will soon be very minimal. Thanks to Amazon!
This is the standard flour in my house, though only my husband is gluten intolerant I use it when ever I need flour, just as I would any all purpose flour

My gluten-free (milk-free, soy-free, egg-free) 9-year-old loves it.  The taste and texture of the flour in sandwich bread is great.  Don't get me wrong.  It's not like wheat bread, but it IS delicious.  I'm not gluten-free, but I prefer this over wheat bread.  I'm not sure what the other reviewers are talking about when they say the bean taste is overpowering or the aftertaste is bitter.  We love the taste!  It's so much more convenient than trying to mix the flours at home, too.  We're big fans!  I can't wait to try it in cookies, pancakes, and other items!

column9: Useful, but Leaves a Bitter After-taste
column10: I have used Bob's Mill All-Purpose Gluten-free flour a few dozen times.  It is affordable, easy to use, and it is high in fiber, something people with Celiac Disease crave and desperately need in their diet.I have used it for making pancakes, cookies, and bread.  It has good form and volume.One drawback is having garbanzo bean flour in the ingredients.  You have to use a lot of sweetener:  brown sugar, white sugar, honey, and/or stevia to counter the bitterness of bean flours.Still, it is nice not to have to combine several flours (ie tapioca, sorghum, xanthum gum, and rice flours with potato or corn starch) from scratch.  This product is healthful, convenient, cost-effective, and robust, but the flavor downside may have some people searching his competitors.  There are gluten-free flours that are far better tasting.

column4: J. Loscheider "No one knows I'm a radical"
column9: Good for much, not for all
column10: This is really a baking mix, and it's not a bad one by any stretch. I'd rather use sorghum, tapioca or corn starch for making sauces or thickening soups, though. What's really nice about Bob's Red Mill All-Purpose GF Flour is that it allows for easy substitution in your Betty Crocker cookbook. I wouldn't recommend it for making yeast breads, though I prefer it for quick breads - muffins, cornbread, and the like.As with any gluten-free flour, you have to make some adjustments, both in terms of the recipe and in terms of your expectations of taste and consistency. Without gluten, baked goods won't hold together as well, so you need a binding agent. Xantham gum is best with this flour, but guar gum will also work.Taste ... you really need a strong flavor in the recipe to cover up the aftertaste. Dark chocolate? You won't notice the bean or tapioca flour aftertaste. Fruits? No problem - I've made delicious blueberry muffins and dark chocolate-cranberry muffins. Sweet taste? Aforementioned cornbread was delicious - especially if you make it with buttermilk. Snickerdoodles? I'd start with sorghum honestly.Consistency - this is a dense, heavy flour. Sifting is essential. If you don't sift, your recipes will turn out still, but they'll be thick and heavy. You'll also need to add extra liquid (milk or oil or egg substitute) to help the dough hold together, rise and gain volume. This rules out yeast doughs for me - I think you can successfully make a bread but I prefer a millet-sorghum-tapioca-potato starch loaf (I also like the slightly spicy flavor of millet).All in all, this should be a pantry staple for the gluten-free household, though keep supplemental flours to experiment with.

column9: My go to pre mixed flour...
column10: I used this flour regularly these days.. When my son was diagnosed with Celiac and myself with lifelong Gluten Intolerance I learned to mix flours pretty quickly. But mixing flours and keeping them fresh is a difficult task with a 5 1/2 year child under the autism umbrella. Initially, the bean flavor of the flour was not my favorite.. But, I have learned to use it under so many applications it is hardly noticeable... I have written down some of my recipes using Bob's All Purpose Gluten Free Flour mix here.. [...] I use Bob's for my Pumpkin and Morning Muffins as well as Vegan Bread..My son and I are Gluten/Wheat, Dairy, Casein, Soy, Corn and Egg free at this point. So, It is very nice to have a mix that is nutritious and readily available with all the from scratch cooking I have to do..

Pros: Perfect TextureCons: Strange TasteI made my first small loaf of bread in my bread machine using this flour yesterday evening (2/18/2010).The result was a light golden-brown, very soft, sandwich-type bread that is easy to slice. I simply loved the texture of how the bread came out.  It's perfect for making sandwiches and toast.  However, it does have a strange taste, which I guess is caused by the bean flour as everyone mentioned.I would've given this flour 5 stars if it tasted better.  I gave it 3 stars because I love the texture so much.  The texture is just what I had been looking for in a gluten-free bread but I'm not a big fan of the taste.I usually buy Pamela's flours which I absolutely love, but when I made her bread machine bread recipe, it was a bit too dense for my liking. Plus Pamela's is a bit out of my budget right now.  I bought the Bob's All-Purpose because it is sold in bulk at my local health food store for $1.99/lb. which is a great buy for celiacs/gluten intolerants on a budget.I'm the gluten-sensitive one in the family but surprisingly, my daughter who is a very picky eater really enjoyed this bread.This flour is worth the buy if you can get used to the taste.
Great to use this gluten free product. It does serve the purpose. Use in all recipes especially cookies, and cakes.

My wife has been on a gluten-free diet the last few years.  We stumbled on this product in the grocery store and have stuck with it ever since.  She mostly uses it to make banana bread, muffins, etc., but also uses it to bread pork chops and chicken.It tastes fine to me, no detectable aftertaste or anything, and it has the right amount of protein so that baked goods mostly rise the way they should.Recently our grocer stopped carrying this, so I turned to Amazon.  It's exactly the same price as the grocery store, and my wife can bake stuff again.

After reading the reviews I was leery of trying this flour.  I purchased a single bag to try, and I'm so glad I did!  Generally most of the gluten free flours have very little nutritional value.  I know this is true of regular all-purpose flour as well, but considering I can't have regular multi-grain/whole-grain things I figured that if I could find a gluten free flour with extra nutrition in it, it couldn't hurt.  Generally I've used this in a ratio of 1:2 or 2:1 with regular gluten free all purpose flour; I've never tried using it just on it's own based on the reviews here.  I've been very pleasantly surprised.  It's helped the regular flour retain more moisture in cooking so I haven't had to rely on adding much xantham gum.  I haven't been able to taste the beans or an aftertaste at all.  It might be due to the mixing with other flour, the amount of spice I use in my baked goods, or I just have tastebuds that don't notice or don't mind.  My husband is pretty picky though and he's eaten baked goods using this and hasn't mentioned anything about a bean flavor.  I'd suggest giving this a try if you're willing to mix it up with another flour and if you tend to like spiced baked goods.
Use just like you would use bleached white flour.  Butter, flour, milk and cheese and you have a great cheese sauce for mac and cheese.

I really do like this flour for baking. Yes, it has a beany flavor, but only at first, it goes away once you bake your items. I can see how someone who is particularly sensitive to that flavor would not like it, though. I myself have had good results with it and just made some *awesome* gluten-free Blondies. No complaints from family members about beany-ness. I made bread with this flour and was not all that happy with how it turned out, but I am new at gluten-free baking, so it may just take some adjustment. I am especially glad that it does not contain xanthan gum, which I will not use because it is made from corn and is at high risk for being GMO. I just add guar gum when needed. But it does so well at baking cookies and muffins that I will definitely make it a staple in my pantry.

I use this flour to make bread in my West Bend Hi-Rise breadmaker:- 3 cups Bob's Red Mill AP baking flour- 3/4 tsp. sea salt- 2.5 Tbs. sugar- 2 Tbs. potato flakes- 1.5 tsp. xanthan gum- 1.5 cups milk (I use soy or coconut) @ 80 degrees F- 2 eggs, beaten- 1/4 c. canola oil- 1 pckg. Red Star Quick-Rise yeastCombine dry ingredients.  Pour milk into machine, then eggs, then oil, then dry stuff - level it off, then sprinkly yeast on top.  I use the Sandwich setting, medium crust, makes 1.5 lb. loaf.  Has a nice texture, makes great toast.If you detect a bean-y flavor, just use more sugar next time or herbs/spices.

I bought this flour specifically to see if I could make my favorite chocolate chip cookies with it, Toll House.  There is a recipe on the back of the bag, but I didn't use it.  I substituted the Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free Baking Flour for the same measurement of regular flour in the Toll House recipe.  Other than that I followed it exactly and I added chopped pecans.  The cookies are delicious and you cannot tell they are gluten free at all.  The only difference I noticed is they tend to fall apart easily if removed from the pan too quickly.  If allowed to cool completely (about 10 mins) prior to removing from pan, they hold up perfectly.  The Bob's Red Mill Chocolate Chip Recipe calls for Xanthan gum which is expensive and I don't feel is necessary when using the Nestle Toll House recipe.  The texture was perfect and very similar to the wheat flour version.  These cookies actually reminded me of the first chocolate chip cookies I ever had.  The batter melted around the chips as they baked, making it look like the chips were poking through the surface of the cookie.  For the best flavor possible always use real butter for chocolate chip cookies.
I use the Gluten free AP flour for my gluten free items and my customers love it! I recommend it for all your gluten free baking.

I wish I could use this flour. I'm new to gluten free and didnt think of the issues "bean flour" could cause. The taste is fine and the banana bread recipe on the bag is wonderful UNTILL its digested. We all had horrible gas pains. I tried it in a couple of recipes but our systems just couldn't adjust. I had to throw the rest of the bag away.

I've used this flour for a few recipes and all the recipes worked out fine. It works well for pizza dough, cobbler, and bread. There is some bean flavor that is quite strong in its raw form, but I've never found the flavor to seep into the cooked product.

column9: Great Gluten Flour if you're in a hurry or anytime!
column10: This is a great gluten free flour to use if you're in a hurry trying to cook something or anytime! I enjoyed making the gluten free banana bread on the back of the package. It was good but grainy. But when I don't have time or don't feel like mixing up some other gluten free flour blends or don't have any in the house it's great.

We recently went GF for health reasons and I stopped baking.  It's been hard.  Purchased Bob's GF All Purpose Flour at store to try along with Pamela's GF Ultimate Baking Mix.  I read the reviews and sifted the Bob's flour before using.  Definitely can taste the bitter/bean flavor if you lick the spatula of cookie or brownie dough, but once cooked I couldn't tell that it was there.  Finished cookies and brownies tasted like they used to with wheat flour.  They were denser than Pamela's for sure, but that's how I remember my brownies tasting.  I really liked it and think it was a great substitute.  Best priced GF flour mix I could find too.

column9: Can't tell the difference from regular flour
column10: My wife and I cook with this flour all the time and use it to coat chicken or fish with breadcrumbs and other toppings. We have never baked with it so I can't speak to how well any homemade desserts come out with this flour, but for regular cooking we have never found ourselves missing regular flour. Bob's Red Mill makes so many high quality GF products and this flour is generally available at most supermarkets and even quite often in discount stores at up to 50% off the price.

I've been using this product for most of my Gluten Free Baking. I love that I can use my own recipes substituting it 1:1 for reg flour & adding Xanthan Gum (a guide for how much xanthan gum to add can be found on Bob's Red Mill Website along with recipes).  I frequently make my own banana bread recipe, which turns out really moist, & actually tastes like real bread (not dry & grainy like some gluten free breads). It is now a staple in my kitchen.

I purchased this flour to make a quick, gluten-free biscuit recipe that a friend gave me and it has worked great for that recipe.  Tonight, I decided to make a peanut-butter pie for my hubbie's birthday.  Feeling lazy, I used the all-purpose flour to make the pie crust (instead of mixing my own flour mixture...which I usually do!).  Well...the garbanzo bean flour so many reviewers have complained about made the dough horribly bitter.  I added some confectioner's sugar to sweeten it.  I ended up with a gooey mass of something that I plopped into a pan and baked so as not to waste it!  I had to start all over again and made a cereal crust instead.  Double the trouble, double the mess!  THAT's what I get for being lazy!  Anyway, the point is, this flour is great for breads, biscuits, rolls, and so forth, but NOT for anything sweet!  Don't use it for your cakes, cookies, pie crusts, etc.  You won't get the flavor you expect!  Perhaps it should be renamed, "Some Purpose Flour!"  Happy baking!UPDATE:  Originally, I emphasized that this flour is not for all purposes.  Well, now it seems it is for no purpose at all because it is full of bugs!  I keep my flour in Lock 'n Lock containers and none of my other flours have suffered the same fate (in the same cupboard).  This leads me to believe that the little buggers were already in the flour when I got it...  I'll be looking for another flour mix now!

I have to agree with the others who commented on the aftertaste.  I ordered this because of the reviews about convenience and was very excited to try it.  I made cookies with it this weekend and couldn't stand the taste of the batter or the cookie (I was hoping cooking would get rid of the bad taste).  My husband and daughters didn't mind it, but my son and I couldn't eat them.  Be aware that this is an item that can not be returned, so try a bag from the store first.  I unfortunately did not.

This mix is so good that it's all I now use for all of my baking.  We have a son who is gluten, dairy, egg and many other "frees" due to allergies.  This mix makes my life so much easier.  I've used it for cookies, cakes, muffins, sweet breads, to thicken gravy, and many other uses.  It is a keeper in our kitchen!

I made a pie crust for an apple pie out of this flour.  I had to throw the apple pie out.  The flour smells and tastes like garbanzo beans, because that is it's main ingredient.  It worked fine for a curried steak and kidney pie, so I will be only using it for savoury dishes that can be spiced up Middle-Eastern style.  Unless you have celiac disease, I highly recommend spelt flour for sweet baked goods.  It actually tastes better than white wheat.  I usually use whole grain in combination with oats and flaxseed for some healthful muffins, but the white spelt will give you the same baking results as white wheat, particularly if you are making fragile pastry or baked goods with yeast.
