Bob's GF All-Purpose Flour blend is one of my favorite quick fixes for most of my general needs for baking. I always try to have most of what a recipe calls for, but there are times where I cannot find one or two things at the store, or I just don't feel like running back out to get something I forgot. In times like that, this flour mix goes easily into most any recipe. Does not leave bad aftertastes and is fluffy enough to make a great cake, too!Would highly recommend for any GF family or individual!

This is a pretty good flour mix - however has a bean aftertaste. Because if that, I don't like it for bread. However, it is wonderful for breading chicken or fish, and OK for cakes like chocolate where the other flavors hide the bean taste.

column9: Can't get the smell out of my kitchen, or the taste out of my mouth!
column10: I'm new to gluten free baking, but I really liked this brand, and thought it was a good choice rather than having to buy 4 different kinds of flour for one recipe. Boy was I wrong! I made a batch of pumpkin cookies with this. The consistancy was fine, but the taste was FOUL! Someone else called the taste toxic, and I think that sums it up well. I even tried to make another batch of different cookies to make sure it wasn't something else that was wrong. More horrible cookies...more wasted ingredients. Do not buy this for baking, you'll only end up wasting your time and money.

I am giving it 2 stars because I absolutely LOVE Bob's mixes.  My favorite is the Vanilla Cake Mix.  BUT this product I unfortunately bought a case of and I cannot use it for anything.  I cannot stand garbanzo beans in the form of flour.  I like it prepared other ways but in flour it makes EVERYthing taste like it.  I recently made cheese garlic biscuits with it because I assumed that garlic would mask the tast of the garbanzo.  WRONG!!!  :/  It was EXTREMELY noticeable even though I added a lot of extra garlic and cheese.  We ate them because the TEXTURE was nice.  If you have taste issues but like the texture of things, then this baking mix might fly.  BUT if taste is what you are looking for then I would go with Pamela's baking mix or quite frankly, it is easy to make your own.

column9: Better than no flour I suppose!
column10: When my hubby realized he had to eat gluten free, this was one of the first products I tried. VERY disappointed, I can tell you! The baked goods were nothing like I expected, and the beany taste was very off-putting. The bread I made with it collapsed a few minutes out of the oven (as it cooled) and was inedible once cold. The good news is I let it dry out, crumbled it up and used it for breading on baked chicken.I gave up on baked goods for a long while. Then recently I bought "Gluten Free on a Shoestring" and she recommended Better Batter mixes. They are much pricier but taste like the baked goods I am used to.Bob's Mill makes many great products, but I don't care much for this one. Perhaps there are recipes where it shines; I haven't tried any of them.

column9: Not as good as Pamela's or Bisquick
column10: After reading the first few chapters of Wheat Belly: Lose the Wheat, Lose the Weight, and Find Your Path Back to Health and after years of joint inflammation (and now difficulty losing weight), I decided to ditch wheat from my diet. Being desperate to get started, I picked up a bag of this flour at a local store as it was the only one available. My husband and I like our pizzas on Saturday night and since the frozen aisle didn't have anything good in gluten free, I decided to make my own crust. As some reviewers said, the bean flavor really ruined the taste! The pizza crust actually came out well and is one of the best I've ever made with any flour texturewise. But I just didn't like the flavor. I plan to use up the rest in another pizza, but this time will add spices like garlic and oregano plus a little more salt and sugar to the crust itself to mask that taste. My advice would be to get Pamela's or Bisquick gluten-free. Both are good and don't have weird aftertastes.

Just made my very first gluten-free loaf of bread using Bobs Red Mill flour. Definitely not as glorious as a loaf of regular white flour bread fresh out of the oven, but not a terrible substitute. Next on the agenda, gluten free pita wraps. I think I can actually live with this new change in diet, even thrive! Already feeling more energy and less anxiety. :) But I can't speak for everyone as this is the first gluten free flour I have tried.

column9: awesome for people tired of corn goods
column10: This product is amazing I use it to create a variety in the tortillas I prepare and I use it for cakes as well. It tastes absolutely amazing. Although adding a little bit of xanthan gum also helps solve the problem of it rising well for bakery.
I love all Bob's Red Mill gluten-free products. Every baked good I have made with this mix has turned out wonderfully.

column9: More versatile than you think: Great fresh pasta!
column10: Fresh Pasta from Bob's:1 c. Bob's AP GF Flour2 tea. xanthan gum1/2 tea. salt1 Tb. extra virgin olive oil2 eggs, beatenAs reviewers have noted the fava and garbanzo bean flavors can be quite present in baked goods that aren't strongly flavored but the above fresh pasta recipe doesn't suffer from that problem, and can be treated like 'normal' fresh pasta. I can't explain it but it's a great thing.

I really wanted to love this flour. I really did. I made banana nut muffins, bread, peanut butter and jelly cookies, corn muffins, etc with this flour and it all tasted terrible. Granted, I have to be on a dairy and gluten free diet so things aren't going to taste exactly like they did before but, my baked goods were infinitely better when I was only using gluten free oat flour. I bought a couple of 44oz bags because I love Bob's and I thought I found THE flour that would make baking fun and delicious again. I've thrown the rest away so that was $20 or so down the drain - awesome. The bean taste is so strong it cuts through everything. There is no mellowing whatsoever. I've tried adding extra sugar, extra vanilla extract, extra anything with flavor just to lessen the bean-y aftertaste or make it go away. No such luck. I'm sure this flour is good for something (can't think of anything though). If you don't mind a strong bean-y taste (and the aftertaste really lingers), then go ahead and buy this flour. Otherwise, find something else (and please send me suggestions!!!) or make your own blend at home.
This stuff is hand's down the best GF flour product I've tried -- and I've tried a lot.  You do need to add a touch of xanthan gum for breads and such.

column9: Not what I thought but still works
column10: I'm new to ordering on-line for gluten free foods so when I ordered this product I thought it had the xanthum gum already in it. But it didn't. It wouldn't have mattered but I never seem to get it right when I add the gum. So I try to avoid the mixes that I need to add any.So I use this flour for cooking like adding into casseroles. Just not baking. :-(So I like it still since it was a great price for flour.

Ever since my fiance has been diagnosed with celiac's, I have been trying to adapt the numerous bread, cake, cookie, and other pastry recipes he loves to be gluten-free. I usually make my own mix, which gives me greater control in adapting the flours to the different types of baked goods (e.g., higher starch content, lower protein). I have, however, gotten a little tired of stocking up to almost 2 dozen types of GF flours, and so I decided to give pre-mixed flours a try. I tried Bob's Red Mill since I've used all their other products and have been really impressed by them. I used this flour mix to make a chocolate cake. When it came time to fold in the flour, the beany smell was so overwhelming it really made me want to barf. I felt so disgusted by the batter, which I have worked quite a long time, and felt I ruined the cake. Since the cake was for my fiance's birthday, I didn't want him to not have a cake, so I went ahead and baked it. The beany smell subsided a lot while the cake baked, and the cake took almost 10 minutes longer to be done )compared when I used to make it with gluten flours). There was an aftertaste, which, while subtle, can be clearly tasted (metallic/plasticky). If baking spiced cakes/heavily flavored baked goods, then I guess this is fine in a pinch. However, for delicate stuff, this GF APF mix will ruin the experience for you

After not having access to a kitchen while in my law school's dorms last year, I was happy this year to have an apartment where I could bake again. Unfortunately, I found out when classes started again that one of my dear friends had discovered over the summer that she has a gluten intolerance. Since I bake to share, I resolved to find a way to bake for her as well. I found Bob's Red Mill flour at the grocery store and figured I'd give it a shot; I didn't realize I'd need xanthan gum, so it took a second trip to the store before I was actually ready to bake. Everything I've made so far has turned out perfectly. I haven't noticed a strong bean flavor at all, even when making a white cake for my friend's birthday last week. It didn't turn out quite as fluffy as I would have hoped, but it tasted fine and was plenty moist. (It was a new recipe anyway, so that could be why.) Overall I've been pleased with the product and its availability. While I kind of wish they'd just include the xanthan gum, they do recommend different amounts for different baked goods so I can understand why they'd sell it separately (beyond the obvious potential moneygrubbing reasons).

column9: The Garbanzo flour kind of ruins it
column10: I love Bob's Red Mill and as a gluten-intolerant person, am very thankful for their products. Over time since I've GF I've learned that some GF flours taste funky, sour or just plain nasty. Garbanzo bean flour fits the bill. It is so overpowering. Other than that the texture of the baked goods using this mix is good. Just be aware of the garbanzo flour, it's a bit much. My search is still on for a good GF baking mix.

I like some of the Bob's products, but this one makes a baked good that I would describe as "dry bean insulation". The texture is passable, almost, but kind of mealy. It's not quite crumbly because it comes out on the hard/dense side. It's like foamy-consistency GF stuff, but harder, so it makes me think of that poufy yellow insulation stuff that they use in houses. Hard but foamy, somehow.But the main thing is, the bean flavor is so strong. I can see trying to mask it with other things, but I think it comes through even very strong flavors. For example, we make homemade baked beans (pretty strong maple/bacon type flavor, the way I make them) and have a thin slice of toast with grilled tomato, those beans, and butter on top for breakfast. Even though I am eating this bread with beans on top, I can taste the beans in the bread OVER the baked beans. That's just stupid. I can understand some people who have not tried many of the GF all purpose flour mixes out there might find this mix acceptable, and it's certainly easier to use than making your own from scratch, but I would rather skip bread totally than eat something made from this stuff. My suggestion? Try Pamela's all purpose mixes if you're baking, and try Udi's brand if you don't have the time (they make a genuinely tasty bagel that's not a hockey puck).I even find the bean taste too strong when a cup of this is added to another, non-beany mix, because we ran out. In fact, that's typically the only way we'd use it now, because some got bought by mistake and when we run out of good stuff we forget how much we dislike this stuff and mix in a cup or half a cup to "bridge the gap". I would not consider myself very flavor-sensitive -- I'll basically eat anything, and I actually like beans a lot -- but the flavor is just super intense. Maybe if that was all you could eat for a year you could get used to it, but why bother?

As soon as I opened this the smell was overpowering. It has such a terrible smell. My youngest and I got the batter for chocolate chip cookies all put together and then he wanted a taste. He always wants a taste of the cookie batter before we put it in the oven. He took one taste and ran to the sink and starting spitting and then put his mouth under the faucet. I decided to take a taste and could't believe how terrible it was. I would avoid this if you are looking for a gluten-free flour. There has to be a better brand.

I like Bob's flours, and I've recently gone gluten-free. I bought this mix on recommendation and I really don't like it. The fava and garbanzo bean flavor is way too strong for my taste. Perhaps I just need to have patience while my palette adjusts. But I wouldn't recommend this to anyone who is just starting off gluten free. I'd rather recommend something that has flours that mimic the flavors of wheat like sorghum, buckwheat, tapioca, and almond, etc.

I found this product in the health food section of the local grocery store.  All I can say is thank God I bought the smallest size before ordering a larger quantity.  This is at-best a barely adequate substitute for regular all-purpose flour.  It imparts a strong bean taste to baked goods.  Is that what you're really looking for flavor-wise?  I don't think so.  Sorry,  this  might be good in savory dishes, but as far as desserts or sweet snacks--it's a dud.In terms of texture, I found it to be too grainy.  But in all defense to the product, most GF flours are not really the same thing as regular wheat flour in terms of texture.  That's why virtually all the GF recipes recommend adding xanthan gum.  And on this point--since they all recommend adding the xanthan, why don't they just put it in the flour to begin with?  Or at least include a packet of it in the box (Heaven knows they charge enough for the flour--would a packet of xanthan gum be too much to ask?).I was hoping I had found a solution to the gluten problem of regular wheat flour in this product.  I didn't and am still ISO an adequate substitute.

I Noticed in my late teens that I'd feel sick to my stomach every time I ate wheat products, so began avoiding them but missed out on cakes and cookies and pancakes etc. Now I'm all about Gluten Free, which usually means its rice flour, potato, or almond. I feel so much better now. I bake everything gluten free now and when I share my baked products with family and friends they don't even suspect or notice the difference, now I can bake everything using a GF product that is healthy for me and now I'm not missing out when I go to parties!!!!(Diagnosed Hypothyroid 2007)

column9: Avoid in baked goods, pretty good in pastas.
column10: So I have a love/like/hate relationship with "Bob" I love his other milled gluten flour flours, I tolerate the pancake mix, I hate his biscuit mix. I've tried this flour mix with bread, biscuits and pancake and haven't like it at all, the only thing I do like it in is homemade gnocchi or pumpkin pasta pillows. It imparts a strange smell from the bean flour that overwhelms your ability to discern the flavor.

column9: Great Texture GF but not for sensitive tastebuds
column10: This all purpose mix lends itself wonderfully to the Bette Hagman's The Gluten Free Gourmet Bakes Bread recipes. I see a lot of persons here have a problem with the strong bean flavour.  This may not be suitable for making absolutely plain breads but rather breads that are flavoured.  When I make hamburger buns I use treacle (or rather molasses)in the recipe. I also use sesame seeds.  My son loves it and I think that it tastes great.  The bread that this will make also has the most wonderful texture.  If you want a softer white bread type texture add some sorghum flour.  You will be in heaven.  Don't hesitate to try it but just use things like raisons and dried fruit, cinnamon or even savoury items.  You just might like it!

column9: BRM helped me love baking again!
column10: I love this flour!  I now bake non-stop and don't deny my gluten-free self anything anymore.  Bread, muffins, pancakes; everything turns out wonderful.  I like the hearty taste and extra nutrition from the bean flour.  I will no longer waste time and money experimenting with flour blends or chasing others ideas of the perfect GF flour.  This is it for me!

column9: A 2 because it worked as a dusting but not as a substitute for non-gf flour in recipes.
column10: New to the GF world as of 12/10.  Already tired of the bad taste and smell from GF flours.  Bob's Red Mill products are so easy to find that of course it was the first one I purchased and tried.  Using a mixture of this flour with some salt and pepper for dusting chicken turned out really well.  Next I tried using it in muffins and biscuits as I would have my old non-gluten free flours.  Horrible.  I have been doing a lot of research into this and find it to be products that contain fava beans or other bean flours are just not right for substituting for your old non-gf flour.  I just tried Pamela's and loved it, as close to the old way things tasted before being diagnosed.

column4: Beth S R "Parenting is long days and short ye...
column9: Great taste, and the best place to buy, pricewise!
column10: Bob's Red Mill All purpose flour is a great substitute for wheat based all purpose flours!  My daughter and I recently began a gluten free diet, and the other family members love our baked goods...say they're better than the "old recipes!"  I was concerned about the price of the flour and mixes at the grocery store, came to Amazon and found out the best way to buy is on auto delivery!  Now I pay less than half of what the cheapest grocery price was!  Thanks Amazon!

column9: A must for my GFCFSF pantry
column10: I too have tried to mix my own GFCFSF flour and it never comes out as good as this one.  I have used Bob's Red Mill for making cookies, muffins, breading for chicken nuggets and breads.  The only time it didn't work out for me was for making pancakes.  The bean smell and taste was overpowering in the pancakes.  But for everything else, no one could really tell that my baked goods were GFCFSF.

I used this flour to make homemade egg noodles, and they were really gross! They smelled like vegetables and tasted even worse. I've made gluten-free noodles before with a white rice flour blend, and they turned out great. I recommend Whole Foods 365 brand or Gluten Free Pantry brand all purpose flours (1st ingredient white rice flour) for cooking and baking. Those blends look and feel more like white flour, and you usually can't even tell the products are gluten free.
I LOVE crepes, we tried buckwheat flour which is good too, but they don't taste nearly as good as crepes made out of this flour mix.

Using all of Bob's Red Mill GF products has saved my life.  The flour is a staple in my kitchen. This company took responsibility to produce GF Quick and regular rolled oats, which I can now find in my area. Very good products.

column9: Bad Aftertaste - better alternatives for same $
column10: Bob's has done a good job making a wide variety of gluten free flours available for those of us with dietary needs. However, this particular blend is not worth the money.I believe it's the fava beans, but whatever it is, one of the ingredients leaves that nasty, "ugh this definitely gluten free" aftertaste. Don't bake with this stuff - no amount of sugar will cover the nasty taste!There are better alternatives -baking: King Arthur Flour and/or Gluten Free Pantry AP flour are really good options. KAF is the expensive one but you will not be able to tell a taste difference hardly at all. GFP is cheaper and still tastes pretty good.general cooking: you can usually get away with using corn flour (masa harina, look for Maseca brand) if you don't want to use real AP flour, which is pretty cheap and easy to find at the grocery. Otherwise, you could use Bob's rice, potato, etc flours and make your own blend. But I wouldn't use this prepackaged one - gross!

After making my own gluten-free all-purpose flour mix (based on Jules Shepard's recipe) I decided to just make things easier on myself and give Bob's Red Mill All-Purpose Gluten-Free Baking Flour a try.  It turned out to be cheaper than individually buying all the gluten-free flours and starches too.I have been very pleased with this flour and use it cup-for-cup in place of wheat flour in all my recipes.  I've made many kinds of cookies, cornbread, pizza crust, brownies, pie crust, quick breads, etc. (with the addition of the recommended amount of xanthan gum added in) and they've all been great!  People haven't even know my baked goods were GF until I told them.  :)I haven't had much luck making rolls or breads with this flour though.  They've turned out too dense IME, but YMMV.  All-in-all a great product for what I need it for and the price can't be beat.
Thanks for stocking Bob Red Mills and Arrowhead Mills products. They are hard to find in grocery stores. Now I am looking for Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free four for a good price!

column9: Great as a wheat flour replacement
column10: I bought a bag of this at the store to use in gluten free baking. I replaced the wheat flour with an equal amount of this GF flour blend. The results were great! Everything I have made with this flour as a replacement in a regular recipe for wheat flour has turned out delicious. You do need to add the correct portion of xanthan gum or guar gum, but the side of the bag gives you the idea of how much you'll need. I have used this to make cookies, bread (you will need to cook the bread longer than the recipe calls for, I have found), muffins, and pizza crust. It has all turned out great. Highly recommend this flour blend. I signed up for subscribe and save so that I never run out. Plus, it is a much cheaper alternative to buying the flour in the grocery store.

column9: ok, but theres too much bean in the mix
column10: I bought a case of this and use about 1/3  of this along with rice, and soy flour. I dont like this mix at all. The beans gas up my husband so much he cant eat it and it has a strong taste. I get stomache cramps from it. I'm on a gluten free diet and i like the other flours better than this one.

Always looking for good gluten free products, I tried this.  I did not realize when I bought it that it was mostly garbanzo bean flour.  I made some chocolate cookies that turned out fabulous, moist, firm, not crumbly.  They did not have a "beany" taste but if I eat more than 1 cookie, which I do some times, look out!  I've had some bad times with the pain, gas, and bloating that this product is causing.If you can tolerate the beans than I would recommend this flour but if you are like me, steer clear!  I now have 3 bags of the stuff that I need to give away to someone, ugh!

This flour is great for gluten free pancakes! I was craving pancakes for a very long time, but had a gluten intolerance and couldn't have them. When I discovered this flour, I mixed it with buckwheat flour and now make wonderful pancakes every morning!

column9: Bob's Red Mill All Purpose Mix
column10: I have a gluten intolerance and have recently started a gluten free diet.  I decided to try this all purpose mix to see if I could sub 1:1 for regular all purpose flour.  My cookies came out great, but the aftertaste of the bean flour in Bob's mix is awful.  I'm going to try mixing up my own blend of flours.  I don't think I'll buy this again (and I'll stay away from all bean flours from now on!!)
Granted I am new to the Gluten Free life - but this flour tasted toxic.  I have decided to mix my own flour combos and avoid this one - I expected more from this brand!

I've tried most all GF flour blends out there.  This is the most versatile in my opinion.  Also much cheaper/ easier than purchasing many different flours and mixing yourself (especially via Amazon Subscribe & Save).-Good texture-More dietary fiber than other GF blends

column9: Good flour, nice taste, but a recipe would help?
column10: I have tried a couple of the mixes, and they are very cake like, so I thought I'd try again, making my own. All gluten free recipes seem to call for a mix of flours, so at least this gave you the mix, without having to spend a fortune on lots of flours.Recipes - this is the problem though isn't it??? I had tried various of my own flour mixes, and various recipes, and it is always a disaster, which is why I went for the mixes in the first place...Why doesn't the packet come with a recipe? The packet states how much Xantham Gum you need, then says yeasted breads are difficult(!), you MAY require eggs, vinegar, and POSSIBLY more liquid.... May? Possibly?There is a recipe on the website - very similar to a recipe I have already. But another disaster - in the trash.My husband found this[...]and it worked well. Rose beautifully. Still a little cake like, but more like bread than the mixes.But yet again, not like real bread - is it really too much to expect? (The mix I had in England made gorgeous white fluffy bread - 95% the same as 'normal' bread. So I know it is possible to have 'normal' gluten free white sandwich bread.)Bottom line - a good all purpose flour mix. Others have commented on the strong taste - which I didn't notice at all. Tastes to me like normal wheat bread.

IT seems good, although made rather denser muffins than when I make my own mix. But the convenience is so worth it. Tasted fine too. A little heartier in texture and taste than what I mix but interesting for a change. I'd buy it again...

In my opinion, the best all purpose gluten-free flour ever.  You can substitute it cup for cup for regular flour in recipes (usually adding xanthan gum),and finished baked goods always resemble those made with wheat flour. Bob's Red Mill web site offers so many gluten-free recipes, I never have a problem finding a gluten-free alternative to any wheat flour recipe.

column9: A wonderful flour IF you are not hypersensitive to the bean taste
column10: I think there are too many bean-flour critics who have posted critical reviews of this flour.  If you no-likey the bean taste/smell, then seek gluten-free flour eslewhere.  For the rest of you, this flour is wonderful and does not smell nasty/taste nasty/leave a repuslive aftertaste, etc.  I use it for about half of my gf-baking and cooking (and I do a lot of it), for everything from chocolate chip cookies to muffins to deep-fried squash puffs.  In some cases, I suspect it would work better than the other flour combos in other gluten-free recipes, but I am not willing to be too experimental b/c flops are expensive.  If I am converting a recipe to gluten-free, this is the flour that I always use and I've never been even remotely disappointed.

This flour is great.  I have substituted 1 for 1 for regular flour in many recipes and they have all come out great.  (I'm still working in eliminating the xantham gum flavor).  This is a much better buy than buying it at my supermarked or health food store.

column9: Maybe I was spoiled w/ regular wheat flour...
column10: Yuck! This turned my favorite choco chip cookies to yucky. I may be spoiled with the wheat flour, but since my husband was just discovered to have a sensitivity to gluten, I am experimenting. The only reason I gave it 2 stars is because my husband and kids thought they were okay. I can't stand the aftertaste, which in reading the other comments must be the bean flour in the mixture. There must be a better mixture of gluten free flour out there!
This gluten-free flour tastes great! I have made several baked items with it and enjoyed them.

My husband wanted to buy this for me on a whim, because I am sensitive to Gluten. I should have said no, not until I check all reviews. I actually love garbanzo beans so I thought why not try it?I used only 1/6 of this flour in a Puffed Pear Pancake recipe from Real Simple. I used apples instead of pears and extra sugar/cinnamon. I also added some sugar to the batter to try and help cover up any bad flavor. I am not sure why I thought there would be some, but I did. Maybe it had started to smell funny already?Well, I baked 2 apple pancakes. 1 normal and 1 gluten free. I baked them at the same time in the same oven. That's when I started smelling the yucky smell. I was afraid the good one would be contaminated. Thankfully it wasn't. I have yet to offer the GF one to the rest of the family since they have their own. No one else commented on the yucky smell, so maybe I am just hyper sensitive to it. Maybe you do have to make something savory not sweet to enjoy it. All I can say is I am glad only 1/6 of the flour I used was this stuff. The rest was rice, tapioca, and potato. I am new to making my own baking flour mixes. But I have used specialty GF bread flours to make bread and it was delicious! It didn't rise quite right but the flavor was like french bread. I even eat dry crumbly rice bread and that's okay with me. I have even made white bean muffins when on the South Beach diet and those didn't have a weird, toxic taste/aftertaste/smell.So I plan on trying some other way to use this stuff, but if that doesn't work it is in the trash or I will offer it to a local person who may want to try some free GF flour. Maybe they won't notice the taste/smell.

I used this flour to make chocolate chip cookies with, and threw away the batter it tasted SO BAD. I then tasted the dry flour to see if IT was responsible for the bad flavor. It was. IT was thrown in the wastebasket with the batter.Maybe this flour would be good for savory baking, as opposed to sweet baking. But I wouldn't bet MY money on it.
I have used this flour primarily in bread recipes that call for a gluten free flour blend. It has worked in a variety of recipes and is a staple in my gluten free baking.
The bean flour is overwhelming and ruins the taste and smell of pretty much anything you bake with this flour...too bad. :(

Grabanzo bean flour does not taste good in baking anything sweet or in my opinion anything else. I ended up throwing it away. It's interesting how our taste buds differ as I see some people like the taste of this and I can't imagine how it could possibly taste good.

I tried to make cupcakes for my wheat-intolerant mother using this flour blend. I was pretty excited, because my previous GF attempts had involved rice flour, and the cakes would come out quite gritty. So I whipped up my batter and just before putting the cupcakes in the oven, I decided to take a taste. This flour produced the MOST FOUL TASTING thing I have ever put in my mouth. Ever. I thought I might be sick and had to spend about 10 minutes brushing my teeth to get rid of the taste.Don't buy this. Save yourself.

This item is very good - it bakes up well and tastes almost like wheat flour.Just like other things I have bought from Amazon.com, I have come to expect the beat. This is an excellent alternative for wheat flour.

Can I give 0 stars? Being that this is primarily made from ground garbonzo beans, it tastes exactly like.. ground garbanzo beans. The first time I used this, I made GF pancakes. I almost threw up. They tasted like someone chewed up chick peas and spit the paste into my cast iron pan. No amount of syrup could fix it. The next time I used it, I was running low on rice flour so I used about 1/4 cup of this "all purpose" stuff. Again, ruined pancakes. This stuff is horrible.
Great product. I use them to add to real cilantro as cleaning cilantro takes time. Easy to use a tastes great.

column9: Great for allegic cat; high in protein
column10: My cat, who had food allergies of unknown type, really liked this food and could eat it fine from an allergy viewpoint. It is very high in protein (40%). Neither she nor my other cat eat great quantities of it (the recommended feeding for 5-8 lb. cat is 1/4 to 1/2 C per day, and this is assuming an outside cat) as they don't need it. They both free feed. However, it does make the stool of one cat very soft, though still having a shape--so we have problems with feces sticking to her fur and then she rubs her butt on my carpet!! Hence four stars instead of five. The other cat does not have this issue. Due to this issue, I usually mix this food with another food.  Another comment: when one cat was losing weight due to illness, my vet recommended going to kitten food due to its high protein, but this one is much higher in protein than any kitten food I've found.  While it is expensive, they eat little volume of it, and don't use the litter box as much, so I save on both ends.

column9: My cats love it and give it 5 stars!
column10: I normally buy a different brand of grain-free dry cat food but I wanted to try another brand that had some different flavors and came in smaller size packages so I could rotate the flavors more often.  Both my cats love this brand and just dive right into it as soon as I put it in their dish.  I feed it to them in the morning and give them canned food in the evening, but I get the impression from them that they would rather have the dry food all the time : )  I will continue to use this brand in the future.

column9: Cats like it but my vet still recommends Halo
column10: My vet told me not to buy science diet because it was crap - he said avoid cat food products with meal products in them. He said Blue Buffalo was fine but still preferred Halo - my cats however prefer Blue Buffalo to Halo - and since their the ones eating it, I'll buy this.

Please don't rate this food anything less than maybe 4 stars, and it's a little pricey but this is the highest quality dry cat food I've ever bought and it's excellent. If your cat's don't like it, it's because your cats just have different tastes, it's not the food. All cats are different and respond differently to foods. My cats have digestive issues and can't handle grocery store cat food or any of those foods that have corn and all kinds of low quality byproducts. I bought this food and they have had healthy poops ever since. They love the smell and taste so they enjoy it, it's also much better for them nutritional wise.
I changed my cats' food in one day and they started eating it. I think they like it. Great cat food and a very tasty snack for human friends.

column9: Food is good, cat likes it, price is just stupid
column10: My Siberian cat likes this stuff. He's healthy, lean, and active eating it, and I like the 40% protein, grain-free formula. For wilder or hybrid type cats, the protein and no-grain issue seems to be a bigger deal. The ingredients are all pretty sound, so far as I can tell. The stuff doesn't smell bad, has a good texture to it. I've heard vets and breeders say some other brands were hypothetically better (Evo, Wellness, Merrick), but if you look into it - the ingredients are pretty similar.Downsides - the "life-source bits" which are cold-formed vitamins that aren't cooked (which reduces their potency) probably taste like vitamins. My cat is amazingly adept at avoiding these. I have to collect them from his food when he's done and save it to put in his next bowl so it accumulates until he finally caves and eats it. A little concerning though - all the vitamins are in these bits the cat won't eat unless coerced.Also - since Blue Buffalo started running their national TV ads, their price is up 50%+. This stuff is good, it's not that good. To be honest - the cat doesn't eat a ton, the price of the food isn't a big deal - I'm willing to spend a few bucks more a month to have good stuff - but I've seen no evidence this stuff is any better than more reasonably priced (like Blue used to be) like Wellness and Merrick - so I'm looking into switching.

I've done a lot of on line research looking for the best cat food. I have two adorable kittens, who are now 1 year old. The vet says they are in super condition and I credit that to feeding them Blue Buffalo dry food. I buy it when I can afford it - hence, the 4 stars. The price is too high for me to buy regularly.

I have a sick and very picky eater and he likes this food! Most of the cat's/dog's food is made with grain and fillers so I was looking for something better for my beloved pet. If you're not sure if your pet is going to like the food, you can order a smaller size. This one works well and I would recommend it to other pet owners.

I buy this when I can to send to my mother who lives in the country with feral cats that come into her property.  It is expensive, but due to the outdoor conditions and the great appetites that these outdoor cats have (along with our love of animals), I buy this to keep the cats as healthy as possible.  According to my mother, the cats absolutely love this food.

I have a 10 year old cat who is very finicky. After she got an eye infection, a skin conditions, and lost a significant amount of weight with generic commercial cat food, I did my research to find better food. I tried other grain free foods, but she turned her nose up to them (Wellness Core, Natural Balance). Blue Wilderness is the one that she liked...sort of:PROS:-multiple protein sources (chicken, fish, turkey)-my cat eats it-grain free, high protein-keeps cat healthy w/ shiny coatCONS:-my cat picks out the "life-source bits" which are the little dark things-"caramel" is on the ingredient list-slightly more $$ than other brandsOverall, I'll try another grain-free brand because I'm tired of cleaning life-source bits up off the ground and the "caramel" is not an ingredient I'd like to see in cat food. However, this food is still better quality than those commercial brands we all know of.

column9: A little Pricey, but my cats love it!
column10: I fed this to my cats for the first time tonight, and I was honestly afraid they would choke after how fast the wolfed it down! I've been feeding grain free for awhile and wanted to get them something they would eat, especially since the little one has such a sensitive stomach. Only took away one star for the price, it is a bit high.

My kitty has been in this brand of food since he was 6 months old, started in Kitten food then to this type after he was a year old. He LOVES it. Great stuff!....but the price, I thought I was getting the bigger bag, at this price it would have been a deal, it was only 2.5 lbs...ouch! So read carefully on amounts!  I get a 6.5 lbs at the big-box pet store for about $22 and they have a buy program; buy 10 or 11 bags of food and the next one is free! He's my baby and he's still worth it.

I will admit, I have forced my cat to eat all kinds of varieties of cat foods so as to make him not too picky, but this formula is by far his favorite dry food.  The other grain-free brand I tried was Wellness, and he only picked at that.  This food is obviously high quality.  If you're into your kitty, you should be feeding him/her this food.

The food was delivered rapidly and intact.The new formula might be IS better than the old formula BUT my cats just nibble at it eating a little at a time.Other than that I think Blue Buffalo is a bit overpriced-it is an excellent food.I have bought Longevity for my older cats .I have five 21 year old cats-they just nibbled on this a little at a time.They do not like salmon that much.My cats used to eat this chicken recipe like popcorn.My two young cats 4 and 6 months eat Longevity pretty much-more so than the senior citizens.Them eating this slower makes it lasts a little longer.CATS ARE PICKY EATERS!

column9: My finicky cat will not eat this food
column10: Having seen the TV adds for Blue Buffalo pet foods I was very optimistic to try this for my adult cat.  She is very finicky, preferring canned shredded meat to dry food though she will nibble on food like some major brand Cat Chow during the day.  So, I ordered a pouch of this and she just will not eat it.  If I offer it her in the morning and then fresh servings at lunch and dinner, she just will not eat it and sits by her bowl mewing and looking pathetic.  I was very disappointed.

column9: These bulk Energy Drink prices are outrageous
column10: I thought I'd check online to see if buying energy drinks in bulk would be cheaper than buying the 4-8 packs in my local grocery store. Well they're not. At all. In fact the cost of this 8 pack, when you add shipping, is over twice what you'd pay if you bought 8 individually in a convenience store ( give or take some for tax)

THESE ARE SOME OF THE WORST FRUIT SLICES CANDY I HAVE EVER EATEN IN MY LIFE!!! THESE HAVE NO FLAVOR WHATSOEVER.....LIKE EATING PASTE.CANDY FRUIT SLICES ARE SUPPOSED TO HAVE A STRONG FLAVOR.........THESE BARELY HAVE ANY FLAVOR AT ALL...........TRUELY HORRIBLE!!!
Received the order very quickly and was more than satisfied with the product. Would highly recommend to anyone. Excellent quality. Will definitly order again in the future.

column9: Great syrup but notice the name.
column10: This is another great monin syrup that I used to make my own soda.The name is CANDIED orange. Do not expect a marmalade type tastebut a very sweet candy like taste. As a result I wound up using onlyhalf a jigger of this per drink compared to a full measure.Very tasty but not what I expected. If you love orange crush, this is for you. If you love english marmalade like I do, try their blood orange instead.

I read this wrong, I guess. I thought I was going to get a box of 12 breadsticks so I put "2" in for quantity. Well, turns out I was really ordering 2 CASES of 12 boxes EACH. Funny. That explains why it cost me more than $50. I guess I just thought they were that special. They're good. And they are approved on my "diet" so I love them. Just, if you are going to order 2...make sure you want 2 cases. lol

column9: Great crunch for the HCG diet!
column10: I bought these breadsticks for the HCG diet & am sure glad I did.  On such a low calorie diet, the crunch was much appreciated!  I wouldn't want to do the diet without them!  Great product, crunch, & flavor.

I purchased these when I started the HGC diet.  They were a great choice as far as taste goes.  They satisfied my need for a crunch and they had a very pleasant taste to them.  They didn't just have that "stale bread" taste that a lot of breadsticks have. Also, while you do get a few burned breadsticks, you don't get to many.  For the most part they are pretty evenly cooked.On the down side, the quality is not that great.  Every package I opened have had broken breadsticks.  Now I know that breadsticks are fragile and I should expect a few broken ones, but for the most part, almost all of them in a package are broken, and some are broken so bad that they are just dust at the bottom.My biggest issue with the quality is this...so far, we've gone through 8 boxes of these breadsticks and I've come across 15 SEALED packages that contain NO breadsticks.  They are just empty wrappers, AND these empty wrappers aren't just in the box as that weird bonus wrapper you receive on occasion, they COUNT towards the number of packages of breadsticks you get in a box.These breadsticks are by no means cheap, and I honestly do not mind paying for something that is not only part of my diet, but something I enjoy.  I do take issue with the fact that I'm paying a premium price for a product with sub-par quality.
This is the most wonderful product for taking the "edge" off my appitite.I'm always on a diet and these breadsticks keep their crunch a L-O-N-G time.For the $, this is the best diet product I have.

My local store stopped selling the Grissini and I came across these after doing a web search.  Why drive to the other side of town to pick some up when these can be delivered.  They are nice and crunchy.  Because they are smaller I can have 3 sometimes 4 as oppose to only 2 of the other ones I was buying.Tricks the mind into thinking you are getting more. For anyone doing the HCG Diet, these are great.

When I was on the HCG diet, this was required to eat. It was delicious and hard not to eat more. However, it is a very small serving; it is the size of a thin pencil and I wish they would make them a lot bigger because they are addictive!
Grissini Torino Italian Breadsticks are wonderful.  They are like the original grissini Torinese that I remember from my time in Italy.
These breadsticks are HCG approved and are so tasty, way better than Melba toast. YOu have to buy a whole case, but it is worth it. First taste of "bread" in months!

I'm dieting with the HCG protocol.  Breadsticks are impossible to find out my small town grocery store.  Thank you Amazon for carrying these delicious breadsticks.  Thank you Amazon for the prompt delivery.
fast delivery. the packages of grissini were actually larger than i thought (and great for the office munchies).

Easier to grab a stick or two than making popcorn....and I don't need butter or salt!  Lovely for entertaining.  We've gone from a basket of bread to a basket of breadsticks.  Much fewer calories.  I  can't find these in any local stores, so this is great to have them delivered to your door.  It seemed like a pack of 12 would be too many, but the way they are packaged they will stay fresh for a long time and it's great to have them on hand.

These are tasty little breadsticks that my entire family enjoys.  I bought them because I am on the hCG diet and they are an allowed item, but there were SO many in the case that I decided to share.  My kids love them!  They have a nice crunch to them, but are not tough to bite or chew by any means.  The texture is perfect and the taste is absolutely delicious.  They kill off all of my carb cravings!  I will continue to buy these even after I complete the diet, they are just that good.
These breadsticks are Fab-U-Lo-So!  A pack of these babies goes perfectly with a scoop of tuna fish or cottage cheese and a cut up apple for a healthy lunch.  Gotta order more!

These breadsticks are delicious!! Each box has about 9? little pouches, each include about 10 little breadsticks which is about 110 calories. They are quite flavorful, I use them when on the HCG diet, but when ordering from amazon, keep in mind this is for 12 BOXES!!! Which is a ton of these things!! I used the extras over the holidays for an apetizer with a sour cream-based dip... AWESOME!! Definetly worth purchasing and trying!

We are using the Grissini breadsticks as an integral part of our weight reduction diet. In addition to eating the bread sticks with meals, we also use them to make bread crumbs by putting them in a food processor along with a mixture of dry herbs to coat meat prior to baking it. The bread sticks arrived as promised and we have found very few broken so far.

column9: dieting but not HGC - still yum!
column10: Just wanted to say I give these 5 stars even for not being on a diet that calls for them. Less salty than crackers, and more tender than pretzels or packages of breadsticks I remember from many years ago.One box of these is 3.5 oz in weight total, 440 calories, and 6 grams of fat. And that's divided into 5 packets of about 7 sticks each. Pretty hard to overeat these very badly!

I ordered these while on the hcg diet.  They are great breadsticks with good flavor and a super crunch!  Definitely satisfy the "crunch cravings" that I get on hcg.  I will definitely eat them even when I'm off the diet.  Would be great with a salad.  Very happy with this purchase!
I was on the hcg diet and these saved me!  The flavor is great and they are so crispy!  Great snack while still being healthy!

It's says that the expiration date is located somewhere in the package. But, I was suprised that there is no expiration date - I was looking everywhere-  on the product I got. I need to know that detail please.Thank you,

I bought the case of 12 boxes for the HCG diet.  These really were great.  They're that little bit of crunch and carbs you need, and they taste like you aren't dieting!  I'm pretty sure I'm going to have these for forever because of how many I have, but that's really ok with me.  If you're trying to watch your calories, these kind of fool your body into thinking you just ate a handful of crackers.  These arrived in good shape, nothing broken or missing.

I originally had these breadsticks in a restaurant and could not find them in a supermarket or local gourmet shop.  I was thrilled to find them at Amazon and am delighted with receiving them.  They are delicious - light, crunchy and always fresh.  My family is enjoying them as well.  Don't hesitate to try them - you will certainly enjoy eating them.
The Grissini are great for my HCG protocol but a whole case full of them is a bit too much! LOL I will continue to have them anytime I have a carb craving but still watch the portions!

I guess I didn't know what I was ordering! I ordered them to accompany us on the hCG diet ... but we'll be eating them for years to come! (That is hyperbole) There were LOTS in the box. No complaints.

I am now on my second round of the HCG Diet and these bread sticks have been a life saver! I have loved bread my whole life and when I was faced with not being able to eat it I kind of freaked...but I ordered these as they are allowed with the protocal and I am happy i did. I eat 4 sticks every day to stop the cravings and use it as one of my snack items.I suggest these to everyone doing HCG or not - They are very flavorful!!Vicky
These are great for people doing hcg.  They are packaged nicely and give you that crunch you are craving while sticking to your list.  Good deal too!
I love these bread sticks it was a nice change on the hcg diet. wish they sold them in a smaller amounts a whole case takes awhile to get threw.

column9: Love the CRUNCH I get when on my diet!
column10: Anyone who is on a diet will know how it is to miss the cruncy foods that made you overweight in the first place! TRY THESE! You will get the crunch and flavor but not have to feel guilty! This breadstick is also recommended for the HCG DIET!! LOVE IT!
I ordered these breadsticks specifically for use with the hCG diet. They are delicious! I was really pleased with the flavor and freshness.
Although the flavor is excellent, the breadsticks arrived in pieces.  The longestpieces were about 4" long, but most were 1" or 2" and there were lots of crumbs.
I ordered this huge bos of these for this diet i was on.  I still have the whole case left.  Didnt enjoy the taste at all but thats nothing to do with the sell of the product.

I wasn't sure exactly what to expect but these are very tasty, would be a great addition to a pasta dinner stashed upright in a heavy mug.  As someone else here says though, this is a LOT of them, 12 boxes with apx 8 sticks in each of 5 individually wrapped pkgs.  They are very long and thin.  I got them for the HCG diet and I'm glad, but at 2 a day for 6 weeks, I'll have about 10 extra boxes.  I'm not disappointed though, we'll probably find a use for them over the next year.

column9: Bought these for the HCG Diet
column10: I bought these for the HCG Diet... Very similar to soda crackers.  These are very thin crispy breadsticks.  I opted to buy soda crackers for my next go round, not nearly as expensive.

It was very misleading to me whem the ad on Amazon said pack of 12.  I assumed that meant there were 12 breadsticks in the 3.5 Once box and I ordered 2.  Imagine my surprise when a huge package arrived and I unpacked 24 BOXES of the breadsticks.  We'll be eating them for years (if the shelf life is that long)  I was very disappointed that I spent unneccesary money on something I certainly didn't need.

column9: Best GF chocolate chip cookie you will find
column10: I've tried them all, believe me.  Most are just too gritty. But Kinnikinnick's GF Montana chocolate chip cookies taste good. They have that real brown sugar flavor.  Crisp but not gritty at all.  No weird aftertaste.  These are my #1 top choice to buy when I can find them. I am glad Amazon has decided to carry them.  Wild Oats GF mini-chocolate chip cookies are good too, but not AS good as these.
WOW!!  I had no idea that Gluten Free food could be THIS GOOD!!!  Our kids loved them so much they beg for more.  Great product.

column9: Just as good as Chips Ahoy!
column10: I've been eating gluten-free for nearly 3 years and have occasionally missed the little junk food splurge here and there. I saw these cookies on Amazon and decided that, since I've never been disappointed by anything Kinnikinnick put out, I would try them. They are just as wonderful as I hoped they would be. I keep mine in the freezer, as the chocolate chips seem to melt quickly, and just take a few out as I want them.These are truly excellent cookies! I gave the rest of my gluten eating family one cookie each and they could hardly tell the difference between Kinnikinnick and Chips Ahoy.
These cookies taste so good.  I have been diagnosed for about a year now and these cookies are the best I've had. Not too sweet and they have such a great taste and plenty of chocolate chips!!

The only GF cookies that my son will eat. I tried 'em all: cheap, expensive, ordered on the internet, bought from local specialty stores, bought Pamela's etc, etc. All other gluten free cookies pale in comparison. Most others are actually gross. However, these gems are the kind of cookies that you are sitting in front of the tv in the old recliner and its really hard to stop eating them, just like the old (forbidden) Chips Ahoy. This company has a lifelong customer here. Most all of Kinnikinnick's products are the best gluten free that money can buy. Heck, I can't even make them from scratch that taste this good. Happy healthy eating everybody! :)

Those cookies are delicious. I think they could fool anyone that is not on a gluten free diet... They are crispy and light with just the right amount of chocolate chips. If you like gooey or soft chocolate chips cookies those are not for you. But if you like a good crunch you won't be disappointed, they have a great texture and are not gritty like some GF cookies sometimes are.They do not contain soy or dairy which is an added bonus for our family with multiple allergies.My only problem with them is that they're expensive... :-(

These are very addictive. I can't believe that I can't tell they are wheat-free! They are super delicious and do not taste fake or odd in any way. The chocolate chips are divine. I have eaten entirely too many this week after discovering them because I was waiting for them to have a strange after taste or make my tummy funny, but no, these cookies are just perfect. The calories aren't too bad either. It's something like 36 calories per cookie. This cookie gives much joy because eating gluten free is a bit of a hassle and this makes me feel like I am not missing out on anything! Thank you very much Kinnikinnick!!

column9: Best tasting GF cookie, which sucks as I can't stop eating them
column10: They are also sold at Wholefoods.  I have been trying so many brands of cookies and many of them have this dry powdery taste.. Yuck.  However, this cookie sis deliciously crunchy.  I know I should move away from expectations now that I am on a gluten free diet, but as a newbie I am still having a hard time 'cheating' as I miss the old gestures.  Finally, I can indulge on some naughty food wihtout compromising my health or taste.. Yeah!

column9: best GF cookie I have found.....
column10: As you can see from the other reviews, these cookies are exceptional. I have Celiac and most GF cookies I have tried simply taste bad, or have no taste at all.  When you cannot eat gluten, most, if not all of your previous "deserts" cannot be eaten. So it was refreshing to find something that replaced all the previous gluten cookies and deserts. I never thought I would crave "sweets" until I could not eat them.....Kinnikinnick's Montana chocolate chip cookies help fill the void.I just ordered some of these from Amazon as my local store has been out for two weeks....got to have that cookie!

column9: So good my husband eats them!
column10: I have to say that these cookies are so good that when I bought them for my son, my husband and I kept stealing them until they were all gone! I like that they taste like a cookie - not gritty, just the right amount of crunch and a great chocolate taste.

These cookies are very close to the Archway molasses cookies.  They have a very sharp bite of ginger to them, followed by a mellow molasses taste. These are the first GF cookies I have found where I can not tell they are GF. This company makes a chocolate chip Kinnikinnick Foods Gluten-Free Cookies, Montana's Chocolate Chip, 8-Ounce Bags (Pack of 6) that taste like inexpensive store bought choc-chip cookies, not my preference, but not bad at all.  Theses run about $4 each in the store at best, making this a great deal, but the expiration date is not to far out so be aware.

These cookies are hard and crunchy and definitely resemble the store-bought cookies made in mass production bakeries. The taste was good, and the texture similar to somthing from Keebler or another large food processor and baker. I expected these cookies to be more like the gluten-free chocolate chip (or chunk) cookies from Pamela's. Pamela's I would rate with five stars. Overall the Kinnikinnick brand would be fine for kids who want a snack, but gourmet they are not.

I ordered a fairly large quantity of this because my son is allergic to gluten and this type of cookies are hard to come by.  I wasn't sure how he'd take to these cookies but I thought I'd risk it anyway.I was pleasantly surprised to see that he was hooked after his first cookie.  Since that first cookie, I constantly hear "chocolate chip cookie, please?" at home.Good stuff.  Will be ordering more very soon.

column9: I HAVE TO REMEMBER I DIDNT BUY THEM FOR ME !!!
column10: Kinnikinnick Foods Gluten-Free Cookies, Montana's Chocolate Chip, 8-Ounce Bags (Pack of 6)  = These cookies are so good, that I have to keep reminding myself that I bought them for my son who is GF/CF, and for me to stop eating them!!!!  Great prices here too.

My spouse is Wheat free and eats a lot of GF food. Kinnikinnick brand ingeneral is great. The cookies are what a chocalate chip cookie shouldtaste like with out the downside of other GF brands. As another reviewer said,these don't have that wierd grainy texture that GF cookies usuallyhave.  They also don't taste like baking powder-another feature of many GFbaked goods.

I love these cookies! I've been GF for about 4 months now so I tend to be a little picky...But I really do love these cookies! They are so amazing! I would recommend these to anyone even if they didn't have Cealiac or a Wheat allergy.

My son is on the autism spectrum and has some sensory issues.  These are the only gluten-free chocolate chip cookies he'll eat.  They do not have that chalky feeling in your mouth that some GF foods have.
Once the package is opened, it's gone.  Hard and dunkable, tasty and GF, AND no hoarding necessary, there are more than enough cookies to share in this package.

column9: Kinnikinnick Gluten-Free Montana's Chocolate Chip Cookies
column10: This product was delivered in perfect condition.  Not one cookie was broken.  It also arrived in a very timely matter after I placed the order.  And these cookies are delicious!

they are VERY crumbly and fragile. They are more solid if you keep them in the freezer and eat them that way. Not your typical tough ginger snap texture at all, which could be a good thing.  At least half didn't survive amazon packaging and came smashed to bits.  Definitely worth trying, but maybe bought from a store, not from amazon.
I really enjoy these cookies. As a celiac with no tolerance for gluten in any form it is nice to finally find something that I truly enjoy (that doesn't taste like cardboard).
I did like these cookies but I didn't love them. They don't have a weird aftertaste or crumbly texture, but the flavor just wasn't perfect for me. I'm still looking for my "chips ahoy"!

column9: Low fat, high taste Ginger Snaps
column10: My son loves these cookies, so I buy them in bulk and store in the freezer. They have a great taste, are low in fat....something he needs with his Crohn's disease...and very tasty. I am so glad to have a cookie that is gluten free and yummy. They are a bit fragile compared to regular ginger snaps (that could be used to open locked doors!!), but any crumbled ones are good in parfaits with yogurt or pudding, or as pie crust.
These were delicious.. My daughter is allergic to wheat, so they were for her.  She had trouble getting enough for herself since everyone thought they tasted great.
Cookies look good, taste is almost non-existent. I vote for PAmela's Chocolate chunk cookies over these. Unfortunately, Pamela's cookies include only NINE in a package. Pricey.

I bought these for someone else on a gluten free diet.I have only good things to say aboutthese cookies. Personally i like these 'hard' type cookiesbetter than the soft ones. If the price were lower Imight buy them more often and give i them a 5 star rating.
My 10 year old son loves these!  Not as good as regular chocolate chip cookies, but great for gluten free!
Disappointment...these cookies have a stale taste unlike when I buy them from the Health Food Store.

I thought Prime Shipping was not just free but when they say it should get here in 2 days it should. Well my item was ordered on the 2nd and it shows still intransit till the 5th so call me crazy but that is 4 days not 2... hum! So have questions about Prime service! Yes! I did pick the right shipping option!

Dog food has changed ALOT over the past few years.  As pet owners were willing to spend more money feeding their pets, larger corporations bought out the smaller dog food companies and changed the ingredients without notifying the customers.  This was particularly true of the more expensive brands that contained the higher quality ingredients.  Real meat and rice were substituted with "meat by-product" and cheap imported grains (particularly CORN) that were determined to be "unfit for human consumption".  They are taking ingredients that used to be considered "waste" and packaging it up as "healthy & nutritious" food for your beloved pet. Our once healthy pets are contracting debilitating diseases and dying because of the toxic waste materials that are currently being marketed as pet food.Blue Buffalo is one of the few remaining companies that, at least to my knowledge, has not "sold-out" yet.  The food really is nutritious and still contains real meat with no by-products, fillers, corn or soy.  We switched our dogs over this past summer after having lost one to an autopsy/toxicology verified case of "aflatoxin poisoning" from the "healthy & nutritious" dog food we were buying and feeding him.  This was NOT cheap food folks.  This was a well-known brand, highly marketed as "Natural", that we were paying $60/bag for.  The FDA analysis of this food verified that it contained toxins, but NOTHING was done to the dog food manufacturer.  They are still producing their "high priced waste" and heavily marketing it as "natural".My advice to pet owners: Read the ingredients labels thoroughly and often!  Blue Buffalo a great product that you can still feed your pets with confidence.  Because it doesn't contain any cheap fillers, it's more satisfying to your dog so you don't need to feed as much of it thus making it still relatively economical. Don't wait until it's too late for your beloved pet.

Before switching to Blue Buffalo Wilderness Salmon, my boston terrier seemed to have negative reactions to everything he ate. His stools were consistently soft and he frequently broke out in rashes and would scratch and itch until he bled. We kept trying new brands of dry food hoping to find something that agreed with him. We were amazed how quickly things turned around when we started him on Blue Buffalo. His stools are finally normal and his skin has never looked better. His coat is even shiny! I'm so glad we found this product!

Our Bernese Mountain dog had always been on another highly rated food (Nature's Variety Prairie), but his stools were really soft and he was prone to diarrhea.  Our vet suggested finding another food with less fat and more fiber.  Although this food has similar fat content, it has double the fiber.  He has done amazing on this food since we switched.  His stools are normal now and he has so much more energy!  We have been really happy with this food.  It's expensive, but worth every penny.

column9: Know the ingredients of your dog's food!
column10: Blue Buffalo Wilderness Salmon might be a food some dogs do well on.  Mine did not.  It caused itching and loose stool, even after a very gradual switch.  I emailed BB customer service to see if they use wild/Pacific salmon or farmed/Atlantic (which is loaded with antibiotics and dyes--both of which could cause a reaction in animals with sensitivities) and they could not give me an answer.  I'm a fish snob from Alaska but aside from the wild vs. farmed prejudices, I was very concerned that they had no idea the source of their ingredients.This food gets a plus for the fact that it's grain-free.  I appreciate the direction this company is moving.  However, it is NOT a premium dog food in my mind.  Be cautious of any pet food company that doesn't know where their ingredients come from!

column9: AMAZING! FOOD! CAN'T HELP BUT SHARE WITH OTHER PET OWNERS!
column10: Ever since our 2 mini poodles and 2 Maltipoo came in to our household they stole our hearts and became a part of our family. The hunt for the right food came when I heard countless horror stories from friends and family on how leading brand name foods affected and even caused the death of their pets. We all know how costly vet bills can me and because of this reason I believe that being proactive and taking preventive care will be a lot cheaper in the long run. Certain grains and corn are not a natural part of a dogs diet and as you know most or all advertised brands use that as one of their main ingredients. What i love this brand is that it doesnt skimp on any of the right ingredients and makes meat/poultry/etc. (depending on the flavor you buy) the main ingredient! this is awesome because there really isnt any other brand out there that is true to their pet owners and their pets! This manufacturer makes me feel like they actually care and thus they will get my money for their 1 of a kind and amazing food! My dogs love it, they have beautiful coats, they are energetic and healthy all around. Been using this for about 3 years now and will continue to do so. This is our households choice of food- the right food.

I have a 2.5-year-old female boxer with terrible allergies. She scratches, rubs and bites herself raw. She is miserable and uncomfortable all the time and if you've had a dog with problems like this, you know how hard it is to watch her suffer like that. I've tried the vet's prescription formula dog food (at $60 for a 15 lb. bag, yikes!) and other limited ingredient diets, fatty acid supplements in her food, antihistamines, steroids (which have nasty side effects so she can't really take them anymore), plus medicated shampoos multiple times a week and antibiotics for the infections that develop in her scratching-induced wounds. Sure, there are moments of, "Hey, she's starting to look a little better," but none of it really seems to help. Other grain-free formulas showed some improvement in the first few weeks then fizzled and she was back to her mostly itchy self.The first time I have ever seen my dog without any scabs or big red gashes was three weeks after I started her on Blue Buffalo Wilderness (Salmon) with a small amount of a liquid Omega-3 supplement (Welactin) on top. The bald patches where she had scratched out her hair slowly began to grow back in and I found that I was not constantly telling her to stop scratching or biting herself. BIG IMPROVEMENTS! The environmental aspect of her allergies is now also successfully controlled with occasional prescription antihistamines.Some say this food is too expensive but in my opinion it is more than worth the cost. In fact, I am actually saving money compared to the cost of all the vet visits and medication that hardly even worked. My little girl will be on Blue Buffalo Wilderness from now on. I just bought a bag of the duck recipe so hopefully she likes the taste of that too.

I have nothing but great things to say about Blue Buffalo's products. I recently tried out the Wilderness brand (duck flavor). My black lab-mix loves it! As he's recently paralyzed, he sometimes has accidents in the house. Since his stool is solid and easy to pick up, clean up is a breeze. He even rolled over the pile in his wheelchair and none of it was ground into the carpet...just flattened a bit. Who knew stool could be so exciting?I definitely recommend Blue Buffalo's Wilderness brands.

column9: The best brand on the market
column10: We were feeding our dog Puppy Chow when we first got her. Until one day I wondered what exactly was in that dog food..one look at the label really threw me off completely. In my search for high quality dog food I found Blue Buffalo. Every since  the switch she has had an extremely glossy coat and endless energy as she actually uses more of the food. This in turn lead to her needing to poop less because there is nowhere near the amount of filler/junk that's in these name brand foods. We got a Pit Bull recently and we feed him Blue Wilderness and boy has it helped him pick up weight, yet he is very healthy and they both get nothing but compliments from the vet!

column9: Simply Amazing! My Siberian Huskies seem to think so too.
column10: I used to buy the brands you would find at Wal-Mart and the sort, but I thought to myself one day, "If I always spend a good amount of money on things for myself, why can't my dogs have the best food?" So I started researching the best dog food for Siberian Huskies, I read about how most of the super-market brands have grains instead of being natural. I came across a site that reviewed dog food, there I saw Blue Buffalo, my first time ordering this food was from Petco, online I paid $55 and then I bought it from the store and paid $65! Still not quite sure how that works, but I thought about how I always find everything for a better price on Amazon, and so I did.I must say when my dogs (Snowball & Shyko) were eating Beneful, Pedigree, and the sort, they would leave the food there and just not eat it. I was always wondering why they wouldn't eat it, but I realized after I bought this food that they love the natural stuff. Every time they see me simply reach for the bag, they get excited and start howling in excitement. They finish this food in record time, its kind of awkward to say the least, I wish Shyko would understand that your supposed to chew, haha. It makes me feel nice, knowing that my dogs love this food. The love for my dogs has no extent, and so they deserve the best dogs food there is, and this is it, for them atleast.

I have tried everything from Royal Canin to Solid Gold for my Queensland Heeler and all seem to be decent for his joints and overall health but he did some to scratch a bit on the Royal Canin and had extremely bad gas on the Solid Gold. Alas Blue Buffalo, we are on our 4th bag and he is loving it with no problems at all, attitude and mental awareness are as great as ever!!! Two Thumbs up!

Our toy fox terrier was developing one raw spot after another. I began thinking it was allergies. I must have been right because within 2 weeks on this food they were gone. They have not returned. This food is pricey but it is cheaper than vet visits and meds. Besides the price the only downside is the dogs smell a bit fishy. We affectionately call our dog Nemo when he emerges from under a blanket. No con outweighs the benefits.

I have a smaller beagle who has very bad food allergies. We have to watch him everywhere we take him that he is not eating anything or he will break out in rashes and scratch for days till he bleeds. For the past year and a half we tried different brands to help him with his allergies, He started on Nutro as a puppy and we switched him over to Natural Balance Venice and potato and didnt see any improvement. We finally decided to take him to the dermatologist and she suggested Royal Canine Rabbit and potato. Not only is that food not helping him either, its $70 a bag and my poor beagle has trouble chewing it. I finally came accross the Wilderness Salmon food, just after a week of him eating this brand he has no longer had long episodes of scratching and Ive noticed his little bald spots of where he has been scratching are no longer red. His stool is firm , and even a little fuller then before since he eats it up like a little pig. Even with the transition from mixing his old food with the new, he would take mouth fulls and drop them on the floor and only eat the blue wilderness nuggets. The size of the food is perfect for his little mouth as well. Only downfall is that he gets smelly breath. But that doesnt bother him at all. Im so glad he is a happy healthy little guy now, and its all thanks to Blue Wilderness.

When I met my last rescue pet, Dixie, approximately 8.5 years ago, she was a real mess--both externally and internally. She exhibited a nervous condition (G.E.R.D.) that my vet said was due to her previous horrendous living conditions; that is to say, that everything that went down her goozle promptly came right back up! She was painfully emaciated, skeletal almost, and her blood-work was all over the place. So, after a round of IV fluids and 2 small bags of 'Science Diet' chow, Dixie came home with me to recuperate and to learn how to live in a loving home. The first thing I did was to research which pet foods would address her particular condition; I knew that I didn't want to keep her on the 'Science Diet' regimen--it's too full of ingredients that I feel don't belong in a proper diet for dogs. Lo' and behold, I stumbled upon the "Blue Buffalo Wilderness" formula for dogs. It seemed like a good fit, due to all of the proper ratios (protein/fat) and totally "GRAIN-FREE". Viola! The rest, as they say, is history....8.5 years later, Dixie now weighs in at approximately 24 loving, happy pounds of my friendly and well-adjusted best friend.

We've been using this flavor of Wilderness for a few months now and our dog loves it.  He's an 18-month-old Olde English Bulldogge, so we end up going through quite a bit of food.  His coat is great, his energy is definitely up over previous high-quality foods.

I tried several different brands of dog food for my Alaskan Malamute mix, she would love one brand one day then refuse to eat it the next day. I finally decided to go down to my local healthy petstore and ask for help. The woman was very knowledgeable about huskies and malamutes and told me about Blue Buffalo and the Salmon flavor. What caught my attention the most is the wolf on the front and how it looked so similar to my dog. To this day this is the only food my dog will consistently eat, and I love the great ingredients inside.I also found that mixing a scoop or two of the Blue Buffalo Salmon flavored canned dog food with the dry food keeps my dog interested and looking forward to her meals.

column9: Great food for my dog's allergies
column10: My dog would consistently get itchy at various times of the year, especially in spring and fall.  We attributed her symptoms to seasonal changes in weather.  However, after I started giving her Blue Buffalo Wilderness Salmon dry dog food, her allergies basically disappeared.  This is a slightly more expensive dog food, but my dog will get this for the rest of her life.  It saved me a lot of money on vet bills and allergy prescriptions.Her dry fur grew long and silky.  Her energy level increased with this food.The ingredient list is impressive as well.  It has real protein.My dog would ordinarily turn away from dry dog food, but this particular bag has a lot of small flavor bits in it in between larger dry chunks.  It seems like the flavor bits are very appealing to my dog.Please make sure to give your dog water with this dog food.
Blue products are healthy and nutritious. My dogs love the food. Using grain free to help with dry skin and allergies.

I own a miniature poodle and she is in love with this food. However it is high in protein so you dog will need to eat less of this then the normal store bought food. It's best if your dog is really active too because if you feed your dog this food and s/he just sleeps all day your dog will gain weight. Overall I highly recommend this product. You truly do get what you pay for.

I recently added this food to the foods I rotate into my dogs' diet, and they absolutely love it.  Clean bowls all around.  High quality ingredients make me happy.  Protein level is higher than most foods, so if you need a lower level protein food, this may not be for you, or you will need to mix in another food.  If you are using a high-protein diet, then I highly recommend this food.The one drawback is price.  Per pound, it is the most expensive food I feed.  I rotate foods to add variety and keep interest in food, as my dogs seem to get bored with the same thing every day.  Despite the price, it is probably one of the most desired foods by my dogs, so at least the payoff is there.Shipping was surprisingly fast, free shipping was a great bonus.

column9: Good for my big guy but not his favorite flavor
column10: Blue Buffalo continually produces high quality foods for dogs and for my 75 lb Pittie, it is very important as he has several stomach and skin issues.  He does very well with the Wilderness variety but I will note that he is not as enthusiastic about the Salmon recipe as he is with the Duck recipe.  Overall, this is another solid food in my opinion and it always ensures his coat is shiny, and that he is in the best health, which at 12 years old is critical. I find that the prices on Amazon are always cheaper and with Prime Shipping I don't even have to lug it around so that is another plus.

column9: The search is over for my French Bulldogs!!
column10: I have two french bulldogs.  I have done absolutely everything to keep them healthy.  One is nearly 12 the other 3 years old.  My older dog was vomiting ALL the time and my younger one was chewing the pads of his feet apart and most recently, throwing up.  I've been buying them premium dog food their whole lives  or so i thought) and have added salmon oil and greens to their diet which did help with their coat and my older dog's hips/joints, but not their upset stomachs.  I know that Frenchies have a very sensitive system but this was getting ridiculous!My oldest daughter recently got french bulldog puppy and put her puppy on a completely raw diet of "Stella and Chewy's".  She swears by the frozen patties and wanted me to at least give it a try.  Well, given that I live far away from the nearest pet store that sells raw/frozen food, I decided to research different premium foods that would be similar to raw.  I came across Blue Buffalo Wilderness Grain Free Dry Dog Food, Salmon Recipe, 24-Pound Bag here on Amazon, and after reading the reviews decided to give it a try.  I wasn't sure because with the wolf on the cover I thought that maybe it was for larger breeds, but that's not the case AT ALL.After the past couple of months of having my Frenchies on this dog food ALL throwing up has ceased.  There has been zero incidences.  The pads of my youngest dog are healed up and he no longer needs to wear a cone around his neck to keep him from chewing at them.
