I have used this product for several years and it makes wonderful yogurt and has some of the most useful bacteria in it.  I make a batch then take a sample out and put it in the freezer to use for the next batch.  That way the box of starter packets last quite awhile.  I keep them in the freezer.  I only use a new packet if for some reason my sample becomes messed up and starts developing an off taste.  This rarely happens, but it has happened and then I have something to start over with.  Great product!  Healthy solution!
I have used this starter for decades with excellent, consistant results each time. All Yogourmet starters are much better than others I've tried, I won't use anything else!

I've tried others but I keep coming back to this one.  The price is the best overall and I seem to always be able to get it from Amazon quickly.I've been making yogurt for years now and I can't stand the stuff in the store.  Unfortunately, I never seem to be able to save the last couple tablespoons of the previous batch for the next!  This stuff is so inexpensive and convenient, I really don't mind anymore.  I use this for at least half the batches I make and the consistency of each batch is wonderful!  By far my favorite brand.

Priced right & easy to use!  I keep the boxes in the refrigerator.If you have a yogurt maker, making yogurt can't get much easier.  (You can make yogurt with out a yogurt maker too.  You can use a warm oven or warm pad, ect. & you need to maintain the correct temp.  You can reserch all of this on our wonderful informative interenet!) There are lots of different makers out there.  Check them out & get what suits you best!  The basic idea for making yogurt is to heat your milk until it just starts to climb the sides.  Then you let it cool to about 90 degrees or so.  You can put your finger in it & it's comfortable.  If you have skin on your milk, skim it off.  Add the yogurt starter to the milk & mix it in well.  Pour it in your yogurt maker jar/s & incubate it for 4 - 24 hours depending on your needs & desired tartness.  You can even add fruits, syrups before pouring in the milk/culture mix!  Just like "fruit on the bottom" in stores only way way better!  Anyway, instructions come with the yogurt starter so your covered!Make your own yogurt at home, it's cheaper & more satisfying!Good luck & have fun!

I was very impressed with this starter.1 It sets up in four hours2 it made a nice smooth yogurt3 each box makes six quarts, so this package of three boxes makes 18 quarts4 the packages are set up for quarts, the amount I useJust a hint for beginners, if your yogurt isn't as thick as you like, the original heating time is important. The longer you hold it at 180 degrees, the thicker your yogurt. I use a double boiler to keep mine from scorching.While I recommend the Yolife Yogurt Maker (YL-210) because you can use your own jars and vary the sizes, you can even make yogurt using your crockpot. Just google yogurt recipe crockpot.This is a super starter and works very well.

I love this product and have been using it for many years now. It makes a perfect yogurt every time. I use the Yogourmet incubator too - a gift from my mother when I got married 12 years ago. The gift that keeps on giving is always the best! I have tried all of the Yogourmet freeze dried starters with fantastic success. The Yogourmet Casei Bifidus Acidophilus Probiotic Yogurt Starter, is my favorite, found here on Amazon for a GREAT price. Due to the higher price though, I tend to use the original freeze dried starter the most. I give this company a 100% positive review. I have never had problems with any of their culture products or with the Yogourmet incubator machine.I use 2 quarts of milk with the recommended 10 grams of Yogourmet starter. I have found for myself, that the key to making great yogurt is to heat the milk to 185 degrees and continue cooking it at this temperature for 10 minutes. Cooking at this temperature kills any harmful bacteria in the milk that remains even after pasteurization. It also breaks down the proteins in the milk insuring a great yogurt SET. Apparently, the proteins are easier for your body to digest in this broken down state as well. Cool the 2 quarts of milk to 112 degrees, add starter, (10 grams freeze dried starter or 1/2 cup leftover yogurt from original batch) 1 1/2 cups optional powdered milk, up to 1 cup optional sugar and up to 1 tablespoon optional flavoring extracts. Incubate until desired tartness is reached. My kids prefer the maximum sugar so the yogurt tastes more like store bought. Although with this much sugar, the milk takes longer to turn into yogurt - closer to 8/9 hours rather than 4/6 hours. Try using honey extract, vanilla extract, raspberry extract, etc.

I make yogurt twice a week with yogourmet using the yogourmet multi. The family loves it. The timing I use is different than the instructions, it seems to need at least 8 hours to become thick enough. I also let it stand for 2 days in fridge. Afterward, I use hand mixer on low to give it a creamy texture. At that time I add stevia, liquid vanilla & or some type of berry. I jar it up in 8oz canning jars with reusable plastic lids. This way we always have serving size available, easy to grab and go. (I also use raw milk)

I recently bought the Yogourmet yogurt maker along with this starter.  I had never previously made yogurt, so I thought it would be best if I used a starter instead of trying plain yogurt for the cultures.  It turned out perfectly for me.  The directions are simple, and the product does what it should - produces delicious yogurt.

I've been using this yogurt starter every week for over a year and get perfect yogurt every time. I've used skim, 1%, and whole milk and I always add half a cup of powdered milk when it is heating. column9: THIS is the culture recommended for the SCD diet.
column10: I use and enjoy this all the time. I strain out all the whey and waterafter incubation and get a v-e-r-y thick yogurt after draining.How thick you ask?  Well thick enough to support a chief's knife standing upright.The taste is great!  Just the right amount of tart -- how real yogurt issupposed to taste without the post incubation sweeteners added to most commercial yogurts found in supermarkets.THIS is the SCD recommended culture because it contains three, and only three cultures:  -- L.bulgaricus  -- S.themophilus  -- L.acidophilusSpecifically, it does NOT contain Bifidobacterium (frequently shortened to Bifidus) which is considered anathema to the SCD diet.Nor does this culture contain any "other", "unknown" or "miscellaneous additional" bacteria which are frequently listed under "Ingredients:" on commercial yogurt containers.  Yogourmet cultures are produced by Lyo-San, Inc. in Canada.  Lyo-San <lyosan.ca> specializes in growing pure cultures as well as mixing & packaging their freeze dried cultures in precise amounts.[Lo-San does, however, offer a variety of other culture combinations which DO CONTAIN Bifidus.  Those packages containing Bifidus DO NOT have a cover graphic depicting a bowl of yogurt with SIX Strawberries.]
This product went out of code in 2008.  Do not buy.  Amazon was more than fair and refunded all of my money.  I am very pleased with Amazon but will not buy this one again.

column9: Easy!!! if you have a gas oven
column10: If your gas oven is warm inside, you can make yogurt extremely easy.1. Pre-warm a gallon of milk to room temperature in its original bottle with water bath2. Pour some milk into a clean cup, stir to dissolve one bag of dried starter, pour back3. Similar to step 2, dissolve sugar/splendar/vanilla extract and pour back4. Cap the milk bottle, shake to mix, throw into the oven and enjoy yummy yogurt next morningNote:1. You can add sugar after step 4 if you don't care about the thickness of your product2. You only need 1 bag of this starter for a full gallon3. Keep your product in fridge -- it becomes thicker in cold and taste better

This is less a review of Yogourmet's freeze dried starter and more of a clarification of the value.  I mean, how much is there to say about a starter? It either works or it doesn't.When I ordered my Yogourmet yogurt maker, it came with a box of the freeze dried starter.  The box contained 3 double packets of yogurt.  A single packet will do the job for a quart of yogurt, and a double packet is needed if you are doing a full two quart batch.  Long story, short: I thought I was just purchasing a box of 3 double packets when I read the description (Pack of 3).  That seemed a little pricey at $12.  It turns out that that this item is actually 3 BOXES of starter (each with 3 double packets).I just wanted to clarify that in case you skimmed through the product description too quickly, like I did.Happy yogurt making!

I can't tolerate milk(unfortunately), so I make soy yogurt. I love this starter because it's just so easy to use, and the flavor is full and tart.Personally, I like my yogurts sour enough to bring tears to my eyes, so I incubate my yogurts a good ten hours, sometimes twelve.  My only suggestion for making soy yogurts is that you might want to add a teaspoon of maple or agave syrup to your soymilk to give your culture something to munch on.  Soy milk is not the same as milk, remember.I don't have an electric warmer; instead, I use a "Yogotherm". Basically, it's a two-quart plastic bucket and lid that you pop into a styrofoam holder to maintain the temperature. A great $20 find if you don't have the patience for washing out tiny cups.

I'm new to making my own yogurt, and I'd heard people discuss the two main methods (add a prepackaged starter, or add another yogurt to start).  I did my own scientific test to see which one tasted better to me.I found that using this starter gave the yougurt a little bit more of the tangy taste that many people like.  It worked well, and the set up was firmer at 24 hours than the yogurt-started yogurt.It worked well, and so far I've had consistant results.  Directions are easy to follow, and pouches are easy to open.  Outer box is recycleable.

I've used a few different brands of starters and I like this one the best.  It not only gives a good tasting, thick yogurt, I can use a few spoonfuls of the yogurt as the next starter.  Not every brand re-uses as easily to start the next batch.  I generally buy starter every Spring.  I'm on the 3ed 'generation' right now and the yogurt is the same on the 3ed generation as the first.  It will be interesting to see how many generations I can get out of one starter.

Product produces an acceptable yogurt.Flavor is non-descript.Yogurt becomes more sour the longer it is retained in the yogurt maker.Overnight production creates a very sour yogurt.A more flavorful yogurt can be produced using other European cultures.

You can't beat the consistency and convenience.  Making yogurt was such a chore in the beginning with the pasteurization, the mixing of the starter batch etc.  I have refined the process to where it takes just a couple quick steps.  Scald a quart of milk in a measuring cup in the microwave for exactly 8 minutes, let it cool in a sink full of cold water, add one of the packages of Yogourmet, mix it with an electric mixer for a couple minutes, pour in yogurt maker (I use 8 oz glasses in mine)and you're done.  Very little mess to clean up.  Get very consistent results and a delicious, tart yogurt every time.  I make a fresh batch every morning in minutes.  Recommend the product highly.

I'm very happy with this product. All the yogurt I've made with it has turned out great, with a nice tang-y flavor. I use it about every 3rd or 4th time I make yogurt, in between I use a small bit from the previous batch as starter to be more economical.

I'm an experienced yogurt maker and thought I would give this a try. I've made three batches with it thus far and each has been runny. I use the heating pad method, always ensure I don't disturb the milk after incorporating the culture, etc. It's the same method I've always used to great results - except with the Yogurmet starter. At best, it was an expensive trial with disappointing results. I won't be buying again.If anyone reading this has suggestions for a good freeze-dried starter, please leave a comment. While Stonyfield works great, I don't always make yogurt batches back to back and having to go buy some to make some seems to defeat the purpose somewhat. Ideally, I'd like to have a freeze-dried starter on hand at all times, which I was hoping the Yogurmet would provide. Unfortunately, all it seems capable of turning out is yogurt for use in smoothies. And yes, I know I could strain it through a cheescloth/towel or add dried milk powder to firm it up, but I've never had to do that when using other starters. Unfortunately, the fall-back brand of starter I used in the past is no longer available so I'm trying to find a new one.Your suggestions for alternatives will be greatly appreciated.
I did not use this personally but ordered this for my wife and she liked the product! I guess this must be good
This is the BEST way to make yogurt!  I love it, and would not make yogurt any other way.  As for the Yogourmet brand, it is my favorite.  I LOVE it!
I've always used this product and think it works great.  Four hours is all it takes for 1 quart of yogurt.

This is the only yogurt culture I will ever use! It makes perfect fat free yogurt consistently every time. I follow the package directions exactly (2 packets of culture added to heated, then cooled milk). The only changes I found I need to make is that I add the nonfat dry milk powder and 1 packet of Knox gelatin after the milk heats to 81 degrees Celsius. I make 1 1/2 gallons of yogurt with this culture every week and it has never failed.

This starter makes excellent yogurt.  I have never had a bad batch since I ordered this brand.  I use organic milk, so I save money.  I get two batches out of one package.  I just save 1/2 cup of the finished yogurt for the next batch. Saves money and you know exactly what's in your yogurt.

This product is good. I had been using it for years, and consistently produced excellent yogurt.This is the first time I purchased from Amazon, but actually a little more expensive than local WholeFood store, also I can just purchase 1 pack of it at local store, instead of 3 pack. Thus, I would purchase it from my local store next time.

This is really a great yogurt starter. You get perfect results every time...yogurt is so easy to make! I use a Salton Yogurt maker: mix the starter to the milk at the right temperature and place it n the yogurt maker for 4-6 hours. After that in the fridge for a few hours and my yogurt is ready! Also the taste is excellent. You get 6 packages in each box, for a total of 18 individual ones. The price is good, comparable to what you pay in the store, with the convenience of receiving it right to your door.
This product makes very good yogurt. I have been buying yogourmet products a while now and I have been very happy with it.
A very good tasting yogurt starter at a good price, that can be made without using any sugar.  Easy to use in conjunction with an electric yogurt maker.

I really like this starter. It's a little spendy, but we get much more consistent results than when we use the previous batch of yogurt as starter.Hanging the yogurt in cheesecloth for a few hours makes an incredibly thick, creamy yogurt, a lot like Greek yogurt.We use fresh goat's milk, and oh boy! Do we love our yogurt!

Makes the best yogurt.  Smooth, tasty, and really, really good with berries.  Also, nourishes the bacteria in your intestines, which makes it a very healthy food.  Try it in a smoothy instead of milk.

I found this product in a Canadian Grocery a number of years ago and when I went back a couple of months later couldn't find it again. I use this all the time now, that's why I bought so many. The flavour is great and it works every time. I even bought some for my trainer to use at home instead of always taking Yogurt I made.
I use this starter to make homemade yogurt. Great flavor profile and easy to use with good instructions.  I do not use the the yogourmet equipment to make the yogurt. I only use this as a starter.

This product makes yogurt making a no brainer.  Added benefits - no more non-recyclable containers and I know what is in my yogurt, and how fresh it is.  This starter dissolves easily, has clear instructions and good packaging.

Yogourmet is a terrific product!  It produces no-fail yogurt every time. It dissolves quickly, makes yogurt with a good taste and texture.  Before using this product I was using the end of the previous batch as a starter and had a few less than desirable results. With Yogourmet,there's never a problem. I don't use a "yogurt maker", just a couple of canning jars and an insulated cooler.  This product makes the whole process simple.  I'm very happy with it.
This worked great in my Yogourmet yogurt maker.  I would buy it again.  It is the approved SC Diet culture.  My yogurt came out very thick and creamy.

We use this to make homemade yogurt in our Yogurt Maker and it has given use excellent results every time.It dissolves easily in tepid milk and leaves no clumps, we are very happy with it.I even made yogurt cheese out of our yogurt, it was wonderful!I bought both this type and the Yogourmet Casei Bifidus Acidophilus Probiotic Yogurt Starter, 6-Count Boxes (Pack of 2) so giving the same review for both.
Easy to use. Makes good yogurt. If you got runny yogurt, you probably need to adjust the cultivation time. Recommended for yogurt lovers!

I tried using Dannon yogurt as my starter but the yogurt was too thin.  I decided to give this a try, and because of my first failed attempt with the Dannon starter, I used 1 cup of cream to 3 cups of milk to see if it would help it to become thicker.  My yogurt is perfect now after only 4 hrs in my yogurt maker.  I then use 1/2 cup yogurt from my jar to make the next batch.  Works like a charm.
this product is very good and I was glad to see a sale as I make my yogurt fresh every week.

I have been useing this brand and making my yogurt for about 3 mths I guess. We love the fact u can add your own items to suite your taste buds for that day. The #1 favorite is making smothies( out of this world). I do not know the screen name, but there is one reviewer that gives a lot of great tips that work very well. So take your time to read some of the longer reviews and u just might get some great hints. One I did try and worked just fine was using one side of the package for every 2 qts. So if you make 4 qts, just take out one envolope and cut both sides open and mix, u get the same thickness and great taste as if u used 1 per qt like the directions say too. So that means I get 2 times as much yogurt, then I would if I go by the directions. I even have a little yogurt fan, I make him about 2 qts every 2 weeks, and he loves it ( he is 5), him and his mommy enjoy making smothies also. When he started getting low he will come and ask me to make him more. So even kids love it. I use whole milk, heat it to 180F ( hold it at 180 for about 10min), then let it cool to about 105, mix the cultures in and then place in the qt jars. I turn my oven on for a short min or less at 350 ( place my candy temp gage to make sure it is at 105 to 110), turn the oven light on, and set the jars in ( put them more in the back), at one hr I turn the oven back on 350 for less then 40sec,( test your oven to see how fast it heats up, every oven is different, so yours may get a lot hotter faster then mine) check to make sure the temp is still good (105 to 110). I may do it one or two more times if I remember to. I find this makes my yogurt thicker, then if I do not do a quick reheat. But make sure u do not get the temp to high or u will kill your culture. Mine set in about 4 hours, but we like a little more sour taste so I leave it 6 to 8 hours. Then put it in the refrig, and eat up the next morning. There is so many ways u can rest your yogurt, just find one that works for u, the oven just happens to work for me. YouTube is another place to get hints.

column9: Have used this brand for a dozen or more years..here is why
column10: Have been making our homemade yogurt for decades and the reason I use this starter is even though I remove 1/4 cup of the batch I have made for the next batch, after a few months its good to have a fresh culture starter.  So every 3-4 months after having made literally gallons of homemade yogurt I will open one of the sealed packets of starter culture and start a new fresh batch of yogurt.  But we make a gallon of yogurt per week, because we eat yogurt with a half teaspoon of cinnamon in the morning, and make yogurt cheese for both cheesecake and for mixing with herbs for our own yogurt cream cheese with crackers or on bagels.If you eat little yogurt you could simply buy a small cup of store bought plain yogurt and use that for starter, but you also have to make sure the store bought stuff has no milk from cows that have received hormones or antibiotics. Something we avoid by only using organic raw milk.

column9: It did not work for me at all...
column10: I've been making yogurt for a few months with much success. So I am not new to this...I normally make yogurt with a previous batch, but I came across this product and saw the awesome reviews. I thought I could perhaps get better results with this starter, so I purchased two boxes. I followed the direction to heat the milk up to 180F and cooled it to 73-77F. I thought cooling the milk to 73-77F was strange as I've always cooled it to about 105F before adding previous bacteria culture into warmed milk. Most of the recipes I have seen online required the milk to cool to 105F as well, so I was a little bit confused. But then I thought the Yogourmet culture was special and therefore has a different temperature requirement.Well, I have an awesome thermos that always keeps the temperature for a prolonged period. I put the milk with Yogourmet mixture at 75F and set it aside for 14 hours (instruction said between 12-15 hours). As soon as I woke up in the morning, I excitedly opened my thermos. I discovered nothing but milk. There was no whey, firmed yogurt, nothing. It was literally how I left it.It seems like I am the only person who has had no luck with this culture. I am sure this company is great and the culture works normally as I can see from the previous reviews. I might have gotten a bad culture pack because it really did nothing for me. I am definitely not a beginner so I know I didn't make any mistakes in following the direction. I will email the company and see what can be done.
I found a box in my mom's freezer. It expired 12 years ago. We tried it with our Koolatron TCYM-07 Yogurt Maker and it worked flawlessly.
I have been using Yogourmet for over 40 years and I can't find anything that can beat it????? This a quality product???
My order of Yogourmet arrived promptly and was nice and fresh--not what often happens with food products ordered online.

I've tried about 6 batches using this starter, and it's just not working for me.  After 10, 14, 18 hours (!) still just slightly thickened milk!  I've followed the instructions to a T, and I have an electric yogurt maker, so I know (assume) the temperature is correct, as I've had great success using store-bought yogurt as starter (which I felt kind of canceled out the benefits of homemade), but I just can't get a batch of thick, rich, yummy yogurt from this product.  Must be me, since everyone else thinks it's great, but I'm at a loss as to understand my lack of success.

I found the flavor to be too tart. My family did not care at all for the flavor. To get the thickness I wanted I had to incubate for 17 hours then strain. However when I tried using some 'store-bought' yougurt as a starter ( 1 cup) plus 1 cup powdered milk. The desired thickness was achieved in 8 hours and the flavor was delightful! lick off the spoon mellow. So I am going to experiment with this culture to see if I can achieve the results I want without having to incubate for 17 hours. Any ideas from anyone? -MTF Aurora CO.

Wish I had seen that the ingredients included cow's milk...trying to find something that is milk free.  Don't know if this product works as designed with cow's milk, but doesn't do so good with goat's milk following the modified directions for the Yogourmet Yogurt Maker.

No need to use this expensive starter. You can mix one yogurt (nature and not a 0% please)with one liter of whole milk mixed with half a yogurt container of dried milk which will create a thicker yogurt. I always keep one yogurt I made to make my new batch. Enjoy!

This is just nuts from an economic perspective.This starter costs $12.61 (if you assume free shipping), and this is good for three batches of 2 liters each.  That works out to $4.20 per batch.  The milk for this costs about $4.00 a half gallon for organic milk.  So now you're up to $8.20 per batch.  But you also should add some non-fat dry milk, about 1/3 cup per batch, adding about another $2.00 (for organic).  So the 2 liters (or 1/2 gallon) of yogurt is now up to $10.20, and this doesn't include the amortized cost of a yogurt maker, if you're using one, or the electricity cost.Or instead, you can buy very high quality Nancy's organic yogurt in a great reusable container for under $7.00 for a half gallon and not have to do any work at all.It's up to you.

column9: If you LOVE Chicken wing meat...
column10: UPDATE June 2009: They changed the recipe so these are now more tender (good thing), but they got rid of the slight tangy vinegar flavor. Now they don't taste like chicken wings; just spicy chicken jerky. I will probably buy these about once a year now, instead of 1-2 times per month. Back to the Jalapeno jerky, when I can find it!ORIGINAL REVIEW from 11/29/08: I don't eat chicken wings that often any more (90 fat calories per wing, being deep fried and dipped in butter). And I LOVE chicken wings! But if the flavor you crave is that hot sauce & vinegar comingling with a large chunk of tender chicken, then give these a try. If you're looking for the butter, crispy or chewy skin, and deep fried flavor components, then you won't have those here. I don't buy beef jerky anymore (which is also a favorite), I buy these! I just wish they weren't so hard to find locally. Circle K and Walgreens are the only retail locations I know of. Eat 1 bag, and you'll be addicted or nonplussed. There's not really a middle road.

I DO NOT EVEN CARE IF THIS IS OVERPRICED, THESE ARE ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS. THERE'S NOT A TON OF MEAT IN EACH PACKAGE, BUT IT HITS THE SPOT. GOOD LORD, THESE TASTE SO DELICIOUS, I DO NOT EVEN KNOW WHAT MORE TO SAY.
Best one yet.If you have not tried this one yet your missing out very tender and moist nuggets.The only negative is the 3.25 size bag is much to small.

I bought these to share with the office and the disappeared almost instantly.  They are very good and contain enough protein to keep people going while suppressing that "snacky" feeling.  These are a great snack to carry with you as they are very light (for example, on a flight or road trip).  I highly recommend that you try a few of the other flavors as well.  They have this snack in Chicken, Turkey and Beef in various flavors.

I am an avid consumer of Jack Links Beef Steak Nuggets.  This batch is stale, dry and almost tasteless.  I can purchase these in even remote gas stations and they taste juicy and wonderful. I am too lazy to return them but will never buy them over the internet again.

I can't give these a 5 because the ingredients show they are very processed.  I'm not sure how healthy they are.But the taste is great - very hot  - like about a nuclear on the Zaxby's scale.  If you like hot wings, you'll like these.  Be prepared to not be able to leave them alone.  When my husband buys a bag, we sit there and eat them until they are gone.  Also, have something to drink handy!

I was expected a lot better. i LOVE the beef jerkey nuggets they are so juicy n flavorful and delicious, but when i ordered these just to try them cause i couldnt find them in any store i wasnt too happy. when i tried them they were extremely greasy and not that much flavor.

column9: dry meat and short expiration date
column10: Ordered OVEN ROASTED TURKEY NUGGETS*** for the first time. Meat is dry. Expiration date is too close; received today, SEPT 9, 2011, expiring NOV 21, 2011.In the past, have had very good experience with the Chicken Teriyaki nuggets. Jack Link's used to use dark meat. Jack Link's changed the recipe to white meat and the nuggets do not taste as rich any more.*** Very disappointed with Amazon's approach on linking ALL Jack Link's nuggets together. Meaning: If you post a review for the Chicken Teriyaki ones, you can NOT post one for the flaming chicken, turkey over roasted, etc.?! And the same review will show up under any and all of them. I contacted Amazon and customer service first tried to convince me I was doing something wrong. On the third e-mail, the senior CS guru indicated the nugget products are all linked together and nothing will be done about the issue.

These are the typical red bags of premium beef-jerky you see at the store, only...you get FOUR of them! These four bags of delicious, mouth-watering beef nuggets are a tasty and healthy snack, and I don't feel bad about eating a whole bag throughout the day at my desk.I love all of the varieties Jack Link's has to offer. I've been a die-hard Teriyaki fan myself, so I'm hesitant to sway away from my typical "go-to" bag.If you're looking for a satisfying feel-good snack to take on road trips, sporting events, at your desk, or what-have-you ' you do NOT want to pass this up.

These are pretty good, but a little overpriced - I would only buy if there was a promotion. Some pieces are deliciously tender and seasoned perfectly, but there usually are more that are too dried out and tough, or overseasoned.

column9: Great for snacking or for a small meal!!!
column10: These are great!  They are spicy, but not too spicy.  They taste just like Buffalo Hot Wings but without the bones. I agree with another reviewer who is thinking about microwaving these as I bet these would taste even better warmed up!  I bought an 8 pack of these and keep these at my job for when I get the munchies and want some quick protein and the calories for one bag is only about 280 so that is perfect for a snack or to ward away the hunger pangs.  These would be great for someone doing a low-carb diet or someone who just wants extra protein for their body.  One bag also has just over 30 grams of protein and this tastes so much better than eating just a protein bar.  Bottom line is this... if you love hot wings and can't get enough give these a try.  You won't be disappointed.

I just tried these recently and I can't get enough of them now.  They don't have the texture of buffalo chicken wings, it's more like the stuff you get when you order a buffalo chicken pizza...just chunks of plain old chicken smothered in hot sauce.  Haven't tried it yet, but they seem like they'd be REALLY good warmed up or tossed on a pizza before it goes into the oven.They seem to be a bit more expensive than other Jack Link stuff, but so worth it.  Om nom nom nom nom

column9: Disgustingly salty, in a dog treat shape
column10: I wanted to get some jerky and since I like buffalo wings I tried these. The problem is there is way too much salt, it's disgustingly salty, way more than normal jerky. I can barely eat it. If you eat a 3.25 oz package of these you will have eaten 1840mg of sodium, instant high blood pressure.

I was a bit apprehensive ordering these from Amazon because I had read in other reviews that some of the jerky were moldy. I am happy to say that mine were absolutely mold-free! My family vanquished 2 packets on the spot LOL...
Absolutely love these steak nuggets! Everywhere around here they go for over 8 dollars, so I was thrilled when I found out I could buy these on here. Very tender and the spices are amazing.

Little morsels of moist, pure beef that taste like high quality roast.  I got the Teriyaki by accident - I normally don't like teriyaki ANYTHING - but the only hint of added flavoring on these is a little sweetness.Lean, good cuts of meat with no nasty little gristley surprises.  My only criticism is they must cook these in crack cocaine, because I'm absolutely addicted to them.
I love the steak nuggets (and tenders) even better than their regular jerky.  I swear by all three of the Original, Peppered and Teriyaki Beef flavors.

I'm a big fan of Buffalo chicken and beef jerky, so I thought I'd love the Jack Link's Flamin Buffalo Chicken Nuggets.  I was wrong.  I bought the Steak Nuggets as well, which aren't as good as Jack Link's jerky, but definitely tasted better than the Buffalo Chicken Nuggets.To put it bluntly, they tasted like an old chunk of salty chicken with a slight Buffalo flavor.  They're not very spicy, I was expecting more of a kick.  They also smelled a little funny.  I'd give Buffalo chicken jerky a try, but I won't be buying these ever again. They're OK, but there's so many better options out there.

column9: Jack Links  Teryiaki Beef Steak Nuggets
column10: The beef nuggets are soft and easy on the teeth and tasty. If they are slightly less salty, they will be excellent.Very good snack.Johnson
These were good, but I really couldn't taste the A1 in them.  Tasted similar to the original steak nuggets to me

I would like to say that I have never tried a flavor of jerky that I didn't like...  that was true until a few days ago.  I wanted to try something different and decided to stray from my usual peppered beef.  This was a mistake, I have to say this is the worst jerky/nuggets/meat product I have ever tried.  From the smell to the taste, just not good.  If you really want to give this stuff a whirl, I suggest you find a single pack.  Don't buy 4 of them like I did.  One final note:  taste is subjective, you may really love this stuff, I just didn't.

I find that the buffalo chicken jerky is great for when I'm craving buffalo wings late at night. Sure they're not the saucy goodness of wings at a bar but they definitely replicate the flavor. They are very hot but delicious.

I normally have beef jerkey with my lunch for some easy to transport protein. I decided to give these a try, bought them at the grocery store and they were great. Easy to measure and a lot less stringy than normal beef jerkey.I ended up saving a ton of money using amazons subscribe and save over using the grocery store. Definitely something I'll reorder.
I really like the product.  It was super easy to order online and have it delivered.  Much cheaper than buying in a gas station.  Stocking up is good for long drives, too.

These taste amazing! Best jerky I've ever had. They are kind of expensive, but once in a while Amazon will lower the price slightly and hopefully that happens when they are offering a 10% off Jack Link's products promo code. Anyone who likes jerky or is simply looking for a convenient high protein snack should give these a try.
The bite size chewables are wonderful - 2 or 3 every few hours lets yu diet and never feel hungry.
I purchased these to snack on after my workouts. Now I find myself just snacking on them all the time!! They're really good and come in a variety of flavors.
These are strangely addictive - and a good sugarless snack.  I like this flavor and the original, but the pepper is really strong.  Enjoy!

column9: Love it!  But huge on sodium though.
column10: Flamin' Buffalo Chick + A1 are my all time favorites. The meat is tender, and the taste (based on the ones I've bought) are extreme with flavor. The only problem with jerky is the salt, and these have a ton of it. I wouldn't consume more then one bag a day, but it's your choice and body. I'll definitely be buying more in the future though, because these are delicious.

These are a great go-to snack/meal when you're in a rush and don't want chips or hotdogs.The nuggets are about the size of a stack of three quarters with some smaller ones the size of a couple of nickels.The flavor is spicy with a nice tang.The texture is softer than jerky but not as soft as say summer sausage.Quick comment on quantity - there are three servings, 60 calories each, in the package.  This ends up being a little over a handful for the entire package.Great to have on hand for those on the go times.

This is a nice tasty option that's totally different from jerky.  Convenient on the go just like jerky.  I would have given it five stars if not for the fact that it's quite salty, and that detracts from the flavor.
This is very good just a little too much of the A-1 flavor for us. Next time will order another flavor. If you really  love A-1 you will be pleased with it.

I thought this would be spicy, and coming from someone who eats spicy food all the time and fire sauce on his burritos, this is really only mild. This does not make your nose run, or make your throat burn, ears tingle, which is the funnest part of eating spicy food. Spicy food containing cayenne pepper is very healthy for you and is great for colds and sore throats. With a name like Flaming Buffalo with fire coming out of the name I had high hopes...and sadly this does not live up to the hype in the heat department. It still tastes good. The flavor lingers in your mouth making you reach for another one, after 6-8 pieces or so you get a salty taste that makes you reach for water. I give this 3 stars for taste and convenience. Just in case you don't eat it all in one sitting, the bag contains a zip-lock storage to keep things sealed. It will last 3 days after opening without refrigeration.

They are tasty, well flavored, always premium cuts, nothing tasted substandard.  On top of that high protein and low calorie! Only problem - everybody else thinks the same thing and its hard for Jack Links to keep them in stock.  You may have to wait a few extra days for the specialty orders.

I love this product! Tasty and soft (but not too soft). Very good flavor and it's safe to say, I can't "eat just one!" If you like the jerky, but not the dried up, tough stuff...you might want to give this stuff a try!
These are nice tender jerky nuggets, more tender than the usual beef jerky.  Flavor is very good, great for energy on hiking trips.

I'm a 58 year old grandma, and I can say without any reservations that this is the BEST canned tuna I've ever had -- including the home-canned tuna my grandmother used to make when I was a child.  Yes, it's expensive, but I guarantee you will be able to tell the difference, and the difference is worth the price to me.  This product is sometimes found in health food stores, but they are really just starting to expand their distribution, and you may not be able to find it locally just yet.If you want a can of tuna that comes with just Tuna (no phosphates or hydrogenated anything), salt (low sodium) and water, try it.  If you like it, take one of the boxes to your local health food other other local market and ask them to carry it.  Help this company expand, and then we'll all be able to find it on our grocery store shelves -- maybe even at a better price.  In the meantime, I'm putting in my free shipping order today!

I bought some of this tuna on clearance from my local Food Lion for about a dollar a can.  I had never had tuna like this before.  It is like eating a filet of tuna.  I pair it with Glutino crackers and it is divine.  If you can afford the price, it is well worth it.  I feel better about eating tuna that is randomly tested for mercury and PCB's and I like that it is caught responsibly and that some proceeds will go to help sea turtle preservation.  This is the kind of company I like to support if I can afford it!

column9: Not the tuna it used to be!
column10: Have used this product for years, since my first purchase. Have regularly received this product through Subscribe & Save for a couple years. The last 3 deliveries showed me a product no longer a solid, desireable piece of fish but a pressed-together lump of mixed light and dark tuna. Does it taste okay? Yes. Is this sashimi quality gourmet canned tuna? I think not. Cancelling regular delivery.

This is the best tuna I've ever eaten.  No water or oil added, it is all tuna.  The meat is solid, no little chunks floating around in water, and very little natural oil.  The five ounce can gives you five full ounces of tuna, completely usable.  It is worth the money to buy such a quality product.

column9: As good as albacore tuna gets
column10: If you like albacore tuna in natural juices, that is, without olive oil and added water, this is superlative food.  When comparing prices note that different size cans are sold.  The cans are generally well packed without too much space.  After consuming one-hundred portions, I have never been disappointed with taste, texture, appearance, or value, meaning the amount actually in the can.  It is fillet, not chunks.  Tuna is wonderfully healthful, though not equal to salmon in that respect.  If one eats from the can/jar, as I do, the only equivalent for taste may be imported Yellowfin Tonnino in olive oil.

column9: Used to Be Awesome, Still Pretty Good
column10: I started buying Henry and Lisa's Tuna about a year ago and it was excellent. It was seriously a solid tuna loin in a can that had no fishy smell- you can't beat that. Unfortunately it's gotten progressively less quality with each shipment. At first there was some less quality filler tuna around the edges, and now it seems the cans more frequently only contain the less quality meat. Some of the glowing reviews here are from about a year ago and in my experience the product has changed since then.It is still better than most other brands that I have tried and it's the only tuna I can eat without having to hide the smell and taste with tons of condiments. The extra cost of the tuna is partially offset by what I save in condiments. I'm giving it 4 stars for the BPA -free can, dolphin safe, and that it's still comparatively good tuna.

column9: Must have for our outdoor trips!
column10: I first discovered this brand 4 yrs ago at Wholefoods when preparing for a trip to a national park. I bought this one and another one among the highest priced caned fish, and compared them side by side, this one won hands down.What I like:- It is very tasty, and canned in its own juice instead of spring water that most of other brands use.- It has a loop which you can pull the can open. This is an indispensable feature for my outdoor activities. Again, most of the other caned ones don't have.Since I discovered this product and its salmon version (which is also delicious), they become my lunch staple together with some tomatoes and apples, whenever we go out on a whole day biking, hiking or xc skiing trip.

column9: Excellent - but Wild Planet is equivalent---in every way---at half the price.
column10: This Henry & Lisa's albacore tuna is excellent - but Wild Planet albacore is just as excellent (or better) at less than half the price.  (Try them both and see for yourself!)  So even though the quality is equivalent--- including five to six times the omega threes, sustainable pole caught, and very low mercury as a result of handpicking smaller (younger) albacore --- I rate this tuna down a star for being way overpriced.
I was off tuna for a while until a friend made me try this product.  I'll never eat tuna from any other resource (including fresh) again.  I LOVE this product and you will too.

I have been eating "tuna fish" from cans from the time I was a little kid (I didn't even know it was called "tuna" I thought it was something called "tuna fish").  First packed in oil (heavy and gross) then packed in water (much lighter, less taste and texture).  I would squish the top of the can in until the tuna was dry as a bone, then  load it up with mayo and a little lemon.  After years of doing this I got the "recipe" pretty much down and I've enjoyed my occasional tuna sandwiches for years.  Henry & Lisa's is so different it bears almost no resemblance to tuna as I knew it.  It is so fresh tasting and flavorful it's amazing and hard to describe.  The texture and moistness, even with very little (or even no) mayo is unlike any tuna I've tasted.  It's packed, as I understand it, in the natural oils that are released when it is cooked.  It is not a lot of oil, certainly far less than in conventional tuna.  At first I drained the oil out, like I did with "regular" tuna, now I leave all or most of it in and mix in a little bit of mayo and lemon and it comes out just perfect.  This natural oil is extremely healthy and high in omega 3 fatty acids.  In a pinch, this could be a perfect snack with nothing added, straight out of the can.  Just crush it up and mix it with it's own oil in the can and you have a self contained instant healthy snack.  I prefer to mix in the two ingredients in to make it just the way I like it.I was so impressed with this tuna I decided I'd try and duplicate it with expensive fresh tuna bought at a fancy upscale supermarket. To make a long story short, I was totally unsuccessful.  Apparently the process is not easy to duplicate in your kitchen.I would encourage you to buy three cans and see what you think.  If you like tuna, you will simply be amazed at how good this is.  I am on the once every two month plan where they send me three cans every other month.  I'm thinking of moving up to once a month.  Three a month is just not enough!  This plan helps you to save a few more dollars and it comes out to a little over $5.50 a can.  Expensive, to be sure but entirely worth it!
We're non-red-meat people. Tuna is our primary fish preference, and Henry & Lisa's is the best we've found. It is not easy on the pocketbook, but for special occasions, you do get what you pay for.

I love this tuna.  It has an excellent flavor especially when compared to some of the options available at the grocery store. I have done some cursory checking and this appears to be the most expensive canned tuna I can find.

I love this Tuna! I used to buy it at several stores but a lot of them stopped carrying it. This tuna is so full of Omega 3 Fatty Acids it is crazy! Take a look at other brands of tuna and you'll notice the difference. This tuna is also delicious and sustainably caught! This is one of the few seafood companies I actually trust!

This is THE BEST tuna I have ever had! I will never eat another brand. This tuna is like a fillet in a can. Love it!

column9: Fantastic hors d'oeuvres!!!! Amaze them at the next cocktail party.
column10: I cannot find OLD SOUTH watermelon pickles anywhere in Denver--other brands but not OLD SOUTH....which have the best flavor.The recipe:  wrap a pickle piece & half a pecan in a half strip of partially cooked bacon. This jerky manages to recreate that experience and tastes fantastic.  Try it and form your own opinion.

column4: Miss Cellophane "Clearly, you don't remember me."
column10: I have tried every veggie jerky I can get my hands on, and this is the best by far.  The flavor is perfect.  I love that it isn't spongy, or sawdust tasting like some of the other jerkys I have tried....some of them were ever, slimy, something a jerky should never be in my eyes. After going vegan for a little over a year now, I think one of the few things I missed was chomping on jerky.So after seeing online somewhere that Tofurky Jerky wasn't available I ordered one package of Original Hickory Pepper flavor from Vegan Dream. It's very good. Very tasty. Very good texture. My meat eating husband even said that it's really good jerky and there's none of that grizzle stuff you end up with in your mouth sometimes while eating real meat jerky. I've ordered twice now and I'll be ordering more!

column9: Best vegan jerky I have ever eaten in my life!
column10: I have tried every brand of vegan jerky known to man, including primal strips (gross!)  This brand was the closest tasting to the real thing, if not better!  Most vegan jerky tastes like canned dog food with the texture of wet cardboard.  I purchased the hickory flavor of this brand, it wasn't wet, was nice and chewy and had an perfectly balanced flavor.  No weird chemical taste.  It might be a little pricey but I would gladly pay extra for the best.

I've been veggie for a little over a year and jerky is something that I missed, mostly because I liked the chewy texture and saltiness of beef jerky. This product is very much like the real thing as far as texture and taste. I love this product and I'll be ordering other flavors to try them out as well. I would recommend this product to any of my meat eating friends.
Ate half of one and threw the other 23 in the garbage. Overwhelming taste/smell as if it had been soaked in sauce. Won't order it again.

Not being a food chemist, I'm not sure what the deal is here with vegan and vegetarian "meats."  I really like most veggie-based patties, "chicken" bits, and breakfast sausages.  However, the various "brats" that I so desperately want to grill are, for the most part, terrible.  And I don't just mean "not meat-like."  I mean, they don't taste very good.The food chemists at the famous Monell Chemical Senses Center have, as I remember, "hamburger in a vial."  That is, with your eyes closed, they can fool you into thinking there is a grilled hamburger in front of your face, when in reality it is a combination of chemicals they have isolated from this product.So how hard can it be to really simulate the flavor of bratwurst?In this case, it's jerky.  It kinda looks okay (needs more imperfections... lumps and bumps), has somewhat the same consistency (you gotta pull hard or break off a piece), and, as far as the "original hickory pepper" flavor, you can tell it has pepper.But that first bite made me think of those veggie brats.  Not a good association.I guess this just needs to be an acquired taste.  I do appreciate the effort... the vegan product, the non-GMO soy, and the low-fat (in this case, 0 grams of fat) product.But can't those Monell scientists work up a vial of "jerky taste and smell?"I'll be waiting.

Of course, Sen-Sen is not really candy at all: it is a monumentally strong breath freshener.  It makes Altoids mints seem like pitiful weak kid stuff by comparison.  It's been around for more than 100 years!  Those of us with sophisticated adult palates can appreciate quality bitter tastes in coffees, salad greens, beers, etc...and in this unique licorice "mint".  There is an almost soap-like flavor present, but I think it's more a "knee-jerk" tastebud reaction to the extremely concentrated flavor.  For the most part, kids don't seem to like Sen-Sen, which is fine...leaves more for us grups.  Definitely an acquired taste, but certainly a taste worth acquiring!

column9: SO Disappointed Does not taste like the ORIGINAL at all.
column10: I am very disappointed in these Sen-Sen's. I purchased them because they reminded me of my grandmother. When I was a child 45 years ago my grandmother had Sen-Sen all the time. Before TicTac....before those little bottles of Binaca...long before those "curiously strong mints"...there was SEN SEN.  One of the original breath fresheners, SEN SEN is a powerhouse.  Word to the wise, the main flavor is licorice so you better like this flavor if you're buying this product.  By the way, SEN SEN got a high profile honorable mention in a Billy Joel song back in the 80s.So, you need a breath freshener?  Like licorice flavors?  Then get some of these really tiny squares, pop one in your mouth, and warn your friends to stay back 100 feet until the initial rush is over.

I've loved these ever since my mom introduced me to them when I was a child.  I love genuine licorice just as much (as opposed to the "fake" licorice which is actually flavored with anise).  To the unfamiliar, you're not supposed to pop a bunch of them in your mouth like they are Nerds or cinnamon candy or something. If you try that, you get a mouth-ful of overwhelming flavor that might turn you off to a good little candy.

Sen Sen is a handy breath freshner that takes u bak to 1951(does me) when I was ll. It reminded me of fresh, clean smellin soap aroma--different from anything else! Thats why I had to taste it again, & again!
Hard to find product locally but it's just like I remember it - when I was a kid.

I searched in local stores for this product and proved unsuccessful until I searched at this site.  I was pleasantly surprised that Sen Sen's still existed ALL THESE YEARS and they still taste the same as well as VERY EFFECTIVE (I have to refrain from gum chewing to keep my breath fresh)!!

It was a treat to once again see Sen-Sen.  As a teenager in the 1950s, it seemed to me that everyone had a bag of Sen-Sens in their pocket and their unique flavor and aroma were everywhere.  Used to drive teachers mad; one warned us that it was a tool for drunks to disquise their breath.  Well, at least it wasn't chewing gum (the real candy culprit in those days) so it was consumed openly in class.So to relive my past, I ordered it from Candy Crate and it came quickly and just as they described.  No complaints from me.  Thanks, Candy Crate.

I don't know how many years it was since I had tasted these. I was wondering if they would still be the same when I ordered. Sure enough, they still had the original Sen Sen taste, bursting full of strong licorice.
Always had them in my mind but never saw them again, thanks God for internet.  I was really young when my Dad brought them home.  miniature happiness bits. :)
receved product fast and in great shape. It was so nice to be able to buy sen sen, i havent had them for a long time.  thank you so much

column9: Warning: this is definitely an acquired taste!
column10: I first encountered Sen-Sen about 45 years ago as a kid.  I found it next to a store checkout and bought myself a pack.  I had read about it in some book I loved and thought I'd give it a try.I fell in love with the taste.  Sen-Sen was my entre to my love of black licorice, the really strong stuff that you can only get from Italy or the Netherlands.I've had friends ask to sample it.  I first warn them to take ONE tiny square.  And then I warn them not to chew it.  And then I reassure them it's okay if they spit it out.  (About half of them do.)The ones who can take Sen-Sen usually become fans (or at least, they'll ask me for some every time they see me.)  That's why I buy a dozen packs at a time.  Not only is it tough finding it locally, but with a dozen packs, I have stocking stuffers for all those friends who ask for mine.
I've given these to people who've never heard of them before and they're amazed over the powerful and awesome taste from such a tiny bit.  You do have to like licorice or anise taste though..
Just like I remembered.  I paid way too much for it, though.  Unfortunately, I was forced to pay the price.

I don't know what made me even think about Sen-Sen, but glad I did.  Found this merchant, ordered, and voila!  They arrived in a timely fashion, tasting just the way I remembered.  Flashbacks to asking my grandmother for some; she'd open her "pocketbook" and pull them out, shaking her head and wondering aloud why a child would be interested in a smoker's breath mint...

I was so excited when I ordered this seasoning base. Finally a veg-friendly soup base with low sodium! Sadly, however, I was disappointed. The seasoning is quite bland with no resemblance to beef flavor what so ever. Just because there is less salt doesn't mean they can't add other seasonings to make it flavorful! And because there is so little flavor, you have to add more of the product to water to get any kind of flavor. This means you end up with the same amount of sodium or more as if you were to use less of the sodium-laden bouillon cubes sold everywhere.Honestly you're better of just buying vegetable soup base or vegetable bouillon cubes. You'll end up with the same amount of sodium while saving on calories.VEGANS be WARNED: It is listed as being vegan on the site, however there is NOT a vegan seal of approval like there is on the chicken base.  The ingredients do not state any animal products being used, but the phrase "natural flavorings" can be a warning sign of animal products unless stated otherwise. And if they were willing to certify the chicken base as vegan why not do the same for the beef if it too were vegan?
I purchased several varieties of this base. I find using the recommended amount creates a base with little to no flavor. I had to triple the amount - and it still was lacking...

While these are insanely expensive, they are wonderful and keep a long time in this dried form.  I was lucky enough to find them on sale so got several bags and they've kept beautifully. They can be chopped into smaller pieces, of course, for other applications. The richly infused reconstituting water offers a good base for a sauce. I'm so pleased, I'll be sticking with it.  Highly recommended.
