I wouldn't suggest this product unless you don't mind spending $25 and giving it to a kid that doesn't care about quality.  I was buying it for the grandma of my children for Christmas.

column9: Eight O'Clock French Roast Coffee and Amazon's Subscribe and Save a Winning Combination
column10: We've enjoyed Eight O'Clock French Roast Whole Bean coffee daily for about ten years.  We love its bold taste and aroma, and, although we're not coffee connoisseurs, we've tried many different coffees and have not found any we like more at any price.  The only dilemma was when we moved we were unable to purchase the 36 oz. bag in our new location.  No store carries it in the 36 oz. size, only the smaller 12 oz. bag which was inconvenient since it would only last about a week, and was costly.  I had located on-line vendors, but they charged a premium price to what we were used to paying before we moved, and added shipping on top of that.  When traveling on business I used to buy a 3 to 4 month supply at a time to keep us in coffee.  Then I learned of Amazon's Subscribe and Save program and found it at a lower price than we've ever payed, and shipping is free.  So far we've received three shipments, two regularly scheduled monthly orders and one extra shipment that I ordered because we were going to run out before our regular order shipped.  Amazon even emails me to let me know when my regular order will arrive and allows me to delay a shipment or place an order early if running low. We couldn't be happier with the coffee or with Amazon's Subscribe and Save program.

column9: My choice for the daily Brew!
column10: While I love a good and robust Starbucks as much as the next guys, the Eight O'clock Coffee French Roast is my coffee of choice for the daily brew.  It has always arrived fresh and bold in the whole bean variety.  I grind it to a sufficient espresso roast, and then load up the coffee pot.  It makes a consistently good, smooth, and bold cup of Joe every day - at about half the cost of higher end brands.

This is my sixth large bag of Eight O'Clock whole bean coffee that I have ordered from Amazon over the past five months, and I have tried four different kinds, or flavors. All, except for the Hazelnut flavored coffee beans, were great.This bag of coffee beans is excellent, as were four of the other two lb. bags of Eight O'Clock coffee. It has a very smooth flavor with no bitter aftertaste. I am now a regular Eight O'Clock whole bean coffee lover of almost all of their different coffee beans. It is consistently good and is as good, or better, than other coffee beans that I've paid twice as much for.
8 o'clock french roast beans makes the best coffee ever and it makes it so much easier to keep it in stock with subscribe and save  Awesome idea.

I was hesitant to buy this much coffee without trying it first; luckily, it's pretty good! Not rancid, flavorless, and no "off" flavors. I'm no coffee connoisseur, but I like it as much as the starbucks beans that I normally buy, and it's way cheaper (just 10 dollars for 36 ounces with subscribe and save).

column9: always a good pot of coffee
column10: Eight o clock coffee has been a part of our morning routine for years. The french roast is a favorite, smooth and tasty.

column9: Wife exclaimed "You made really good coffee!"
column10: I had purchased this brand at a local canned food warehouse store in the past, but not this flavor of beans.  I wanted to see if I could save money on Amazon for some coffee I could tolerate.  When I recognized the brand, and saw that the price was very good, I purchased the Eight O'clock French Roast Whole Bean, 36-ounce bag.I'm pleased to say that the result was beyond my middling expectations.  These beans make a great cup of coffee.  We use a high quality burr grinder to get an even grind and a nice French press for some stronger coffee. The first day I made this in the morning, after weeks of a different brand, my wife said "You made coffee really good this morning!".

A great taste at a resonable value. By using the subribe and save and grinding the beans myself then mixing a more expensive brand with the EIGHT o'clock that I ground at a ratio of 3 scoops to 1. I am then able to come up with a delicious cup of coffee at a fraction of the price that you would pay for a gourmet brand. By mixing the 2 I'm able to make my 36 ounce bag of coffee last from 1 arrival date to another. I am always asured of a great cup of coffee in the morning.
Truly the best coffee ever. We buy whole bean and grind for every pot brewed!  Perfect flavor....not that burnt flavor or weak flavor you get from other brands!

This coffee is very good. Its taste and quality are very close to Alterra coffee in our local shops, but with better price.  I previously tried Eight O'Clock coffee, Colombian roast, which is also very good.

This is the best coffee we have ever tasted! We love the bold, rich flavor. When we have visitors or house guest's, they always rave about the coffee and tell us they have changed to Eight O'Clock French Roast.

Buying in this size is much cheaper than buying in the store.  This coffee has a very good flavor - it is nothing spectacular, but haven't had a bad cup of this coffee - it comes out great in our Cuisinart.
This was the first time we had bought whole bean coffee. I only grind enough for a pot at a time and keep the rest in an air tight container. It is really good coffee, no bitter taste.

I read the 4+ star reviews and bought a bag, looking for a lower cost source for flavorful dark-roast coffee.  The coffee contains unripe beans, recognizable by their lighter color.  These 'quakers' (as they are known in the coffee trade) impart an off-taste to the coffee. It does not have a full-bodied french (dark) roast flavor.  The coffee beans are not well-selected, nor are they sorted after roasting to remove the unripe beans.  Overall, the beans do not exhibit much 'oily' character, and lack the full flavor I want in a dark-roast coffee.  Sorry, this was a disappointment and I will not be buying more.
I have become a kind of a coffee snob and must say that this eight o'clock coffeeis a great brew for the price. THe whole bean is always a more robust flavor and this product doesn't disappoint.
Eight O'Clock to me was the original A & P brand that we bought eons ago.  Saw it at a good price and bought the French Roast.  It is dark, flavorful and excellent value for a morning starter.

I'm not saying it's poor quality coffee.  What I AM saying is that it's not French Roast.It's not double roasted.  The beans are not double-roasted, dark and somewhat oily.There are at least a half dozen brands that are close to or nearly French Roast.  Another coffee available from Amazon.com, San Francisco Bay French Roast whole bean coffee, is what I prefer.

I am an avid coffee drinker, and have tried everything under the sun, and no matter what I try, I always end up coming back to this. I don't know what it is about this that just tastes so perfect to me, but the deliciousness of this coffee is undeniable. Anyone who mocks 8 O'Clock drinkers for not knowing their beans obviously has never tried it. This stuff is absolutely delicious.

column9: Best coffee value you can find!
column10: This is without a doubt the best coffee for the money that I've ever bought.  And better than most more expensive brands as well!  I didn't try this brand for years because it was the cheapest on the shelf and ...well you get what you pay for right? Not always true!! This coffee makes a consistently great cup of coffee.  Smooth, never bitter.  This is an amazing value!  Buy with confidence!

Tasted this coffee while on vacation at my sister's home in Minnesota and was instantly hooked! Has that full round flavor of deep roasted coffee -- can't imagine drinking any thing else when I make my morning brew! Eight O'Clock Coffee does the French Roast Bean proud!

Eight O'Clock Coffee, French Roast Whole Bean, 36-Ounce BagAbsolutely the best coffee...smooth, full-bodied, everything you want in that morning mug...or whenever. This is not French Roast. Your first hint his when you open the bag, its medium brown and not black. French Roast is supposed to have sticky beans, these are bone dry. They are small, without aroma, and the coffee tastes terrible. I don't think I can return an opened bag, but I would if I could.

I ordered this by mistake, as I have no grinder.  However, I was still able to use it all up (by beating the beans in a thick envelope with a rubber mallet each morning), good thing I don't have any neighbors!  The coffee was delicious.

column9: Tastes like the bag it came in
column10: First off, I am not a coffee snob. I will drink a cup of gas station coffee as long as it doesn't taste like dirty dish water. I bought this product knowing that Eight O'Clock is not a high-end, artisan coffee. However, I was hoping that once ground, it would be somewhat palatable despite it's low price. Unfortunately, that was not the case. This coffee has no flavor, just a plastic, stale aftertaste. I'm not sure if there is an issue with quality control at Eight O'Clock, or if the beans are just extremely low quality. Either way, I would suggest spending your money on something else; there are other inexpensive brands that don't taste like a grocery bag in liquid form.

column9: eight o clock coffee, french roast
column10: I like this coffee a lot. Nothing better than whole bean coffee, fresh brew smell, nothing like it!Very good coffee.
I've tried many others and for the price this coffee can't be beat! If you're looking for an even bolder coffee, try the Eight O'clock Italian roast.

In the never-ending search for an inexpensive but really good coffee bean, we gave this a try. I read a lot of the reviews from people who said they weren't connoisseurs, but thought it was pretty good. I'm not sure if I qualify as a connoisseur (or if I want to), but it's not nearly as dark-roasted as I generally prefer my coffee, and more importantly, the taste --- no matter how strongly I try to brew it --- is just kind of weak. The search continues.

column9: Delicious French roast beans and great value
column10: I started buying these years ago when an eminent consumer testing magazine, I believe Cook's Illustrated, did a taste test on French roast coffee beans and Eight O'Clock came out near or at the top, above pricier brands. The taste of French roast is important to me and when I tried this brand I agreed with the magazine taste test. To top it off, the price is right.

If you like your coffee to give you a strong rush of caffeine jolt with a dark roasted bitter taste (like most Starbucks), then this coffee may not be for you. If you like milder tasting coffee that has bit more aroma and taste, then this coffee may fill your needs. Starbucks this coffee isn't, and that isn't necessary a bad thing.I recommend everyone try this brand of coffee at least once. It was ranked #1 by one consumer magazine as the best coffee.I do like the taste of this coffee. Even though it is a French Roast, it tastes almost like a Hazelnut with very nutty flavor. The natural and pleasant flavor of the coffee isn't drown out by the bitter taste.The caffeine rush is also very mild and subtle. If you find yourself too hyper from drinking Starbucks, then this could be a good alternative brand.This coffee is also surprisngly affordable. It costs little over 1/2 of Starbucks coffee by weight.

column9: Just finished my first 2 lbs of Copper Moon Sumatra
column10: I thought I might be disappointed, but the Eight O'Clock French Roast is quite decent.  I'm still waiting for my Italian Roast which seems to have been deleted from my Cart.Ciao

column9: Quality substitute for higher priced "premium" roasts
column10: This is a good substitute for the higher priced "premium" coffees out there. It provides a subtle, yet bold taste, and is quite pleasing. It isn't quite as bold as the SBux French Roast, but it does the job - and for the price I really think it's a steal.

column9: This is what I was looking for
column10: I did love the Folgers Brazilian (style) coffee but this is great in that it's more economical, tastes great, and I can order it on a monthly basis.

We love whole bean french roast coffee by Eight O'Clock, but were having such a hard time finding it in super markets. Amazon had it and we are so pleased we signed up to receive the coffee once a month. The price is right that is for sure. If you like French Roast whole bean coffee, I highly recommend this purchase.

Love this coffee! Comparable quality to brands which are much more expensive. My local grocery store stopped carrying the large size bag of the french roast. Now I rely on amazon to get my coffee fix.
This coffee did not have a strong bold taste that I like from French Roast. It was more like a Columbian coffee. It was smooth tasting. Just not strong enough for my taste. I would not buy it again.

I was introduced to Eight O'Clock coffee brand over 40 years ago when my father and mother bought it.  It was a daily staple in our household.  Little did I know that this coffee was still being sold and of course, I snatched it up.  Being the french roast lover in my family was an added bonus.  I cannot say enough good things about this coffee.  Back over 40 years ago it was the cheapest coffee on the grocery shelf, but you could never tell it by its taste which exceeds the taste of some of he high end brands of coffee.  Eight O'Clock coffee is where its at and should be if you are a coffee lover looking for the best.  They just don't get any better than this and the added bonus is the cheaper price.

My folks drank Eight O'Clock coffee the whole time I was growing up, so when I became a coffee drinker myself, it was an easy product to pick up.  Over time, I sampled all sorts of other roasters and varieties, sometimes finding something better, sometimes not, occasionally even switching my everyday brand of choice for a while.  Eventually, I always ended up with Eight O'Clock again simply for the value: I have not found a reasonably good-tasting coffee at a lower price.  If you're a regular consumer of coffee (our house makes a pot per day for sure, sometimes more), you've got to find the brand that fits all your minimum criteria, and for me, this is it.

column9: great whole bean coffee at a great price
column10: We've been using Eight O'Clock coffee for years and the French Roast is our favorite. We always have family and friends compliment on how good our coffee is and most of that is due to the consistent quality and freshness of the beans. If you are big coffee drinkers the subscription price comes w/free shipping at Amazon and can't be beat anywhere.

We cut back on our coffee consumption and only drink it in the AMs.  We wanted to have a flavorful pot for our daily cuppa so we asked our son (a quasi coffee expert).  He recommended 8 O'clock and specifically the French Roast.  We've found it to be superb.
Great coffee.  This was a very fast, easy transaction.  Surprised at the full, rich body of the coffee taste.  Also pleasantly surprised at the size of the volume & package.  Very pleased.

I've always enjoyed Eight O'Clock coffee and this did not disappoint.  I drink this coffee pretty much everyday and brew it using a standard drip style single funnel with filter.  Even when fairly finely ground, the coffee is still smooth and easy to drink without being bitter.  I will definitely be ordering more of this.
Wow. This stuff knocked my socks off. Will be a frequent buyer now and can't wait to try their other offerings.

This is a flavorful cup of coffee but it is NOT French roast. French roast is very dark and has an almost smokey flavor. Eight O'Clock is good but if you're looking for french roast this isn't it. This is a medium to dark, mostly medium, cup of joe that tastes like their old Bokar coffee from the A&P. I am mixing it with an espresso roast to have it be my morning coffee. Waste not want not.
What a deal! Three pounds of fresh coffee beans delivered to me each month for way less than purchasing the same item at the store.

column9: I've tried several brands at Costco
column10: My son and I both think this is a really good cup of coffee.  We grind ours in the Bodum Bistro Electric Burr Coffee Grinder, http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00430E94Q/ref=wms_ohs_product - pricey, but we picked it up when it was $80 and you get what you pay for and it's fun.  We keep it cranked all the way to the coarse, french press setting and it's perfect cup every time.
The price certainly is right and for most coffee drinkers this would be ideal.  We are used to drinking a more rich full bodied french roast coffee and this falls short in those categories.

column9: Meh.  Not that impressed. Kind of lousy.
column10: I mean, yeah, it's coffee.  True dat.  But it's not that good.  I think you are better off with the Eight O'Clock straight Arabica blend.I thought I was doing myself a favor cuz I love French Roast.  But this is perhaps the worst whole bean French Roast I've ever encountered.I tried everything --different grind settings, French Press, "melita" style manual drip, coffee makers. All were: meh.I'd say if you like French Roast a lot, go with one of the slightly more pricey brands available on Amazon.  There is this one organic brand,name escapes me at the moment.  It's a little more money, not much, so it's reasonable.  Very good whole bean stuff.  Wish I could recall the name.Thanks for tuning in.

We have been receiving the autoshipments for a while now, which is great, but the product we received this time is terrible.  The coffee is not fresh smelling or tasting, and I noticed this morning that the use by date is close.  I'm going to have to toss it and go buy something else.

This is just ok.  The good news is that it's cheap.  But a few days ago I drank a really high quality (and really expensive) organic coffee and there was absolutely no comparison.  If you put lots of sugar or flavored creamer in your coffee, this might be fine.  But if you drink your coffee with little cream or sugar, get a higher quality coffee.  If you French Press your coffee and love the ritual of making coffee, spend the money for better and fresher beans.

column9: In my opinion not french roast
column10: Beans are not dark or oily, very mild flavor. Beans are not consistant in color, this means the beans are not roasted evenly. I hate to say it but Starbucks is 3 times better. I will try other french roast from amazon.All orders from amazon arrived on time.

column9: Not very dark for a dark roast flavor...
column10: No, the color in the bag I got looked more like Breakfast Blend, with a combination of light and dark roasted beans. Well, in the bag I got, there was even one GREEN coffee bean in there. It performs poorly, the brew color out of the auto-grind espresso machine I have quits rather too quickly. That prompts an adjustment to use less water, which means I have to do more brew cycles to fill a cup, three instead of two. That kinda kills the savings.This bean works very well for blended drinks, since the lighter flavor doesn't become overpowering when blended with ice, milk and sugar.I ate a few beans and they had this immature taste, not full-bodied coffee, like a burnt pinto bean taste. It seems like they got a supplier that includes a higher percentage of immature beans (not fully ripened when picked) which tens to roast into a lighter color than the rest. Either the picking machine's driver did not adjust to prevent picking the immature beans, or they decidedly had it set to increase yield at the sacrifice of the quality.Only using this one for iced coffee drinks.

column9: too weak... not a medium dark roast...
column10: It doesn't have weird and very bitter aftertaste some other coffees have, but basically it doesn't have much taste at all.I'm a strong-coffee-lover, which is why I ordered medium-dark roast. French roast isn't dark-roasted, but it shouldn't be this much weak, either.I guess I will grind more beans next time.Yet, I can't smell much of coffee aroma, either.I'm quite disappointed and won't order anymore from the Eight o'clock again.I read other reviews in other websites, and it seems like they 'used to' be good before they changed something...sigh...
The taste was stronger than I anticipated, although I wouldn't discourage anyone from trying this  coffee..we all  have a different taste for coffee

I've tried a couple of different French Roast coffees through Amazon. Cameron's Organic French Roast was by far the best but their prices have jumped considerably.I've also tried Coffee Bean Direct French Roast Papua which was okay but had a different flavor for a french roast.  The moment I opened the Eight O'Clock French Roast I had a bad feeling since the beans were very light in appearance and not very oily at all.  I've been drinking it for a few weeks and it ranks with some inferior grocery store bulk varieties. If you love a good french roast in the mornings like I do then I suggest you look elsewhere.  I saw an article that mentioned that in 2010 it was highly rated by  Consumer Reports (or similar consumer guide) but they noted that in 2011, despite the  "new look, same great taste" ad at the top, the newer version was inferior. I'll keep looking for a good(not necessarily great) french roast at a reasonable price.

When I think of a hazelnut-flavored coffee drink, I generally think of the type produced by a barista with a syrup. By definition, my expectation of the Tassimo pod was therefore relatively low. To my pleasant surprise, the mild hazelnut flavor already emanates from the machine during the brewing process, and the result is a perfectly balanced cup of coffee with an intense but not overbearing hazelnut flavor.

My first impression isn't as great as I thought based on reviews from the same product.Started to brew my fist disc and I noticed that it poured too much water, resulting in a mix with no consistency, it tasted fair enough but felt like a hot juice. It improved a little after adding some milk though.I've got a brand new Bosch brewer so it's not a matter of the machine itself, seems it's programmed that way.I'd rather buy the starbucks blends than this one, specially the Latte Primo; that one has great creamy texture.

I buy a lot of If You Care brand products & was very pleased to see they make environmentally friendly gloves.  I ordered them through the subscribe & save program thinking I wouldn't worry about household gloves again!I am so disappointed in these.  I am canceling the subscription with amazon.  The cotton flock lining is a joke.  I certainly cannot feel it.  The rubber is stiff & the fit is poor.  I ordered the size small & have to keep tugging them up because they are too long in the fingers.  They move down a bit making matters worse.  For some reason the pinkie finger in particular is way too long; more so than the extra length in the other fingers.My hands start to sweat in these pretty darn fast.  When I need to take them off, they don't come off easy despite the fact that they are too long/big.  I have to practically peel them off.  They are not comfortable.  The only thing to like about them besides being environmentally friendly is that they are a pretty cheerful green color.I am going back to my old gloves by Casabella.  I have yet to find a better pair of household gloves.  They fit well, last long & are very comfortable.  They also have more meat to them for protection when you are using really hot or cold water.  Don't try using the If You Care with scalding hot water!  Amazon sells Casabella & Casabella is what I recommend.

I have been buying these gloves for a few years now from a local health food store.  I am pleased that I found them at Amazon for a much better price.  The fit for me is perfect (size small) and the gloves seem to last a lot longer than gloves that I used to buy at the grocery store.  I started buying these gloves because they are relatively environmentally friendly, but I now buy them because they last.

column9: Only way to get these where we live!!!
column10: All the local grocery stores/chain stores used to carry Lays Salt and Vinegar chips - which are my husband and daughter's favorite! Then they were NO where to be found!! I live in LARGE metropolitan area in TEXAS!!! I wrote to Frito-Lay - and they were NOT helpful - they just said "not all items are available in all markets and you cannot direct order"Doing a search for the individual packs of Baked Lays for school lunches (another impossible to find item) - I found these! My family is sooooo happy!!Thank you, thank you, thank you!!!

We were able to buy the large bags before at our Cub Foods.  Now we can't even get this size. I married a Canadian & this is what they are used to.  My daughter has Loved them since she was able to eat chips.  She is almost 9 so I got her the whole box for christmas.  It made a fun gift.  She has had to settle for pringles but the Lay's are so much better!!!  Please bring them back to the states!!!!
Be nice if were in larger bags, not real big, like 4 or 5oz bags. Lovethem anyway.
I enjoyed the taste of Lay's Potato Chips, Salt & Vinegar, 1.5-Ounce Large Single Serve Bags (Pack of 64).
Impossible to eat just one (that is a bit of a problem), much better tasting than the plain potato chips.

column9: One of the worst green teas I've ever tasted!
column10: I had just recently ran out of green tea and the tea I usually get on amazon was no longer available, so I decided to give this one a try since it was 15% off with the gevalia discount + 15% off with subscribe and save. I made the tea and couldn't swallow more than one sip. It smelled horrible and had a really bad fake lemon-like taste. I forced myself to try it again, just in case it was just a one time thing, nope, still bad. I recommend you don't buy this tea, instead get yogi green tea. This green tea is bad quality and tastes atrocious. Plus, I can't return it to amazon since it is a grocery item...

This tea is not to my preference.  I am an avid tea drinker.  This tea is bitter and I would get a better brew by gathering the grass from outside that the gardeners blew over to the edge of the parking lot and throwing it into a pot of hot water.  I didn't taste any citrus in it.
Another Gevalia Tea that I have had over the years. It's Green and really Green in colour. Great tasting tea. I enjoy a cup of tea any time.

column9: Try this tea if you don't like the taste of green tea
column10: I have been drinking this tea for over 10 years now and it is some of the best green tea on the market. I had never liked the flavor of green tea but I was trying to drink it because of the health benefits but no matter how much I tried to drink regular green tea, I couldn't get it down because of the taste.  So I decided to order this flavor along with their other green tea flavor, Ancient Cherry, and now I can finally drink and enjoy green tea.  I steep the tea for 5 minutes for best flavor.The citrus flavor is light enough so that you know it is flavored but not so much that it overwhelms the tea.I recently bought some other brands of flavored green teas to try and save money but they just don't measure up to the Gevalia flavored green teas.

My mother loves this water, and she cannot buy it in West Virginia where she lives.  I found it on Amazon and had it delivered to her.  She was so excited!  She commented that it was so well wrapped that not even one of the glass bottles was broken.  That made her happy, which in turn made me happy!
I used the cute little glass bottles for the centerpieces for my wedding. They are so unique. I was going for a country shabby chic theme. They were delicious to drink too!

column4: G. Chen "what is in a nickname"
column10: I had this first in Las Vegas, when I went for a trip.  I was so thirsty from walking around in the hot desert. When I went to a restaurant, Bouchon, they didn't have any lemonade. So, the waiter offered me this stuff... I wasn't sure at first. I thought it was a trick to get me to pay more money for something that is the equivalent of squeezed lemon in water with some sugar. BUT IT WAS SO GOOD. I had limonada everyday when I was in Vegas, everywhere that they offered it. I would demand to have a bottle of the good stuff.Unfortunately, when I came back to my natural habitat on the East Coast. I did not find any Limonada anywhere. When I tried to google for it, even that masterful search engine found nothing. Fast forward a couple months later, I go to a charity event. They offer as a giveaway to the people who attended drinks, sponsored by SAN PELLAGRINO. <3  Heart be still!!!  It was my beloved Limonada in the US. In the north! Say what???Hoping that maybe limonada had somehow made its way to my cold region, I decided to try again my search. I looked online. BEHOLD Amazon, this retailer sells it in 6 packs! In the glass bottle! Straight from the bubbling springs of Italy. I purchased some right away. In didn't care if shipping was about double the price of the product. A few days later, these wonderful bottles made it's way to my refrigerator.I've been enjoying one a day. This supplier seems to have the best price so far of all the places I've looked. You can get a larger quantity for cheaper price per bottle. One retailer is selling it for $48 for free shipping for like a case with 48. However, if you want to try it out first, you might want to go with this listing. Currently, the price is $15 (including shipping & handling for 6 bottles). Not a bad deal for the most delicious bubbly lemonade in the world.

I can only find these in the can now if I go to a grocery store.  I think that they taste so much better from the glass bottles. Which I can only find on amazon now. It taste very good and I love the lemon flavor. They should make more than just 6 in a pack i think!!

column9: The most delicious beverage I have ever tasted
column10: Absolute perfection in a bottle- Just be careful, this stuff is really strong, so you might want to just take sips when you first "get to know it". I'm chugging em now though.

A very natural, crisp drink, but it is LEMONY like I've never tasted before.  Gave me some wicked heartburn, but then again, that's just the way I reacted to it.  If you're into a lightly carbonated Lemon drink made with the well known and trusted San P. water, this stuff is for you.  If you tend to get heartburn/reflux, I'd advise you to steer clear.

When you compare the zesty Limonata Sparkling Lemon Beverage to other sparkly lemon beverages, you begin to realize the sheer perfection of the Limonata beverage by San Pellegrino. The balance of lemon, sparkle and zest takes this drink to the level of a gourmet beverage, which requires no mixing. I may have tasted this before, but recently ordered it while eating out at a Restaurant.San Pellegrino is also made with mineral water found near the town of San Pellegrino Terme which is located 70 kilometers northeast of Milan. The water flows from a thermal spring at the foot of a Dolomite mountain wall. The use of this water definitely adds to the energy this drink seems to possess.The carbonation seems more sophisticated and delicate. The only way to describe it is to say these waters are the champagne of sparkling waters.~The Rebecca Review
This stuff is the most delicious beverage out there - but it's difficult to find in a 6-pack of bottles so I ordered it from Amazon. That's quite an expensive way to go, but boy was it worth it!

I bought this tea hoping it would help give me a little more alertness working the graveyard shift. It tastes wonderful, but I felt no extra energy during or after drinking. It is a very nice mellow tea though, definitely enjoy it.

column4: Doreen B. Bishop "Doreen Bishop cat parent"
column10: These are so GREAT for those times when you have a beer and nuts. The perfect size and not a lot of calories. Always have a box of these out for my quest who ask me where I get them and now we are putting them in our kids lunches. They are lovin them and I know it is a healthy old fashion snack. TRY them ,BET you can't eat just one :-)
I love planters honey roasted cashews!  These are perfect for a healthy snack on the go!  I've tried some other brands of honey roasted cashews and I definitely like planters the best!

I mean really, what's not to love? AND they are in more reasonable portion control packages, which will keep them fresher (and discourage eating all of them at once).  My dad also likes these (he generally likes the snacks at my place better than his unimpressive stash).  They're great to keep in my purse for AFTER dealing with a blood sugar low to help maintain a steady level until the next meal- and the touch of sweetness is a treat :)
I got these for my mom who is now 92 and she said that she just love these peanut and the way they were pack.

column9: Yummy, Fresh Each Time, No One Else's Dirt
column10: I like the single serving usefulness of this packaging.  Just the right amount for me.  Single serving to certain guests also have benefits.  Price on Amazon is also excellent.  Quality of nuts is reasonable in terms of freshness, size and taste. Not extremely high quality, but good enough for most people such as me. I'd buy them again when I run out.  If you are a nut snob, these may not compare to high end quality nuts.
These are okay. I tried them because I love honey roasted peanuts. However, with these the honey roasted flavor kind of overpowers the unique cashew taste. I think I will stick with salted cashews.
If you love salty smoked jerky that is hard, long cut, and has the hang marks on the end this is great stuff. I personally love all of those traits and this is some of the best.

column9: Very Very Salty, only ate 1 or 2 sticks and threw the rest away
column10: This jerky has been by far the saltiest I have ever had. I actually like salt but to a certain point and this went way beyond it. My favorite jerky was the World Kitchens brand brown sugar but it's no longer available. Unless you really like your food Extra Salty I would stay away. as far as tenderness I'll give it a 7 out of 10.
im sorry but you just cant compare anything with wild bills.  this jerky was not bad but a little fatty and has a funky smell to it.  would not buy again.

My husband has been praising Wild Bill's for years now.  We saw it was available on Amazon, but by the time went to purchase it, it was no longer available.  So we got this one since it compares itself to Wild Bill's.  I can't say that it tastes much like Wild Bill's, but I like it better!!  Even my "Only Wild Bill's will do" jerky-loving husband said this stuff was beyond good.  We may not bother with ol' Wild Bill as long as we can get this one.  Buffalo Bill's is good to, but so far this is my personal favorite!  Thin strips that are a bit "leathery" but so long as you have all your teeth no problem.  Heck, you could probably be missing a few teeth and still have no problem.  Last I checked, jerky is made for chewin!
I've tried many different types including my own.  This is some of the best jerky I've ever had.  Similar to Wild Bill's Jerky, but less salty and a hint of sweet.
My dogs alway like these treats.  The size makes the perfect for small dogs and it is hard to find them in my local stores.

These are great for training your dog.  They are really itty-bitty and dogs love them.  It's much easier than cutting up hotdogs for training and not messy at all.  I keep a stock of these on hand all the time.

I thought I would never see these again, and then, on a lark (yes, I love birds) I looked on Amazon one night to see if they knew where to find CROWS in the classic box along with my other favorite candy....FRUIT GUMS.  I was astonished to be able to order multiples of each.Both arrived quickly, and upon being sampled, were even better and fresher than I remember.  With this kind of candy, you can run the risk ofbiting into a not-so-fresh piece and losing a crown.  I have ordered and reordered since and never once gotten anything that wasn't perfect. You get a dozen boxes in an order, and if you have any guilt, decide to give 6 boxes away.I am giving these to some of the younger people on my CHristmas list to be sure the addiction goes on.  Pushing Crow.  Why not?  After the recent election.....

column9: Pure Black Walnut is hard to find.
column10: The recipe my Grandmother passed down calls for pure Black Walnut Extract.  The grocery only had artifical Black Walnut so I looked online and found this product.  I took a chance and I am very happy with it!  This makes my brownies taste just like Grandma's!

This black walnut has excellent flavor.  My ice cream was wonderful. I was unable to locate this in any stores.  I also purchased the bourbon vanilla.  Waiting to try that.  The ingredients were simple... water, alcohol, black walnut.

column9: Tastes pretty good, but not organic
column10: These are pretty good chocolate covered raisins.  The chocolate is not very sweet, and is almost a semi-sweet chocolate taste.  The raisins are good, but not as good as organic raisins.  Would be 5 stars if the ingredients were organic.

Bought this to try it out and it's wonderful! Use it on tomatoes and mozzarella and you'll never go back to balsalmic vinegar again.  It clings to the tomatoes and cheese, so you don't need bread to get the flavor. Have purchased several and am sending to friends.

I ordered these sugarless Twizzlers to replace the regular Twizzlers I love so much. My goal was to still eat Twizzlers, but cut down on calories.It didn't work. The first thing I saw on the package was "Not a low calorie food." Bummer! As far as taste was concerned, it wasn't bad, but these Twizzlers tasted a bit on the dry side, unlike the melt-in-your-mouth consistency of the regular product.So, while it was a good try, these Twizzlers did not replace regular Twizzlers and I will probably not be purchasing them again.

This is a fabulous, easy to use product that results in large, healthy flowers.  I tried the liquid form and was not nearly as pleased with it because it was much more work to walk around my large yard with the hose and that bulky spray device.  With the Shake and Feed, just sprinkle some around everything you want to feed and turn on the water.  Of course you must be careful not to over-fertilize plants that might be planted in an already fertilized soil.  That's just common sense.

Using this with the regular Miracle Grow soil ends up damaging the plants. Well it did for mine anyway. The leaves quickly turned yellow, and brown and black spots developed on them. They looked like burn marks. A friend of mine told me it's because it's overfertilizing them and putting too much chemicals in the dirt. I then spent some time picking out as much of it as I could and eased up on the watering. The plants have gotten somewhat better. The leaves that were already starting to turn yellow before I did all that are now not turning yellow as fast. The look of it also kept throwing me off. Whenever I thought something was starting to sprout, it turned out it was just one of those little green pellets. So there's no need to use this stuff and I certainly won't use it anymore in the future.

column9: DO NOT FEED YOUR DOG THIS TREAT
column10: Note: His blood work from his last visit to the vet in April were all normal. My dog has not been sick up until I bought this bag of jerky on a whim in June.In late Aug I had to take him to the vet because he was suffering from diarrhea & fever of 106. They gave him fluids & medication which treated his gastrointestinal upset.  However, last night I brought him in for a check up and requested a blood test to see if his kidneys/liver were doing okay (since I was paranoid from the treats I had fed him). Results came back and he has inflammation in his liver (ATL), his liver enzymes are high (from the toxins that are in this jerky). I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND ANYTHING FROM CHINA.MUST READ CAREFULLY THAT THE FOODS ARE ACTUALLY MADE IN USA RATHER THAN PACKAGED IN USA.

column9: A classic tree for a beginner
column10: This little juniper tree provides a great starting point for trying your hand at Bonsai as a hobby.  The pot and tree arrived wrapped in a plastic bag then stuffed into a box with foam peanuts.  Everything was in great shape.  If your fisherman is missing his fishing pole look for a crude looking toothpick as you unwrap the tree.  This is the fishing pole.  After rising the loose dirt out of the man's hand I was able to delicately push the pole into his grip.  It knocks loose at times, but is easy to put back.  It could be glued or pasted in, but that might cause problems down the road as it gets bumped.  So for now I'm content to just fix it when it gets knocked out.  The bird was a bit beat up (paint marring).  But it gives the whole setup a nice weathered look.  This keeps it from looking too factory finished.  You'll need to purchase some bonsai tools for the tree.  I purchased the kit found on this site that came with the pruners, bamboo brush, and broom rake.  Also you'll need to get some training wire.  The tree as it arrived was parked squarely on top of the fisherman.  After a month of training wire, it is trained off of him and the rocks.In the end, buy this little tree and you'll be pleased with the purchase.  It's a hobby that requires patience.  And remember, that any scratches, dings, or bumps carry with them a story unique to you.  So instead of getting upset, think of any little damage you do as a unique part of your experience with the tree.  Have fun.

column9: Dog loved it, until his first bowel movement.
column10: I am a big fan of treats that are digestable.  I purchased this product thinking it would be safe to feed my dog.  I left the treat for my dog on my way out the door for work, when I arrived home 4 hours later the treat was fully gone and the poor dog could not control his bowel movements and had diarrhea.This diarreha lasted for 2 days, and was so bad that I had to take a trip to the vet which ended up being one of the most expensive trips I've made there yet to have him tested for various illnesses.I didn't attribute the diarrhea to the product at first, but a week later I again gave my dog this bone treat and a few hours after eating the bone the diarrhea started back up again.I'm unsure what exactly about this product is "healthy", and would argue against it being "edible".  Sure technically you can give this product to your dog and if he eats peices it won't require surgery to remove.  But you'll spend 2-3 days dealing with uncontrolable doggy bowel movements, and excessive dehydration.  And if your not quick enough to realize it's this treat causing your problems you'll spend a few hundred bucks at the vets office like I did.And don't get me started on how quickly these things can get eaten....From now on I'll stick with bully sticks.

column9: Yes, it is edible but healthy??
column10: Seriously?? By whose standards??Since when are wheat starch, glycerin, cellulose, potato starch, bacon flavor (?what does this mean?) healthy?I bought this thinking it would last a few hours or days but my dog just gobbled it up in minutes.I love the nylabone chew products but I don't recommend these unless you have very large dogs that can eat them as treats.
It didn't take very long either. Not fun to come home to.The dogs liked them though.

For the price, it would be nice if these bones lasted longer, but they do their job so I'm not complaining. I spoke to someone at a pet supply store who recommended these as an alternative to rawhide chews, and he said they're fully digestible, while being good for dogs' teeth and gums. My dog (a 30lb beagle/coonhound) LOVES the bacon flavor, and it keeps him occupied for a little while (probably about a half hour). At this rate, these are a little more expensive than rawhides, and serve the same function, but are safer for your dog, since they are more easily digestible than rawhide. Ultimately, these bones are a pretty nice treat for my dog, but I'll also be looking for some longer-lasting chews to keep him occupied for longer periods.
I agree with the previous reviewers - I should have listened! My Boston Terrier chewed up and ate an entire bone in less than 5 minutes. This may be a good "treat" but I would not call it a chew toy!
I can't necessarily blame the product but my dog sniffed this and wouldn't even pick it up.  Looks like I'll be donating the other box I bought to his dog friends in the hopes that they will eat it.

column9: our pupply loves the bacon flavor
column10: She absolutely loves this bone.  She likes to chew on it for a bit and then bury it somewhere in our cushions.  triple pack is nice because it drastically reduces the price at a brick and mortar store.
Our 5 year old boxer ate these with in 10 minutes. I was hoping for something that would last longer, but she did love them!

Since I have been seeing so many recalls not only on dog food but treats, I decided to look for something that is made in this country and found these.  My two Pom's love them and it is their morning treat.  They won't let forget to give them to them as they make sure they stare me down till I do. lol  They can be eaten without any worry of anything happening to them as they don't contain plastic or any other foreign material. Unless I find a bad review or hear that there is a recall on these, hope there isn't, I will continue to buy these Edibles.  My boys like the bacon flavor the best out of all the different flavors offered.  Amazon also offers a really good price on these.
All gone! Trixie really loved it and we would purchase this product again. The price was a bit high for a bone that lasted no time at all but she is worth it!
These are awesome! They keep my puppy busy for several hours and satisfies his need to chew! I will be buying plenty more!

First the good news: the dogs really liked these.  Now the bad news: they are really more of a treat than a chew bone. My guys ate about a quarter of the souper size in less than 5 minutes.  I had to take them away before they ate the whole thing in one try.  I was hoping for something that would keep them occupied for awhile but this is not it.

This is not worth it.  My pit ate it in large chunks in under a minute.  i bought it locally for what i'd pay for dinner- not worth it in terms of money or time in keeping him busy.  he takes longer to eat an entire bowl of food..

My dogs seems to love the flavor of the bones but they don't look to be much bigger than just the regular "Large" bones you buy in the store. After Buddy (my dog) brings this one out of his hiding place (he hides all the bones that are easily edible), I'm sure he will devour it immediately.

My dog is being treated for a condition that requires me to reduce her exercise level to almost nothing.  I'm desperately trying to find treats that will keep her quiet and aren't rawhide.  The vet told me I shouldn't give me dog rawhide on a daily basis, so I decided to try these edible Nylabones.My dog loved how these tasted, but she finished them in a matter of minutes.  The description calls these "edible chews," so I was expecting these bones to keep my dog occupied.  I wouldn't call these bones "chewy" either.  They seem to be slightly tougher than a Milkbone, but just as dry.  I have been a fan of Nylabone products for as long as I can remember.  I raised all my puppies with Nylabones, but these edible Nylabones don't last long enough.On the plus side, my dog did enjoy these treats and they didn't give her an upset stomach (she has a pretty tough stomach though).

First let me say that all three of my dogs love these.  They are not very aggressive chewers, but these only lasted a matter of minutes with each one of them.  For this price, I expected a toy/treat that would last much longer.  Save your money and buy a box of milk bones.

When my first set of bones arrived covered in thick, hairy, green mold, I just sent them back and asked for a replacement. I thought that it might just be a one time thing. But my replacment set of bones came covered with the same type of mold. I am very disappointed! Amazon rarely disappoints me, but it has this time. I will just have to look for these at my local pet store.

My dog loves these.  A little pricey, but can be broken into 2 or 3 smaller treats.  My boxer boy has a sensitive stomach, and these have never given him any "digestive" (read "gas" or "the runs") problems, although I limit him to just a third of a bone a day.  May not be the healthiest, as one reviewer said, but seems to make my dogs limited life happier.  Not to mention, most real bacon is loaded with salt, chemicals, and saturated fat...not too healthy either!

We bought the multi-pack that comes with the standard non-edible nylabones. After 3 minutes of our puppy chewing on this "edible" bone, we got concerned that he had bitten off a chunk of it. To our relief, the bone is technically "edible", but the fine print says for puppies 6 months and older. To me, that's a little misleading. I'd consider a puppy under 6 months old.Our dog passed the 1-inch chunk he'd eaten, but it was his first soft stool in the 6 weeks we've had him. The rest of the bone found its way into the garbage. Nylabone should reconsider selling a multi-pack of these bones mixed with the non-edible style. We were ultra-concerned when handing him a bone that he managed to eat assuming it was the same as the others.My advice, steer clear of these "healthy" edible Nylabones.

column9: Dog loved it; but it's a treat, NOT a chew!

column9: Very disappointing if you have previously used the plastic Nylabones.
column10: My puppy is teething so I had previously purchased the original Nylabone made out of flavored plastic. The dog loved it, not super excited about the regular bone but she did put a lot of work into destroying it. When she finally finished the original plastic bone I decided to go back to the store and grab some more. I was looking around and came across these, "natural," flavored bones and thought.... "SWEET!!! Same great bone but easier to digest!" How wrong I was. First off this is NOTHING like the plastic teething bones. They crumble easily... and by easily I mean my 3.5 month old Wheaten Terrier destroyed these in less than 30min, and she's only about 15 pounds right now. They are recommended for dogs 6 months + with pretty much a full set of permanent teeth because they can shred the bone more easily and to a finer debris. For my dog this was BS... she destroyed these into tiny little flakes that can be easily digested AND managed to get them all over her underbelly and tangled in her fur. The mess wasn't an issue.. the durability was. This is basically an expensive treat, I much rather give her bullysticks over this as a treat (and they last longer). If your dog is teething, this is def NOT the Nylabone version you want. Stick to the original plastic flavored bones or frozen towels. Both work great.

column9: This is one of the best dry dog foods you can buy
column10: This is an outstanding dry dog food. High in protein(42%) and low in carbohydrates. Contains no grain fillers like corn, barley, wheat, or rice. It's pricey, but you're getting a far superior product. The major carbohydrate source is potatoes, which are also a good source of B vitamins and other minerals. There is a good range of fruits/vegetables in the food, whole eggs and a good range of probiotics. The product does not contain animal fat, but instead sunflower and herring oils which are excellent sources of Omega 3/6 EFAs.This food is outstanding in that it contains no grains whatsoever. Grains are not a natural part of a canine diet and it is pleasing to see dog foods on the market that exclude grains completely from the diet. This is a far more natural food concept and combined with a complete lack of any low quality or controversial ingredients is the reason this food is placed in a class above the more conventional form dry dog foods.

This is truly the best dog food for your pet if they have allergies.  This is the only product I have been able to give my rescue that hasn't cause ear problems or constant itching.  I highly recommend it.  It is pricy but saves on vet visits.

I am on Amazon to buy more of this brand after we bought a small package locally (about $35) to try it out before ordering online.  It is a fabulous dog food that will not only keep your dog's digestive system in great shape (and all you dog owners know what I mean -- less poop, with a solid consistency), but also will cost virtually the same as a cheaper brand, because your dog will need to eat so much less of this good lean protein.  We have a 70-lb. lab and I am estimating he will go through one of the $35 bags of small bites per month.  Not to mention the cost savings and peace of mind in having a healthier dog with fewer vet visits.  If you haven't already done so, read all the analyses and reviews on [...] plus their Info and FAQs sections to educate yourself about dog food.  You will never again buy dog food from the grocery store (pure junk!!)or from most vets (used to be good but formulas have been cheapened and changed and they are now mostly junk too!) For now, Innova Evo is one of several outstanding brands but you must constantly read labels because even good foods change.

column9: Expensive but not as expensive as you think.
column10: The price per bag is more expensive but you feed your dog much less because there is no grain in the food. Therefore, the price per day is much less than common middle of the road dog foods like science diet. Here is how I figured it out:My dog:40 lb. Border collie, 4 years old, energetic and healthy, been fed Evo his entire lifeFood serving size per day based on manufacturers recommendations:According to Science Diet - 3 cups or 295 grams per day.Evo - 1 7/8 cups or 226 grams per day.Cost:Science Diet Adult Fitness: $44.39 / 35 lb. bag or 15,875.73 grams.Evo Red Meat Small Bites: $ 61.99 / 28.6 lb. bag or 12,972.74 grams.At the recommended serving size each bag of dog food will last for:(Grams per bag / daily serving size)Science Diet - 53.8 days.Evo - 57.4 days.Cost per day to feed dog.(Bag of food cost / total number of days a bag of food will last)Evo Daily Cost - $0.93 per day.Science Diet - $1.21 per day.Evo representatives have recommended switching between the salmon, chicken. My dog likes all of them it just makes sense because humans are not supposed to eat the exact same thing every day either.Pros:My dog is healthyHas no allergies to any ingredients (has allergies to other things like pollen)He like the taste of all three types of Evo food. (salmon, chicken, red meat)Not overweightCons:Can't think of any other than his poop smells awful... I assume from the protein.

column9: GREAT FOR ALLERGIES & NOT AS EXPENSIVE AS YOU THINK!
column10: I have a Jack Russell Terrier that is SUPER ALLERGIC to grains.  I've had her on EVO EVO Red Meat Small Bite Dry Dog Food & the Evo Herring and Salmon Dry Dog Food 6.6lb For well over a year now.  I used to have to give her steroids every spring & fall. (Which I HATED to do!)  Her itching was so bad, that it kept ME awake at night!  I researched all kinds of dog food & dog food information I could get my hands on.  (I'm a Certified Dog Trainer & used to work as a Vet Tech, so I have a pretty good knowledge dog food knowledge base).  I found this book; Unlocking the Canine Ancestral Diet: Healthier Dog Food the ABC Way, which is an EXCELLENT BOOK!  After reading it, I thought about making my own dog food, but decided it was not reasonable for me to do that, time wise.  The book has a list of recommend dog foods & I decided on EVO.  I'm SO GLAD I DID!!  SO IS MY DOG!!  It is now July 2012.  They've (I have 2 Jack Russell 'Terrorists', but only one with allergies) been on the EVO dry dog food diet for almost 2 years & I have NEVER had any issues with loose stools, the dogs not wanting to eat the food, etc.  In fact, the dog I have with the allergies is a 'picky' eater, but she LOVES EVO!  Especially the Herring & Salmon flavor.  Since I've been feeding this food, I've noticed that my other JRT has developed an ABSOLUTELY BEAUTIFUL coat!  (I have one roughy & one smooth coat)  The smooth coat with the amazingly beautiful coat is due to the EVO.  It's even helped with the amount of shedding!  (Nothing can totally eliminate shedding, but this has cut down on the amount of shedding enough that I have noticed a difference!  I'm thinking that Josh Crick, got a bad bag OR, what I think is more likely, is was past the expiration date.  Also, (as you will find out if you read the book I recommended, which is just a thin little paperback, packed with info!)  You should NEVER take your dry dog food out of the original bag & store it in one of those bins.  Anything that can't be used up in 2 weeks time, I keep in the freezer.  This keeps the DHA in the food from breaking down & keeps dust mites & other little critters (that we can't even see) out of the food.  I CAN'T STRESS HIGHLY ENOUGH, that the expiration date, proper storage & just plain taking good care of the dogs food & plain old common sense, IS SO VERY IMPORTANT!  PLEASE read that book!  It's AWESOME & even has recipes in there so you can make your own dog food.  Also, reviewer Josh Crick stated that 1/4 of the bag he bought was powder, raises a HUGE red flag for me.  There has to be something either in that bag or something else wrong!!About the price, everyone considers this dog food expensive, but with no fillers in it & depending on your dog's activity level, it takes a LOT LESS for the dog to get the nutrients he/she needs.  So you may pay more upfront when you first buy this, but if you store it properly, it will last much longer, because you feed so much less.  My smallest JRT is 15 lbs.  She is pretty active.  Living in Michigan's Upper Peninsula & only a mile from the northern part of Lake Michigan, I take the dogs to the beach to swim & they get to run loose in the woods, chasing all kinds of small mamamals, (yes, including skunks!), she only requires about 1/3 of a cup of food each day.  In fact, I have to watch her, because she tends to get a little 'chunky' now & then.  Personally, I think that this food is actually cheaper when all is said & done.I hope this review helps!  I'll be monitoring this, so please feel free to ask any questions!!

I use canned tomatoes in, well, nearly most things I cook.  I tend to stock up on the 32oz cans of whole plum tomatoes but sometimes you just need a little less, and the fire-roasted flavor can be a nice touch. They also aren't ideal for making tomato sauces but I use them for lots of other things: adding some tomato to bean chilis, throwing together a quick salsa, making spanish rice, adding to soups or stews, and (this is seriously delicious) stirring into a prepared batch of Annie's mac and cheese, along with a can of chickpeas. column9: absolutely the best canned tomatoes AND organic
column10: This is a ditto of my other Muir Glen tomato reviews, but I feel the same way about all of them, so here goes...I've generally avoided red sauces and anything with canned tomatoes, but Cook's Illustrated's recipe for almost-fresh pasta sauce made with these (or any Muir Glen tomatoes) has changed me for life. I'm also buying organic whenever I can, so now I've started experimenting with other tomato recipes using these and am loving them. My friends and family laugh at me when I do "subscribe and save" and buy a case at a time, but it's a great bargain and there's always a can (or more) on the basement shelf.

Received a 12 can case of these tomatoes yesterday. Several cans were dented. One can, though sealed and undented, was unfilled. Amazon's packaging was intact; obviously, there had been problems at the canning facility. I have purchased these tomatoes many times before, from local markets as well as Amazon, and have never before encountered defects of this or any other kind. However, given recent well-publicized problems with food-borne illnesses arising from sloppy practices at other food packers and canners, I am leaning toward avoiding this brand in the future.

column9: Muir Glen Organic Fire Roasted Tomatos

column9: Good, if you can acquire the taste
column10: I've gone back and forth on this cereal, which I had not tried before ordering it through Amazon. On paper, it sounded great--walnuts, cinnamon, wheat-rice clusters. What's not to like?I had to get over the taste hurdle, and that took two boxes. This cereal does not taste like an oat-based granola. It has a strong wheat-y taste that can be a surprise initially. I found that I liked it after awhile, but it took some getting used to. This cereal occupies its own niche in the market and cannot be compared to things like Honey Bunches of Oats.A couple of other observations:1. A serving has 20 percent of the RDA for fiber. That's great. It has 10 percent of the RDA for fat. That's not so great.2. The cereal is a bit more crunchy than granolas like Honey Bunches. It is much less crunchy than the Kashi cereals I have tried. I found chewing it to be very pleasant and easy.3. The texture is nice--interesting. Some cereals are just bland in this respect.4. The cereal is appropriately sweetened for me. I like some taste of sweetness, but not a lot. This cereal was in no way cloying.It should be possible to serve this just as is (with milk), if you wish. Many other cereals really require the addition of blueberries, bananas and what-not to make them interesting.

Walnut spice is my daily cereal. I prefer it with vanilla soy milk rather than cow's milk as I find the taste a bit too strong otherwise. The texture is fantastic, being a bit crunchy but not too sugary. Another reviewer said it had too much sugar, and while it's true that it has 17g per bowl, it also has 5g of dietary fibre and 5g of protein, so that sugar isn't as bad as it sounds. Also, the suggested 2/3 cup serving size is huge. I find 1/2 cup or less is enough to fill me up for a couple of hours. With other cereals, I need 2/3 cup or more to feel full. I've been eating Walnut Spice every day for over a year and I'm amazed that I haven't gotten tired of it. I actually look forward to a bowl of cereal each morning. :) Having Amazon drop-ship it to my door is pretty nice too because the only store that carries it in my area is 20 miles away. I was worried that ordering it online might result in getting a box of crumbs, but the Amazon shipment is actually in better condition than what I get in the store (i.e. whole flakes, less crumbs).
The cereal was very tasty, but as is my usual complaint, it was somewhat over priced.  I did like the cereal though and so did others in my family.  Would order again.

I've been a vegan for six years, so I know a thing or two about rice and beans, and definitely have some strong preferences. I don't like Zatarain's rice and beans (red or black). There are a few different reasons for this, but the primary one is that on two separate occasions I've found "stuff" in the mix. Both times it was the same thing: a sort of fibrous, bone-like object, about the size of a marble. The first time it happened I was rather grossed out, but the second time I quit this stuff for good. I've found that both Wegmanns and Giant offer store brands of rice that taste better and are often more cost efficient, and I have not eaten Zatarain's since that.

Here are some tips:Do not be alarmed when you see red beans in the packet and wonder if you bought a complimentary additive to a separate purchase rice. I can assure you: there is rice below.Wait until rice cools down before overeating in haste and wondering why there isn't a hologramic warning label.

The fact that this cereal is low-fat makes a good product even better if you are trying to lose some weight or wanting to keep in shape.Sometimes your diet will require you eat frequently and consciously, and in those cases you need to have a snack at hand when you get hungry, in order to keep your metabolism high all day long. In such cases finding a good and balance option could be hard. I love this 6-pack and I always have one at home an another pack at the office. I try to eat five or more times a day, so in my case having a healthy snack at hand wherever I am when I get hungry is a priority.Since you are checking this product I have to guess that you are probably a person that cares about what you eat, either because you are interested in losing weight, getting in better shape or just be healthier and keep in good shape, so I will share my own experience in the weight loss game and staying in shape gameMy own successful personal experience in weight loss is based on strategies to boost metabolism. Don't stress yourself, eat frequently, eat just what you need each time, and choose wisely what you are going to eat, supplement your diet. Yet simple and it works. I loss more than 200 lbs and shrink my waist (from 44 to 32), and I have been able to keep in good shape since then. Every single aspect of my life has improved since then.Keep in mind that a good diet is just part of the equation, you also need a plan that helps you keep on track and monitor your condition. Based on my own personal experience I can recommend some tools that you may want to consider, to establish your own strategies for boosting your metabolism, loosing weight, and even more important keeping that weight off. They are:- "Ultrametabolism: The Simple Plan for Automatic Weight Loss" by Mark Hyman. A practical an realistic plan for weigh loss.- "The ABS Diet", which is another very practical, readable, insightful, and inspirational book, that also includes an exercise plan.- A Body Fat Monitor or Scale. This will help you monitor your progress, to assure that the weight you are loosing is fat (fat lost = increased metabolism) and not muscle, water or bone mass (decreased metabolism).- A Heart Rate Monitor Wrist Watch. This is an excellent tool that will help you monitor and control your Heart Rate in order to keep yourself in a burning fat state (increased metabolism).- "Heart Monitor Training for the Complete Idiot", a primer on the use of Heart Rate Monitors for health improvement or weight control.If you want to star focusing only on your diet, the first two may be worth considering. If you exercise, or want to start doing it right, the last threee are for you. If you do both, all the recommended options can improve your results.I am 39 years old, With the help of the tools I just mentioned not only I went fro size 44 to size 32 pants, but also obtained substantial benefits that included weight control, cardiovascular improvements, lowered blood pressure, and improved muscular-skeletal strength and flexibility, but also the myriad of mental and psychological benefits derived from being in the best shape of my life.Get this 6-pack of Low-fat Muesli to help your 6-pack ABS.

column9: photo did not represent candy received
column10: I am very, very disappointed.  I bought myself the white chocolate almond bark as a present to myself for giving birth to my 42 year old son.  The advertising photo showed whole almonds.  The candy I received had not one, NOT ONE, whole almond.  There was just crushed nut slivers.  Absolutely not what I was expecting for the price I paid.  Chocolate was of good quality but don't expect it to look like the photo.

Stunning flavor! Accurate to the core on how almond tastes only in a sweeter version! Close to amaretto but there is a difference and I do love both! I am glad I got both as well because I contemplated if they would be too similar and not worth the cost of both however as much as I love both flavors, I had to do it and I have no regrets!This Almond matcha is sweet and nutty. The aroma is captivating!! My daughter was in the process of making macrons and decided she will add some almond matcha to them. Unfortunately we had to stop because we were out of parchment paper - can't use waxed .... so anyway off to the store we shall run and I am going to pick up more sparkling water because I want to make an Italian Creme Soda with this almond matcha which will be AMAZING! Frothed up lovely even in milk.I love that Red Leaf uses natural flavors!

The prepared matcha is probably one of the best-smelling prepared matchas I've come across. The almond-extract aroma is mitigated and it now smells actually nuttier, sweeter, more like marzipan or an almond paste cookie. First sip... wow, yum. This is so almondy and sweet on its own (I haven't added any sugar), it's like eating an almond cookie, or a big hunk of marzipan. You can still taste the matcha, though, and it's a flavor that goes well with the almond. I do think. Ok, I couldn't resist adding just a touch of sugar (half teaspoon), and holy crap, is this like almondy matcha candy. It makes me think that this would be a good addition to a sugar cookie as opposed to almond extract to make a matcha almond cookie. This has been my favorite matcha so far, and I will definitely be back for more when I run out.

Purchased when I heard about this cookie spread from Belgium. So searched cookie spread from Belgium on Amazon and found this fabulous treat. My husband scoffed at me when I told him I ordered a jar. But he loves to spread it between Biscoff cookies. When he went looking for the spread and discovered it was gone he told me to order more.  I jokingly told him about the 8 pack and he demanded I order that one!  Well we have 6 packages of Biscoff cookies to use.I love to eat by the spoonful or on my toast. Haven't tried much else. Can't wait to get my 8 jars!

column9: OMG... better than bacon... if you can believe that!
column10: Know those cookies that Delta serves when they want to be really nice? They make a spread! OMG this stuff is good, evil good. On toast with a little butter. Delicious :) Great price savings when bought in this 8 pack.

I was lucky enough to discover Biscoff Spread  (with smudged labels) at the 99 cents store and decided to give it a try since I am such a fan of the Biscoff brand of Belgian speculoos cookies that they have served for many years on Delta Air Lines.  It's an odd concept, a spread made of cookies, but I'm glad that I didn't let that stop me from trying it.The label says that this is a "European alternative to peanut butter."  I completely disagree as it it only has the look and texture of peanut butter.  It smells and tastes just like the Biscoff cookies, but sweeter, with a hint of caramelized sugar and cinnamon.  It is much more like dulce de leche than peanut butter.This spread is good with ice cream; on pancakes, scones, and apples; or just eaten from a spoon as a nice treat after a meal.  A thin layer even salvaged the plain graham crackers I bought by mistake instead of the cinnamon honey variety.  It would also be good on cupcakes, waffles, or popovers.  Eating it on toast doesn't appeal to me but maybe with raisin bread it would be good.  It really is tasty and hard to resist, especially with milk or coffee.The basic recipe for Biscoff spread is speculoos cookies, canola oil, and sugar so it's not particularly healthy.  Each tablespoon has 88 calories with 52 of them from fat.  On the bright side, a tablespoon only has 33 mg of sodium.Ingredients:  Biscoff 57% (wheat flour, sugar, vegetable oils [one or more of soy bean oil, sunflower oil, canola oil, palm oil], soy flour, brown sugar, sodium bicarbonate, salt, cinnamon), canola oil, sugar, soy lecithin, citric acid.
This spread is tasty.  It tasted just like the cookies.  You can have it on toast or put some in oatmeal.  Very Good!!
These are simply divine.  Rich, dark, delicious, pretty much all around perfect.  I wish they were less expensive, but hey.
Good dark chocolate but didn't live up to the hype of other reviewers.  I prefer the Lindt darks over this, especially the 90%.  Rest assured I didn't throw this out though.

The first time I used the Kinnikinnick Graham Style crumbs, I was very pleasantly surprised to find that they made an excellent pie crust that tasted just as good as regular graham cracker crumbs. I served the pie to members of my family and never told them that the crust was wheat-free. They loved it and couldn't tell the difference from a regular graham cracker crust. This is a great wheat and gluten-free alternative that I will use again and again.

column9: These Graham style crumbs have STYLE!
column10: So last night I made a key lime pie with a graham cracker crust.  I served it to my non-gf significant other, and guess what? He had no idea it was gluten free.  And guess what else?  He ate the ENTIRE PIE!!!  The crust was delicious - perfect taste, perfect texture, in a word: perfect.  It's hard to find these on the store shelves where I live, and they appear to be out of stock frequently on Amazon...frustrating for a constantly-cooking woman like me. I'm picky about gluten free foods, and honestly there are other Kinnikinnick gf products I truly despise.  These, however, will become a staple on my shelf - the Graham Style Crumbs with STYLE!

My best friend has Celiacs disease and when she heard I was making cupcakes she challenged me to make Gluten Free cupcakes. One of my most popular flavors is my S'mores. I am so impressed with this stuff! I tasted it before I used it in my cupcakes and couldn't taste any difference from regular graham cracker crumbs. I highly recommend these for any recipe that calls for it.
This is great for graham cracker crust.  I made a cheesecake, and my gluten eating husband raved about it!  Can't wait to make another pie with it.
Taste like the real thing! I made a Cheesecake for Thanksgiving and not one person knew the crust wasn't real Graham Cracker Crumbs. Thank you Kinnikinnick!!

We used these crumbs to make pie crusts for Thanksgiving.  The results were excellent!  Taste and texture were just like regular graham cracker crumbs.  We were able to make 2 no-bake crusts from one box, making them cost-effective as well.
I love these crumbs. I use them for crusts for cheesecakes and for desserts and everyone comments on how great it tastes. I have to eat gluten free and these are wonderful!

column9: Great Gluten Free alternative to Graham Cracker crumbles
column10: These are a tasty Gluten Free alternative to standard Graham Cracker crumbles. If you need a graham cracker crust - ideal!

Full disclosure - I never tried using other crumbs, so maybe it is not about these ones in particular... But I used the whole box trying to figure out how to make it work, and it did not turn out fine a single time. I tried the recipe on the box, googled other approaches, used liquid/soft butter, prebaking/no prebaking but still the pie crust came out rock solid and did not get out of the pan. So it seems like it's easier to make the pie crust from scratch.
Currently use this brand daily, but the price has nearly doubled in the past 2 months, so I will be looking for another brand.
It came right when it was supposed to. Well packaged. Nearly half the price I normally pay at retail stores.

The Maxwell House French Vanilla T-Discs are an excellent product providing a rich French Vanilla flavored cup of coffee. I highly recommend this product to anyone who enjoys a delicious cup of vanilla flavored coffee!

column9: Always good to the last drop!
column10: I've had my Tassimo coffeemaker for over 3 years and really enjoy the varieties of beverages it will make.  The only drawback, as far as I'm concerned, is the lack of flavored coffees to choose from.  Out of the 2 companies that make a vanilla flavor for the Tassimo, I prefer the Maxwell House because it has a richer vanilla flavor.

column9: Absolutely delicious... a great tea and a great buy
column10: I adore a robust tea and this is it!  I can brew three (3) strong 12 cup coffee press pots with a small portion of tea.  Not at all bitter even when I let it steep a bit long.  I will purchase again.
I love the honey dijon dressing.  It is fat free and sugar free.  In addition to using on salads, I use it instead of mayo on sandwiches.  It really has a good flavor and it not too sweet.

On a whim because I was out of salad dressing I decided to give this a try.  Being calorie free and sugar free I didn't hold much hope for this.  But I can say that it is incredible!!  I use it in tuna, on salads, salmon, and as a marinate with some balsamic vinegar. I love to really "dress" my salads, so now I can do it guilt free!

Walden Farms Honey Dijon Salad Dressing, wonderful taste, easy to carry with you for social events. I would buy again & again.  No refrigeration needed for this product.  I would buy again & again. Use for dips and for making low calorie, chicken or tuna salads.  Can use for vegetable dips as well.

column9: The worst dressing I have ever had
column10: This was literally the worst dressing I have ever had. I have been obsessed with low and no calorie foods for almost a decade, so I'm pretty good at dealing with the taste of these types of foods. I made a beautiful spinach salad with mushrooms, tomatoes, and beets. Then I put this dressing on, and COULD NOT EAT MORE THAN ONE BITE. Extremely upset with this waste of money.

I decided to look this up after trying it on what began as a wonderful salad. The taste OMG the taste is horrendous! I wasnt able to get any down and started dry heaving from it.  Luckily all I had in my stomach was water so what came up wasnt so bad.  I also purchased Bacon Ranch and Chipotle Ranch but I really don't know if I will ever try them.  I didnt think a salad dressing could be so bad.

Ok although this product doesn't leave me hunched over the toilet bowl vomitting, i still DO NOT like the taste of this dressing at all. Its not completely horrible,  but the taste is almost too sweet. Its hard to place where this concoction went wrong, but i like Walden Farm's Raspberry dressing soooo much better!

I despise low-fat/non-fat dressings and would prefer to eat a salad plain rather than use them.  But these Walden Farms Dressings taste great and make a diet less monotonous.  My husband likes them too, and he always prefers the high calorie version of anything.
the smell alone is enough to make u gag. I would rather practice portion control and have a better quality of life than struggle through a bottle of this stuff
Tired of not getting the dressing you want? I am!!  this works perfect, keep in wallet or office, car, etc.

The Keen-Wah Decadence bar is CRAZY GOOD.  The first thought I had when biting into it was Rocky Road ice cream!--SUPER rich & chocolately, and you get this explosion of textures in your mouth of chunks of almond, and the crunchiness of chia seeds. The chocolate is just right, not too sweet, but sweeter than dark chocolate.  The best part is, THE INGREDIENTS ARE ALL ORGANIC, Gluten-Free, VEGAN, and Non-GMO.  I've been searching for some great vegan bars this past year, and would definitely say that this one, along with Vega's newest line of protein bars Vega Sport Protein Bar Single - Chocolate Coconut (which I also reviewed) are the BEST tasting, and contain quality ingredients.
