column9: Like marriage, it's great if you have realistic expectations
column10: Looking at the reviews of this an other Vacuvin products, you see reports that are deeply contradictory. It's interesting that there is such a divergence of experience with such a simple product. The ideas behind Vacuvin are pretty simple.First, air is the enemy of an open bottle of wine. Bacteria in the air want to turn alcohol into vinegar. The air itself oxidizes and dulls the taste of all but the most robust wines.Second, you can remove some of the air with a simple pump and thereby slow down the rate at which wine deteriorates.Why then, do we have both no-star and five-star reactions to this product?Maybe the biggest source of disagreement is expectations. Vacuvin slows the deterioration of wine in the bottle, but it doesn't stop it.Another possible reason for all the disagreement might be a question of temperature. The biochemical reactions that kill your wine are temperature sensitive. They proceed faster when the wine is warm and slow down when it's cool. Putting a pumped-out bottle in the refrigerator or wine cooler will slow down the spoilage processes and make Vacuvin more effective.A third issue is the way the wine is handled before the Vacuvin plug goes in. If wine has a lot of air dissolved in it by being poured from decanter to bottle, there's no system that will keep it fresh.For more info on wine storage, check out my book, New Short Course in Wine,The--Lynn Hoffman, author of New Short Course in Wine,The and bang BANG: A Novel from Kunati Books.

Until recently, Johnnie Walker Double Black was only available in duty free airport stores. About a year ago I purchased my first bottle in duty free. Johnnie Walker has now released this to select liquor stores.This is very similar to Black Label, but with an added punch of more smoke and stronger more pronounced flavors. It has a much sharper edge than Black Label. This stands up to ice rather well.Because it was so rare, Double Black developed a mystique. This is a good blended Scotch, but it isn't worth trekking all over to find. If your local liquor store carries it, it is well worth a try.I happen to like Double Black a bit better than straight Black Label. I'm a big fan of the smokier Scotches, Lagavulin, Scapa, Laphroaig, and others from Islay. I like Green Label a lot more than either Black Label. Of all the Johnnie Walkers, I dislike Gold Label, and, of course, Blue Label is my favorite. One of the primary single malts used in Johnnie Walker blends is Cardhu.If you can find it, this is a lovely Scotch.

Johnnie Walker Black Label is a good solid Scotch for drinking all by itself.This blended Scotch with all Scotches over twelve years old, is an interesting character. All alone in a nice glass, the first flavor is a lot of smoke. After a little time in my mouth other flavors develop, pepper, vanilla, and a little bit of honey. Add a little bit of water to the Scotch and most of the smoky flavor goes away, and that aftertaste comes out - the vanilla, pepper, honey flavors. But then add an ice cube to just the Scotch and things change up over time. At first the smoke flavor is around. As the ice melts and water gets in the Scotch, the smoke goes away and the other flavors are left. Once the ice gets the Scotch cold, all that smoke comes back. It's fun to play the disappearing smoke game. I'm not sure I'd mix this Scotch - it takes plenty good enough on its own.I'm a big fan of the smokier Scotches, Lagavulin, Scapa, Laphroaig, and others from Islay. I like Green Label a lot more than Black Label. Of all the Johnnie Walkers, I dislike Gold Label, and, of course, Blue Label is my favorite. One of the primary single malts used in Johnnie Walker blends is Cardhu.The Double Black is worth a try. Everything is just amped up a couple of levels.There is a strange Johnnie Walker Scotch that is worth trying - Swing. It's not in the smoky zone, but it is one very nice Scotch.Johnnie Walker Double Black Scotch Whisky 750 mlJohnnie Walker Scotch Swing 750ML

I have been using this product mostly in bread and pancakes for a while and it works well. I like that the shelf life is much longer than what is stated on the package. Also, it is convenient to add the powder to the flour and then I add more or less water to the batter depending on desired thickness. Another nice thing about using buttermilk in pancakes, rather than milk, is that I can then use just baking soda rather than baking powder (due to the acidity in the buttermilk). Oh, and my shipment was delivered without incident.

column9: Great product that gives a richness to baked goods and...
column10: I make a fabulous sourdough buttermilk waffles that can not be made without Saco buttermilk powder. I've used Saco Cultured Buttermilk Blend for several years. It gives a nice, extra richness when added to baked goods. I usually add the dry powder with the flour and add water as  the wet ingredient measurement as called for in the recipe. If you don't use buttermilk often, Saco's buttermilk powder is great to have around for the times the baking mood hits. It really makes sourdough bread special too. Try adding 3 to 4 tablespoons as part of the flour measurement in making bread or rolls - whether they are plain, sweet or savory. Really delicious!

I love keeping this on hand at all times because I never seem to get through a half gallon of buttermilk before it goes bad, but I like to have it for use in biscuits, breads, and to brine chicken before frying. This stuff is very economical and super convenient. It does require refrigeration once opened, but that's no big deal to me. I mix up batches of biscuit mix and pancake mix in advance, then just add the liquid ingredients when I need it. I can store large quantities in the freezer and whip up buttermilk pancakes for breakfast in a flash. Love it. This is a pantry staple for me.

I have used this product for a long time.  Really handy for baking that uses buttermilk.  The local grocery wasn't getting the ROI from the shelf space required for marketing this product and discontinued carrying it.  This is my first purchase of this product from Amazon. The shipping was prompt, but did arrive with dents in two of the cartons.  Not damaging to the enclosed product. It comes as a three pack product.  I will have to 1) make more biscuits, 2) give some away, 3) try is as 'drinking' buttermilk.  The use by date is 05/19/2015.If you do a lot of baking, I believe you will enjoy and appreciate the convenience of this product.

column9: Great for Recipes calling for Dried Milk!
column10: Arrived with one canister broken open.  Salvaged the order.  Thoughtless packing  and a flimsy canister makes breakage during shipping a common occurrence with this particular product.I'm using this to make bread, pancakes, and the like and have been pleased with the product.  Would have been thrilled but for the broken canister.I called amazon customer service and they offered me two options:  1.  Receive another shipment at no cost or  2.  A refund.Since I need the buttermilk powder I had them ship me a new order.  Though another canister was broken open, I did get two that were good.  The expiration date is good until 2015!  Suspect I can store it in the freezer until I use it.Customer service was incredibly good and they gave 1 day shipping on the replacement order.I would make sure that this is ordered separately from anything else you might need on amazon so it doesn't make a mess on anything but itself!Thanks amazon for the awesome customer service!

column9: Never have to run out to the store just to get buttermilk again!
column10: After having to modify yet another recipe because I didn't have buttermilk on hand I decided to give this a try.  Since that time I have ordered it several times from Amazon who consistently has it for the best price.  I mix the powder with my dry ingredients and then combine it with the wet for less lumps. I love this product and use it weekly in my waffle recipe. It does have a good taste. My last order arrived with no issues or defects in packaging.

I received the Saco buttermilk quickly and in good shape. The buttermilk powder is great for baking. It adds much better flavor and texture than liquid buttermilk. It also lasts for a very long time with refrigeration.

column9: A Must-Have for a Stocked Pantry!
column10: This buttermilk is tasty and easy to use! It's great to have items like this in your pantry so that when you find an awesome recipe on pinterest you can make it up asap instead of running out to the store first! Be sure to read the package because you need to refrigerate after opening, which surprised me.

If you use buttermilk in your cooking and baking, buy yourself some of Saco's powdered buttermilk. I love the convenience of knowing I've always got it in the refrigerator for a recipe that calls for buttermilk

other brands I have bought, are very expensive and they sit and form hard lumps. This is very good for baking, improves texture of my bran muffins, and stays soft and easy to measure. I've had it open for a couple of months, only use a few tablespoons at a time...

I love to bake. Breads, biscuits, cakes, etc. I keep this on hand because it's convenient. I don't have to buy buttermilk specifically for something, I know I have it on hand for spur of the moment baking.This works great in quick breads, cakes and yeast breads. It adds a nice flavor to yeast breads, and it's acidic enough that in cakes and quick breads you get a lot of lift using it with baking powder or baking soda. It also works very well in pancakes.I haven't yet tried it to culture cream to make creme fraiche with.

column9: This is indispensable when making bread
column10: This is one of my favorite products out there, I can get the richness of buttermilk in my baked goods but I don't have to always keep the liquid stuff that spoils on hand.  This stuff has a long shelf life, perfect for those of us who sometimes like to bake on a whim.... like I am right now, I am making some honey wheat bread.I found no problems with the packaging.  It I guess could be sturdier, but as I said I have not ever had any problems.  I like the resealable plastic lid especially well too.

column9: One of my must-have pantry items!
column10: I love buttermilk and use it in all sorts of things - oven-fried chicken, biscuits, pancakes, cake, you name it - if the recipe calls for milk you can bet I've tried substituting buttermilk on a whim.  Thing is the local stuff around here, while excellent, is pricey and I always forget about the half a bottle left over in the back of my fridge until after it's gone bad.I got a canister of this buttermilk powder as backup for when I don't have fresh and I really like it.  It adds a lovely flavor and is so convenient!  I don't use water, however, I use milk to give the recipe a little more substance.  I make sure to always have some on-hand in my pantry and recommend it to others.

This buttermilk powder is wonderful.  No need to ever have buttermilk spoil in the fridge again!  I use it in recipes that even call for just regular milk and add the powder to the dry ingredients...IE: waffles!

I am a diabetic and eat a low carb diet to control my blood sugar, so I have no idea how it is in bread but I bet it's terrific.I use it to make homemade buttermilk ranch dressing and/or dip and it gives it a better flavor than anything from a store.I am so glad I found this on amazon, where we live it was impossible to find locally, but now there are a few sources like smart and final that carry it.My packages arrived in perfect condition and on time, no complaints at all.

I've loved using this buttermilk product for years, so I was really happy to see it in one pound bulk packaging. If you love buttermilk flavor in foods, get this & always have it handy - you won't be disappointed.

Although I have not tried baking with this product yet, I have gone through 2 replacement orders and found the canisters leaking both times.  I think the manufacturer has a bad packaging design for this product that is definitely not mail-friendly.  It is a shame that I cannot find this product in my local grocery store.  But I believe Saco can do something to make the canisters more durable - plastic construction instead of flimsy cardboard and a tighter seal (maybe metal) instead of paper.

column4: J. L. Hodges "Since I gave up hope, I feel a ...
column9: Great tool for the home cook
column10: Repeatedly, I buy buttermilk for a recipe only to throw it out after having used it just once. I saw the powdered buttermilk used on "America's Test Kitchen" during the preparation of pancake batter. Since one of my favorite recipes for dumplings calls for buttermilk, I thought the powdered would be a good substitute. When it arrived, I feared I would never be able to use all three containers before I or they expired. However, the dumplings proved so superior that I have used the powdered buttermilk in many other preparations. The biscuit recipe on the container is superb. They expand so beautifully and are so delicious as to promote bitter fighting over who gets how many.My pancakes are just as tasty as the biscuits. I now think I will have to order more of Saco powdered buttermilk rather than waste any at all.You will not be disappointed.

Use buttermilk powder in baking to replace liquid buttermilk - make sure to add the powder with the dry ingredients, then water where the liquid buttermilk would normally go. Much easier to store in the fridge than quarts of buttermilk, never run out with extra in the pantry. Great in bread machine recipes.

I have used this substitute before we live out of the country and I stock up when we go home for the summer.  It's great in pancakes and muffins and I know I can substitute milk with lemon juice but I find the product produced with this far superior.

I really like this product.  I use it in breads and to cook with. It does run on the rather pricey side, but buttermilk is expensive too.  I keep this in the fridge once I open it.  You don't have to, but it keeps it from clumping up.

column9: Can Flow through  your kitchen often if you learn to use it correctly.
column10: It has been a while, but I bought this product in the high-end grocery store in my local area-that being publix.  I like drinkiing buttermilk, and hoped it could be a replacement for always having to buy fresh. Well, it didn't meet that expectation. On the canister, I believe, it tells you what it's purpose is, and that is to add to baked goods in place  of having to buy fresh each time to cook with.There was a recipe on the back of the canister, for buttermilk biscuits. I made them several times. They were great!  I would not go back to using fresh buttermilk, if I could find this product regularly. Unfortunately-at least in my close local area in tampa bay Fla, I don't see that publix is carryng the product widely, if at all, anymore.  Great product. I'm still looking to find a way to use it to make a substitute for fresh buttermilk to drink. But if not, then I will use it in biscuits, and see whatever else it does well. Guess pancakes should be next since I love buttermilk pancakes. Whoo hoo!!

I've used this product intermittently over the past decade at least.  I don't bake much but when I do need it, it has worked perfectly every time.  I made cornbread with it last night and I had to use a container that was pretty outdated...it was mostly dried out and hard lumps.  I figured I had nothing to lose so tried it and it worked great!  I think I have gotten mine at the grocery store each time before and have had no problem.  I am going to place an order online now.I hope this product stays around and that the company doesn't change the formula (by "improving" it in the wrong direction!).

The 1st shipment we received was packaged well, but when I opened the box I noticed at least one of the canisters had been busted open. They had dents in the canisters like it had been dropped. I contacted Amazon & received a new box the next day. Amazon's customer service is awesome! My boyfriend loves using this powdered buttermilk to make bread.

column9: Outstanding product - as good as fresh buttermilk and much more convenient
column10: I have baked with Sacco buttermilk powder for years with complete satisfaction. In any recipe that calls for buttermilk, just measure the powder into the dry ingredients, and add water to the liquid ones. Buttermilk adds tang and tenderness to waffles, muffins, quick breads and cakes. Sacco's website offers dozens of recipes, many of them prize winners at state and county fairs. For those of us who bake with buttermilk, but don't drink it, powdered buttermilk is the perfect product: unopened cans have an indefinite shelf life, and opened cans stay fresh in the refrigerator for months. Amazon's three-pack is good value - about 5¢/oz below my local supermarket price.

column9: Dehydrated tangy buttermilk good for cooking, baking. Natural but convenient.
column10: Unlike many convenience foods, this does not have un-natural ingredients; the listed ingredients are all real food.  Merely dehydrated.After opening, it must be stored in the refrigerator; but it keeps for months in the fridge, if kept dry.The container is paperboard or thin cardboard and seems recyclable, or biodegradable (except for the plastic lid).  I imagine that water could eventually soak through the bottom, if this container were left sitting in a puddle, which seems an unlikely scenario, unless your family is like mine -- frequent spills and inadequate cleanup.  When storing in the fridge, we nest this buttermilk "canister" inside a plastic container (e.g. Tupperware or Rubbermaid); just in case someone spills anything liquid or messy inside the fridge.Has worked well for baking recipes that calls for buttermilk, for example cornbread.  We have begun experimenting by substituting in other mixes and recipes, in place of plain milk.  The buttermilk adds a tangy taste,  not really sour.  I even like it in mac and cheese (stovetop method).I have never attempted to make a beverage with this.  As a beverage, buttermilk has never appealed to me.  I'm guessing it might be OK, in small amounts, added to a smoothie in the blender.We got this at a local chain grocery store; thus I am unable to provide comment on the seller(s) here.By the way, on that same aisle, I learned of some other dehydrated items for the pantry:  powdered eggs Deb-El Powdered Whole Eggs, 8-Ounce Containers (Pack of 6); and powdered egg whites (without the yokes) Deb El Just Whites Dried Egg Whites - 1 Canister (3 oz ea),  and Deb-El Just Whites, 3-Ounce Containers (Pack of 6).At first, I thought we would use this powdered buttermilk only in a pinch, like when snowed in.  However, we now prefer it.More convenient than the alternative:  If we were to buy a carton of regular, fresh, liquid buttermilk, for a recipe, most of it would spoil before we got around to using it all.Also see other package sizes, some of which are Prime eligible now:  Saco Powdered Buttermilk, 12-Ounce Cans (Pack of 6),  and  Saco Powdered Buttermilk, 12-ounce Can.
I love the convience of this buttermilk powder. I use it in all my baking and with wonderful results!  Much more economical than real buttermilk and stores a whole lot longer.

The product works & tastes just fine, but the packaging was terrible.  Two out of the three containers was broken open during xhipping.  The containers should have been packed more securely so they couldn't move or get crushed.

I have ordered the Saco Cultured Buttermilk Blend, 16-Ounce Canister (Pack of 3) before and the items arrived intact and were good to use.  This second shipment arrived completely crushed. The buttermilk powder was all over the inside of the box and the other items I had ordered.  All of the containers and their lids were smashed and torn and could not be used. It is too bad that there was not any protective packaging material between the cardboard buttermilk containers and other heavier metal canned items inside the larger box.

Ordered twice and the packaging is so bad that the canister cans made of paper do not last in shipping.  the box it was shipped in had no dents and the inside packaging was good.  the seals on the cans are not well made

The package was not secured properly.  1 of the 3 containers leaked and was messy.  Other than that the package arrived on time.

Buttermilk is essential to many recipes.  But, keeping a supply handy in the refrigerator invariably leads to throwing the majority of it away due to spoilage.  I had high hopes for this Saco Cultured Buttermilk Blend as a means of avoiding that problem.  Unfortunately, I have to say that the product doesn't meet my expectations.  I agree that it adds a certain flavor and a bit of loft to a recipe.  But, I don't think it's quite the same flavor or loft I get from real buttermilk (or what passes for real buttermilk, these days).  The flavor is OK:  it's just different.  Also, I think the loft is more from the fact that the batters it produces are runnier (or maybe looser) than I get from buttermilk.  That's probably because today's buttermilk has some form of gum added which thicken things up.  Since the end result of recipes made with this differ from that of using buttermilk, it's probably just as good to use the old standby of adding a tablespoon of white vinegar to a cup of milk.  The result will be different from real buttermilk, but just as equivalent as using this powdered buttermilk.I'd definitely recommend trying this product for yourself to see if it meets your needs.  It's certainly not bad, and could be just fine for you.  But, in my case, I guess I'll just have to accept the spoilage of buttermilk in the refrigerator.  I rate this at an OK 3 stars out of 5.

column9: Better (and WAY cheaper) than Starbucks Frappuccino.
column10: I've been buying these for some time now from another distributor, so I'm THRILLED to find them available now on Amazon with Subscribe-n-Save.This is a very versatile frappe blend. column10: The Best Raisin Bran used to be Crispy Wheats 'n' Raisins (which then became Crispy "Wheaties" 'n' Raisins.) *****Numi Tea's Golden Chai Spiced Assam Black Tea is a premium Numi tea, both certified organic and kosher. The ingredients are fair trade certified organic Assam black tea, organic cinnamon, organic Chinese ginger, organic green cardamom, and organic Turkish anise. There is nothing artificial in this or in any Numi tea.On the box, the manufacturer writes: "Throughout India, chai stalls are a meeting place for provocative tea and conversation. From its homeland in China, chai has journeyed as chai, thé, and tea, recreating itself in every land. Numi's golden brewed, organic Chai fuses rich cultures in a complex and hearty Assam black tea. Indian cinnamon and mild green cardamom evoke a warm balance with the vitality of Chinese ginger. The peaked, sweet aroma of Turkish anise exhilarates memories. Reminisce in aged tradition with an inspiring cup of Golden Chai."Although this is a "chai", note that it contains no sweeteners...I prefer this, and the anise gives a certain type of mild sweetness, but commercial chais often have sugar added, so be prepared for a wonderful no-calorie indulgence that is beautifully flavored but not "sweet" in the same way that sugar is. If you are new to Numi but love chai, this will probably be the best you've ever had.*****

I love this product! I have been gluten free for one year now, and these breadcrumbs have saved many of my recipes. I love to cook, and have had to convert so many of my favorite recipes, like sesame chicken, and orange chicken - where you coat the chicken and fry up for a crispy coating.. column9: A little hard for my taste, but the orange flavor was great
column10: I used these for the candy buffet I had at my wedding and I must say these were literally bursting with orange flavor. I usually find gum balls to be pretty bland no matter the flavor. column4: Lonnie E. Holder "The Review's the Thing"
column10: The cookie industry has learned a new trick.  Set up a package of cookies that have 100 calories and people will buy them.  In fact, they are.  Health conscious Americans are gobbling these cookies down enthusiastically.  Unfortunately, these cookies remain cookies, though if you can limit yourself to one pack, you could be doing yourself, and your diet, a favor.These cookies taste reasonably good.  They have a satisfying crunch and a mild flavor.  Perhaps the only problem with them is that it is easy to be tempted into a second package; and then a third.  Stop at one package and at least your calorie intake will be reasonable for a snack.If you must have a cookie and you can limit yourself to a single package, by which I do not mean the entire box, then these cookies are a good choice.  Fruits and vegetables remain even better choices, but sometimes you just hear sugar calling your name.Enjoy!

*****White Rose Velvet Garden White Tea is an exciting and unusual premium Numi tea. It is a white tea, more rare than other types of teas and less processed as well, having been only plucked and dried (not oxidized). Some people find white tea a subtler and more enjoyable type of tea experience (I know I do). White Rose Velvet Garden White Tea is certified organic, and is both fair trade and kosher.It is made from hand-wrapped white tea leaves and rosebuds! Rosebuds---can you imagine?!?! Those are the only two ingredients, and they are delicate and delicious, different from anything else I've ever tried.This tea, like all Numi teas, is packaged with 100% post-consumer waste, and the tea bags are made from biodegradable filter paper. Numi does not believe in the practice of adding oils or flavorings to bolster flavors, and I love this and can tell the difference; for this and many other reasons, Numi is one of my favorite tea manufacturers.On the box, Numi writes: "Roses have been a symbol of love and beauty since the dawn of romance. Numi's enchanting Velvet Garden(tm) releases a provocative sweet rosy taste as it blushes a soft pink. With every sip this liaison of organic rose petals and delicate Spring White tea imparts a silken smoothness. White Tea is the tender bud of the tea plant making it exquisitely subtle and supremely healthy. High in antioxidants and vitamin C, this uplifting Fair Trade Certified white tea blend will be the beginning of a long lasting love affair." I have to agree. This is truly an amazing tea.If you like Numi teas, get it---you won't be sorry. If you are new to Numi but love white tea, or are curious to try it from the description, I do not think you could find a better source than Numi. If you are looking for a romantic tea, White Rose Velvet Garden White Tea fits the bill perfectly.Highly recommended.*****

When diagnosed with Celiac Disease I really missed eating good tasting cereals. column9: How to identify the expiration date
column10: When I received my box of Kraft fat free mayonnaise packets I immediately checked the individual packets for an expiration date and there was none. I then looked on the box and found a UPC code and another code with 7 alpha-numeric characters (ex: 08M07C0). I called Kraft Foods and was told the code next to the UPC code was the expiration date. Using the code on my box as an example (08M07C0), the code reads as MM(letter)DD(letter)Y. This translates to August 7, 2010. I asked about the letters in the code and was told they have nothing to do with the manufacturing date.  Kraft Foods also said these packets have a Shelf Life of 5 months only. So my box was manufactured on 08/07/10 and expires on 01/07/11. Kraft Foods did not recommend using the packets after the expiration date. I would like to see Amazon list the expiration date of their stock so you know how much useful life is left to a grocery item. Maybe they could create a link on the page that you could click on and have the expiration date displayed.

Hill's Science Diet Puppy Small & Toy Breed dog food provides precisely balanced nutrition to meet your small breed dog's special needs.It is the only brand with an exclusive blend of clinically proven antioxidants.This formula is specially designed to boost immune defenses and support the long life expectancy of small and toy breed dogs.There a myths that allergies are caused by ingredients such as corn but that is not the case. To say that something is a filler would imply it has no nutritional value; when in fact corn is a superb source of nutrients. There is a misconception that whole corn is used - in fact the corn is baked and is much like ground corn you buy. When cooked it is highly digestible.We hear many concerns about by-products in pet food. We need to understand how they are defined and what they really are and what is their nutrient value.By-products is really a play on words. Virtually all ingredients in pet foods are by-products. No one for example uses real chicken breasts as we know it.It's neck and backs of a chicken.Another common myth is that meat should always be the first ingredient, inferring that if that was the case, there would be more meat than anything else in the food. Often the carbohydrates levels are higher than the meats because of the way they are listed in the ingredient panel.Meat first is often the first ingredient only to please the consumer look st the ash levels and mositure levels, and ingreident spliting.I have fed Science Diet to my two dogs and I am very happy with the results. They love the food, it seems to have a good nutrient profile, my dogs have not had any gas or loose stool, in fact the clean up has been minimal so far, poop is much smaller and less of it that ever! I keep searching the yard with the scooper several times a day and there just isn't much to clean up! I can honestly say that they are going HALF as much as they were before! This is definately chihuahua puppy approved. I like the fact that there is a puppy food for smaller breeds. These are real small bites. My puppy was 2.16 lbs at 7 weeks and tiny, so having something that is small enough for him to chew. At 5.5 months old, he still enjoys it.
Decent price - dog eats this food like she's never eaten before in her life.  It can be hard to find this type in stores.

I received my first bag via a coupon from BzzAgent, for free... since price was not a factor I was more than open to seeing positive changes. I really wanted to give this a high rating because our little mutt really seemed to like eating it and it is the perfect size but I did not notice any positive changes in her. By the same token, I did not notice any major negative changes either. However, the first few days she had diarrhea and after that it went back to almost normal consistency but she was pooping about twice as often. She was also thirsty all the time while eating this.I would say this food is average in quality, the pooch liked the taste but did not experience any of the claimed improvements so I do not think the price is justified. Others may have better luck with it but it just did not work better than our old food.

I received a free sample of Science Diet for our Papillon as  part of a Bzz Agent.  I was a little hesitant to try it because I had heard some stories from others who used it and were too happy. We tried it out and our dog is very happy. With her old dog food we would feed her in the morning and she wouldn't never want to eat until later in the day. Now since we have  switched she is real excited when we are getting the food out, she eats it right away.
I bought this for my Pembroke Welsh Corgi and she just loves it. The bits are small and very easy for her to chew.

My dog is sick and on prednisone.  The vet recommended this food because of weight gain from the prednisone.  My Yorkie Loved it! I was really surprised.  He eats every bite.  It's really tiny pieces so its easy for a tiny dog to eat.  I mixed a bit of his old food with it at first and gradually lower the amount of his older food.  Now he is just eating this food. That way there's no stomach upset from drastically changing his diet. I would definitely recommend this food for weight loss and it was neurology vet approved.

I love coconut oil for it's high heat tolerance and for putting a great color on veggies but I don't always want the hefty coconut flavor. This is the perfect solution. Great product I'll be buying again for sure.

I have worked at Starbucks for 8 years.  In November, I left my job to have a baby and my husband and I didn't get coffee beans for free anymore (Starbucks gives you a pound a week).  We tried various brands in the store and didn't like it.  We were looking for something economical and realized that some of the 5 pound bags are actually less per pound than Eight O'Clock Bean.  We used Coffee Bean Direct twice and really liked it.  This time, we ordered this from Copper Moon. It is so stale.. no shine to the beans and it tastes like Maxwell House.  When I started at Starbucks we tried Maxwell House canned coffee and compared it to Starbucks coffee that had been opened and ground for a few weeks and they tasted the same. Fresh coffee gives off gases and cannot be canned until it is stale and that is why most packaging has one-way valves.  I will go back to Coffee Bean Direct.. it wasn't worth saving 3 dollars.
